deps.label: thm:nrn_negative_anchor

blocks.tex:
\href{../figures/tabachnikov-construct-N.svg}{Illustration: tabachnikov-construct-N}

Construction (N) for
$\mu=(1,\allowbreak\,0.96,\allowbreak\,0.81,\allowbreak\,0.67,\allowbreak\,1.04,\allowbreak\,0.75,\allowbreak\,0.83,\allowbreak\,0.92)$: the secondary
peak is $0$ and the maximum is $H=4$, and both flags are negative. The frame
is $(0,H-1,H,n-1)$ and the anchor is an orthogonal quadrilateral (dashed
diagonals; \ref{lem:core}). Bottom row: the anchor, the polygon after
opening the dormant edges, and a zoom on the block $\{1,2,3\}$, which is a
single point in the anchor and now has short dormant edges (orange).

By \ref{lem:peak}, $2\le H\le n-2$ and $\mu_{H\pm1}<\mu_H$. The frame
(\ref{fig:N}) has readings~\eqref{eq:readings} with $i=H$:
$p=\mu_1$, $t=\mu_{H-1}$, $q=\mu_H$, $h=\mu_{H+1}$, $l=\mu_{-1}$, where
$0<p,l<1<q$ and $t,h<q$; moreover $\varphi^+=\varphi(p,t,q,l)$ and
$\varphi^-=\varphi(l,h,q,p)$. Apply \ref{lem:crossed} to $F=\rho_1$,
$G=\rho_3$ on $[0,1]^2$; they are continuous there, because all arguments of
$\arcsin$ lie in $[0,1]$ by \ref{lem:core}(i). By
\ref{lem:core}(v): $\rho_1(0,v)>0$ and $\rho_3(u,0)>0$;
$\rho_3(1,v)=0$ forces $v=l$, where $\rho_1(1,l)=\varphi^+<0$;
$\rho_1(u,1)=0$ forces $u=p$, where $\rho_3(p,1)=\varphi^-<0$; and
$\rho_3(1,1)<0$. So there is a common zero $(u,v)\in(0,1)^2$. By
\ref{lem:core}(i), $\hat L_0,\hat L_3,q\hat L_1,q\hat L_2<1$, and with
$p,l<1$ and $t,h<q$ all eight walls hold, so $\hat L\in\Omega$ and
$\Ctrl(\hat L)=0$ by \ref{lem:core}(iii). If $T\ge\pi/2$,
\ref{cor:rank}(b) gives the rank, and otherwise
\ref{prop:acute}.

We identify a curvature profile with a vector $\kappa\in\R^n$ and a labelled
polygon with a vector $(P_i)_{i\in\Zn}\in\C^n$, with the product topologies.

blocks.label: thm:local
blocks.title: Local C1 choice of realizing polygons
blocks.body:
Let $n\ge4$ and let $\kappa^0\in\R^n$ be positive with a strict four-vertex
window~\eqref{eq:dfv}. There are an open neighbourhood $V$ of $\kappa^0$ and
$C^1$ maps $h\colon V\to\R^n$ and $P\colon V\to\C^n$ such that for every
$\kappa\in V$ the half-lengths $h(\kappa)$ realize $\kappa$ and $P(\kappa)$ is
the polygon developed from them by~\eqref{eq:vertices}, normalized by
$P_0=0$. In particular $P(\kappa)$ is simple, strictly convex and coherent,
with curvature $\kappa_i$ at every vertex.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.localContinuousRealization_of_dfv
lean.code:
theorem localContinuousRealization_of_dfv
    {κ₀ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ} (hκ₀ : ∀ i, 0 < κ₀ i) (hdfv : DFV κ₀ c) :
    Nonempty (LocalDiscreteRealizationFamily κ₀) := by
  obtain ⟨A⟩ := nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_dfv hκ₀ hdfv
  exact A.nonempty_localDiscreteRealizationFamily hκ₀

deps.title: Local coherent choice at every nonconstant admissible profile
deps.label: thm:tabachnikov_local_continuity

deps.title: Local choice from a strict four-vertex window
deps.label: presentation:local

blocks.tex:
By \ref{prop:reduction} and~\ref{prop:split} and
\ref{sec:constructions}, $\kappa^0$ has a regular anchor, and
\ref{thm:anchor-realizes} gives $V$ and $h$. The vertices
\eqref{eq:vertices} are real-analytic in $(\kappa,h)$, so $P$ is $C^1$. The
remaining properties are \ref{sec:setup}.

For $0\le s\le1$ consider the hexagon profile
\begin{equation}\label{eq:band}
  \kappa^{s} = (14,\ 11,\ 10+3s,\ 5,\ 7-3s,\ 3).\tag{7.1}\end{equation}
Every $\kappa^s$ is positive and nonconstant. A direct check of all
quadruples of indices shows that the levels $c$ of strict four-vertex windows
of $\kappa^s$ form the set
\[
  (5,\,7-3s)\ \cup\ (11,\,10+3s),
\]
with an empty interval when the endpoints are reversed. The lower band is
nonempty for $s<2/3$ (window indices $0,3,4,5$), the upper band for $s>1/3$
(indices $0,1,2,5$). Hence every $\kappa^s$ is admissible and, by
\ref{thm:main}, realized by a coherent convex hexagon.

\href{../figures/tabachnikov-hexagon.svg}{Illustration: tabachnikov-hexagon}

Left: the levels of strict four-vertex windows of $\kappa^s$. Right:
realizing hexagons at $s=0$ and $s=1$ with their smallest enclosing circles.
The reciprocal enclosing radius is at most $7$ at $s=0$, at least $11$ at
$s=1$, and never $9$, so it cannot vary continuously.


A polygon $(P_i)_{i\in\Zn}$, not necessarily developed, \emph{realizes}
$\kappa$ if for every $i$ the circle through $P_{i-1},P_i,P_{i+1}$ has radius
$1/\kappa_i$.

blocks.label: thm:hexagon
blocks.title: No global continuous choice
blocks.body:
There is no continuous map $s\mapsto P^s\in\C^6$, $s\in[0,1]$, such that each
$P^s$ is a coherent convex hexagon realizing $\kappa^s$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.GlobalContinuity.no_continuous_regular_hexagon_path
lean.code:
theorem no_continuous_regular_hexagon_path :
    ¬ ∃ p : ℝ → (ZMod 6 → ℂ), ContinuousOn p (Set.Icc 0 1) ∧
      ∀ s ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
        IsSimplePolygon (p s) ∧ DahlbergRegular (p s) ∧
        SignedMengerProfile (p s) = bandProfile s :=
  fun ⟨p, hp, h⟩ ↦ no_continuous_coherent_hexagon_path
    ⟨p, hp, fun s hs ↦ ⟨(h s hs).1, (h s hs).2.1,

deps.title: The hexagon obstruction without an orientation premise
deps.label: presentation:hexagon

blocks.tex:
The invariant is the smallest enclosing circle. For a finite set $X$ of
points let $D(X)$ be its smallest enclosing closed disk and $R(X)$ its
radius; $D(X)$ exists and is unique, and $R$ is $1$-Lipschitz for the maximum
distance between labelled tuples, since enlarging a disk enclosing one tuple
by that distance encloses the other. The \emph{contacts} are the points of $X$
on $\partial D(X)$.

blocks.label: lem:contacts-determine
blocks.title: lem:contacts-determine
blocks.body: $D(X)$ is also the smallest enclosing disk of its set of contacts.

blocks.tex:
Let $D(X)$ have center $O$ and radius $R$, and suppose a disk with center $O'$
and radius $R'<R$ contains every contact. For $O_t=(1-t)O+tO'$ and every
contact $x$,
\[
  |O_t-x|^2=(1-t)|O-x|^2+t|O'-x|^2-t(1-t)|O-O'|^2\le(1-t)R^2+tR'^2<R^2 ,
\]
and non-contacts satisfy $|O-x|<R$, hence $|O_t-x|<R$ for small $t>0$. Then a
disk of radius smaller than $R$ encloses $X$, a contradiction.

In the next two lemmas $P$ is a coherent convex polygon with curvatures
$\kappa_i$, $D=D(P)$ has radius $R$, and $\omega_i$ is the circle through
$P_{i-1},P_i,P_{i+1}$, of radius $1/\kappa_i$.

blocks.label: lem:contact-comparison
blocks.title: lem:contact-comparison
blocks.body:
If $P_i$ is a contact, then $\kappa_i\ge1/R$. If all contacts lie in
$\{P_{i-1},P_i,P_{i+1}\}$, then $\kappa_i\le1/R$.

blocks.tex:
Place $P_i$ at the origin with $D=\{z: |z|^2\le 2\langle O,z\rangle\}$,
$|O|=R$. The circle $\omega_i$ is $\{|z|^2=2\langle C,z\rangle\}$ with $|C|=1/\kappa_i$.
By coherence $C=aQ_-+bQ_+$ with $a,b\ge0$, where $Q_\pm=P_{i\pm1}$. Since
$Q_\pm\in\omega_i\cap D$,
\[
  |C|^2=a\langle C,Q_-\rangle+b\langle C,Q_+\rangle
  =\tfrac12\bigl(a|Q_-|^2+b|Q_+|^2\bigr)
  \le a\langle O,Q_-\rangle+b\langle O,Q_+\rangle=\langle O,C\rangle\le R\,|C| ,
\]
so $1/\kappa_i=|C|\le R$. For the second claim, the closed disk bounded by
$\omega_i$ contains all contacts, so its radius is at least $R$ by
\ref{lem:contacts-determine}.

blocks.label: lem:containing
blocks.title: lem:containing
blocks.body:
If the disk bounded by $\omega_j$ contains every vertex, then
$\kappa_j\le\kappa_{j-1}$ and $\kappa_j\le\kappa_{j+1}$. If $P$ is not
inscribed in a circle, there are two vertices $j\ne j'$ with
$\omega_j\ne\omega_{j'}$ whose disks contain every vertex.

blocks.tex:
The circles $\omega_j$ and $\omega_{j+1}$ both pass through $A=P_j$ and
$B=P_{j+1}$, and by coherence both centers lie in the open half-plane $H$
bounded by the line $AB$ that contains the polygon. For circles through $A$
and $B$ with centers in $H$, the parts of their disks in $H$ increase strictly
with the radius. The vertex $P_{j+2}$ lies in $H$, on $\omega_{j+1}$ and in the
disk of $\omega_j$; if $\omega_{j+1}$ had the larger radius, $P_{j+2}$ would lie in
the open disk of $\omega_{j+1}$. Hence $1/\kappa_{j+1}\le1/\kappa_j$, and
symmetrically for $j-1$. The second statement is
\cite[Lemma~5]{Dahlberg2008}, which applies to strictly convex polygons not
inscribed in a circle.

\textbf{Proof of \ref{thm:hexagon}.} 
Suppose $P^s$ is such a family and put $c(s)=1/R(P^s)$, a continuous function.
Index the vertices $0,\dots,5$ as in~\eqref{eq:band}.

\emph{$c(s)\ne9$.} If $c(s)=9$, the contacts have $\kappa_i\ge9$ by
\ref{lem:contact-comparison}, so they lie in $\{0,1,2\}$. The same
lemma at vertex $1$ gives $11=\kappa_1\le9$, which is absurd.

\emph{$c(0)\le7$.} If $c(0)>7$, the contacts lie in $\{0,1,2\}$, so
$c(0)\ge\kappa_1=11$. Then vertex $2$, with $\kappa_2=10$, is not a contact,
the contacts lie in $\{0,1\}\subset\{5,0,1\}$, and $c(0)\ge\kappa_0=14$. Now
the only possible contact is vertex $0$, and by
\ref{lem:contacts-determine} the enclosing radius would be $0$.

\emph{$c(1)\ge11$.} Here $\kappa^1=(14,11,13,5,4,3)$. The hexagon is not
inscribed in a circle, since its profile is not constant. By
\ref{lem:containing} there are two distinct vertices whose curvature
disks contain the polygon, and each is a weak local minimum of $\kappa^1$.
The only weak local minima are vertices $1$ and $5$, so vertex $1$ qualifies,
and $R\le1/\kappa_1=1/11$.

By the intermediate value theorem $c(s)=9$ for some $s$, a contradiction.

The argument uses only continuity of the labelled vertices. Whether a global
continuous choice exists for $n=4$ or $n=5$ is left open.

There is a second discrete curvature attached to a convex polygon: the
reciprocal radius of the inward circle tangent to three consecutive
supporting lines. Wegner's four-edge theorem concerns these radii
\cite{Wegner1994,Pak2010}. We give a converse as a companion to
\ref{thm:main}. The construction below uses a tangential polygon and
positive edge scaling; it is independent of the four-length system used for
the main theorem.

blocks.label: def:side-tangent-circle
blocks.title: def:side-tangent-circle
blocks.body:
Let $P_i$ be the vertices of a counterclockwise strictly convex polygon,
with outward unit normal $N_i$ on edge $[P_i,P_{i+1}]$.
The \emph{inward three-line circle at edge $i$} has center $C_i$ and radius
$r_i>0$ satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{eq:side-tangent-distances}
 \langle N_{i-1},P_i-C_i\rangle
 =\langle N_i,P_i-C_i\rangle
 =\langle N_{i+1},P_{i+1}-C_i\rangle=r_i.\tag{8.1}\end{equation}
Its central contact is required to lie in the open edge $(P_i,P_{i+1})$.
The contacts on the two neighbouring supporting lines may lie on their
extensions. The circle need not be contained in the entire polygon.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.ThreeLineCircle
Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.IsSideTangentRealization
lean.code:
structure IsSideTangentRealization [NeZero n] (ρ : ZMod n → ℝ)
    (P N C : ZMod n → ℂ) : Prop where
  radius_pos : ∀ i, 0 < ρ i
  simple : IsSimplePolygon P
  strict_convex : StrictConvexEdgeSupport P
  unit_normal : ∀ i, ‖N i‖ = 1
  oriented_edge : ∀ i, ∃ ℓ : ℝ, 0 < ℓ ∧ P (i + 1) - P i = ℓ • (Complex.I * N i)
  supporting : ∀ i j, ⟪N i, P j - P i⟫_ℝ ≤ 0
  circles : ∀ i, ThreeLineCircle P N i (C i) (ρ i)
  unique_circle : ∀ i D r, ThreeLineCircle P N i D r → D = C i ∧ r = ρ i
  central_contact : ∀ i, C i + ρ i • N i ∈ openSegment ℝ (P i) (P (i + 1))

blocks.tex:
\href{../figures/tabachnikov-side-tangent-circle.svg}{Illustration: tabachnikov-side-tangent-circle}

The selected circle is tangent to three supporting lines, with
its central contact in the open edge. Here one neighbouring contact lies
beyond its edge. All coordinates, circle equations and contact parameters
in this example are checked with exact rational arithmetic.


Put $c_i=r_{i-1}-r_i$. By four cyclic sign changes we mean that there are
$i_1<i_2<i_3<i_4<i_1+n$ with
$c_{i_1}>0$, $c_{i_2}<0$, $c_{i_3}>0$ and $c_{i_4}<0$; zero differences are
retained but do not count as a sign. This formulation includes repeated
radii without a genericity assumption.

blocks.label: thm:side-tangent-converse
blocks.title: thm:side-tangent-converse
blocks.body:
Let $n\ge4$ and let $r_i>0$ be a cyclic sequence. Suppose that $r$ is
constant or that $c_i=r_{i-1}-r_i$ has four cyclic sign changes. Then a
simple strictly convex polygon realizes $r_i$ as the radii of its inward
three-line circles. Each center and radius are uniquely determined by the
three equations~\eqref{eq:side-tangent-distances}, and every central contact
lies in its open edge.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.IsSideTangentRealization.tangent_sphere

theorem IsSideTangentRealization.tangent_sphere [NeZero n]
    {ρ : ZMod n → ℝ} {P N C : ZMod n → ℂ} (h : IsSideTangentRealization ρ P N C)
    (i k : ZMod n) (hk : k = i - 1 ∨ k = i ∨ k = i + 1) :
    Metric.sphere (C i) (ρ i) ∩ supportingLine P N k = {C i + ρ i • N k} :=
  sphere_inter_normalLine (h.unit_normal k) (h.radius_pos i).le (h.circle_line_distance i k hk)

theorem sideTangentConverse [NeZero n] (hn : 4 ≤ n) (ρ : ZMod n → ℝ)
    (h : SideTangentAdmissible ρ) : RealizesSideTangent ρ := by
  obtain ⟨hρ, hconst | hdfv⟩ := h
  · obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := hconst
    exact sideTangentConverse_of_const hn ρ hρ hr
  · exact sideTangentConverse_of_dfv ρ hρ hdfv

deps.title: Signed-distance equations imply unique metric tangency
deps.label: st:metric-tangency

blocks.tex:
The main ingredient is a balanced polygon circumscribed about the unit
circle. Its vertices, rather than the contact points, carry the coefficients.

blocks.label: lem:side-tangent-balance
blocks.title: lem:side-tangent-balance
blocks.body:
Suppose $\sum_i c_i=0$ and $c$ has four cyclic sign changes. There is a
strictly convex polygon $Y_i$, circumscribed about the unit circle with each
contact in its open edge, such that $\sum_i c_iY_i=0$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.isCyclicStrictTangentialFan_of_finite
lean.code:
theorem isCyclicStrictTangentialFan_of_finite [NeZero n] (s : ZMod n)
    {U Y : Fin n → ℂ} (h : IsStrictTangentialFan U Y) :
    IsCyclicStrictTangentialFan (fun i ↦ U ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm i))
      (fun i ↦ Y ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm i)) := by
  refine ⟨fun i ↦ h.unit_normal _, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro i
    simpa only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ] using h.normal_cross_pos ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm i)
  · intro i
    simpa only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ] using h.vertex_eq ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm i)
  · intro i j hji hjs
    apply h.strict_support
    · exact fun he ↦ hji ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm.injective he)
    · intro he
      apply hjs
      apply (cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm.injective
      simpa only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ] using he
  · intro i
    simpa only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ] using h.contact_interior ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm i)
  · intro i
    simpa only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ] using h.edge_pos ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm i)
  · intro i
    simpa only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ] using h.edge_ne ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm i)
  · intro i j hji hjs
    simp only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ]
    apply h.cross_support
    · exact fun he ↦ hji ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm.injective he)
    · intro he
      apply hjs
      apply (cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm.injective
      simpa only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ] using he

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.exists_balanced_strictTangentialFan
lean.code:
theorem exists_balanced_strictTangentialFan {n p q r : ℕ} [NeZero n]
    (hn : 4 ≤ n) (hp : 0 < p) (hpq : p < q) (hqr : q < r) (hr : r < n)
    (c : Fin n → ℝ) (hsum : ∑ i, c i = 0)
    (h₀ : 0 < c ⟨0, by omega⟩) (h₁ : c ⟨p, by omega⟩ < 0)
    (h₂ : 0 < c ⟨q, by omega⟩) (h₃ : c ⟨r, hr⟩ < 0) :
    ∃ U Y : Fin n → ℂ, IsStrictTangentialFan U Y ∧ ∑ i, c i • Y i = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨η, hη, hη₁, a, σ, ha, hσ, hsq, hd, hb⟩ :=
    exists_balanced_squareFan hn hp hpq hqr hr c hsum h₀ h₁ h₂ h₃
  exact ⟨fun i ↦ ProjectiveBall.transform a σ (normal (fanAngle n p q r η i)),
    fun i ↦ ProjectiveBall.transform a σ (fanVertex n p q r η i),
    projective_squareFan_isStrictTangentialFan hn hp hpq hqr hr hη hη₁.le ha hσ hsq hd, hb⟩

deps.title: Returning the balanced geometry to its original labels
deps.label: st:cyclic-fan

blocks.tex:
Choose four alternating nonzero coefficients, and place their labels at
$(1,1),(-1,1),(-1,-1),(1,-1)$ in that order. Collapse all intervening labels
to the corresponding side contact of the square. All labels and their
coefficients remain present. Denote this limiting configuration by $X_i$,
and consider the finite rational field
\[
 G(a)=\sum_i\frac{c_i X_i}{1-\langle a,X_i\rangle}.
\]
For sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, all denominators are positive on
$D_\varepsilon=\{(x,y):|x|+|y|\le1-\varepsilon\}$. On its upper boundary arc
$y\ge |x|$, one of the two upper corner denominators equals $\varepsilon$.
If the alternating corner coefficients are $\alpha,-\beta,\gamma,-\delta$
with $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta>0$, and the left and right contact
coefficients are $u,v$, then
\[
 \mathop{\rm Re}G(x,y)\ge
 \frac{\min(\alpha,\beta)}{\varepsilon}
       -\gamma-\delta-2|u|-2|v|>0.
\]
The upper and lower contact labels have zero horizontal contribution,
including near their poles. The corresponding bounds on the other three
arcs give, successively, $\mathop{\rm Im}G<0$ on the left,
$\mathop{\rm Re}G<0$ on the bottom and $\mathop{\rm Im}G>0$ on the right.
Thus the boundary field has winding number $-1$.

Now separate the repeated normals into small, strictly ordered clusters.
This produces a genuine tangential polygon $X_i^{\eta}$, with every edge
positive and every contact interior, converging to the labelled square as
$\eta\downarrow0$. Positivity of all denominators and the strict boundary
margins persist uniformly on the compact diamond. The perturbed field has
the same nonzero winding number and hence a zero $a$ in $D_\varepsilon$.
In particular $|a|<1$.

Set $\sigma=\sqrt{1-|a|^2}$ and
\[
 A=\sigma I+\frac{aa^{\mathsf T}}{1+\sigma},\qquad
 B_a(x)=\frac{Ax-a}{1-\langle a,x\rangle}.
\]
This projective transformation preserves the unit disk, its tangent lines,
and the cyclic order and open contacts of our polygon. All relevant
denominators are positive. Since $\sum_i c_i=0$,
\[
 \sum_i\frac{c_i}{1-\langle a,X_i^{\eta}\rangle}
 =\langle a,G(a)\rangle=0,
 \qquad
 \sum_i c_i B_a(X_i^{\eta})=A G(a)-a\langle a,G(a)\rangle=0.
\]
The vertices $Y_i=B_a(X_i^{\eta})$ have the required properties.

blocks.label: lem:side-tangent-scaling
blocks.title: lem:side-tangent-scaling
blocks.body:
Let $Y_i$ be a counterclockwise strictly convex polygon circumscribed about the unit circle,
with its contacts in its open edges. If $r_i>0$ and
$\sum_i(r_{i-1}-r_i)Y_i=0$, the cyclic edge equations
\begin{equation}\label{eq:side-tangent-scaling}
 P_{i+1}-P_i=r_i(Y_{i+1}-Y_i)\tag{8.2}\end{equation}
define a closed simple strictly convex polygon. Its inward three-line
circle at edge $i$ has center $C_i=P_i-r_iY_i$ and radius $r_i$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.sum_scaled_edges
lean.code:
lemma sum_scaled_edges [NeZero n] (ρ : ZMod n → ℝ) (Y : ZMod n → ℂ) :
    ∑ i, ρ i • (Y (i + 1) - Y i) = ∑ i, (ρ (i - 1) - ρ i) • Y i := by
  have he := Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.addRight (1 : ZMod n))
    (fun i ↦ ρ i • Y (i + 1)) (fun j ↦ ρ (j - 1) • Y j) (fun i ↦ by simp)
  simpa only [smul_sub, sub_smul, Finset.sum_sub_distrib] using
    congrArg (fun z : ℂ ↦ z - ∑ i, ρ i • Y i) he

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.strictSupport_of_positive_edge_scaling
lean.code:
theorem strictSupport_of_positive_edge_scaling [NeZero n] (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    {P Y : ZMod n → ℂ} (hY : StrictConvexEdgeSupport Y) (ρ : ZMod n → ℝ)
    (hρ : ∀ i, 0 < ρ i) (hedge : ∀ i, P (i + 1) - P i = ρ i • (Y (i + 1) - Y i)) :
    StrictConvexEdgeSupport P := by
  have hs := isSimplePolygon_of_strictConvexEdgeSupport hn hY
  have ho := positiveOrientation_of_strictSupport hn hY
  have ht := hasPositiveTurningNumberOne_of_simple_positiveOrientation hs ho
  refine strictSupport_of_polar P (cyclicEdgeHeading Y)
    (fun k ↦ ρ (k : ZMod n) * cyclicEdgeLength Y k)
    (fun k ↦ mul_pos (hρ _) (cyclicEdgeLength_pos hs k))
    (cyclicEdgeHeading_strictMono hs ho) (cyclicEdgeHeading_succ_lt_add_pi hs ho)
    (cyclicEdgeHeading_add_n ht) ?_
  intro k
  have he : cyclicEdge P k = ρ (k : ZMod n) • cyclicEdge Y k := by
    simpa [cyclicEdge, cyclicVertex, Nat.cast_add] using hedge (k : ZMod n)
  rw [he, ← cyclicEdge_length_mul_exp_heading hs k]
  simp only [Complex.ofReal_mul, Complex.real_smul, mul_assoc]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.realizesSideTangent_of_scaledFan
lean.code:
theorem realizesSideTangent_of_scaledFan [NeZero n] (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    (ρ : ZMod n → ℝ) (hρ : ∀ i, 0 < ρ i) {U Y P : ZMod n → ℂ}
    (hf : IsCyclicStrictTangentialFan U Y)
    (hedge : ∀ i, P (i + 1) - P i = ρ i • (Y (i + 1) - Y i))
    (hs : StrictConvexEdgeSupport P) (hp : IsSimplePolygon P) : RealizesSideTangent ρ := by
  let N : ZMod n → ℂ := fun i ↦ U (i + 1)
  let C : ZMod n → ℂ := fun i ↦ P i - ρ i • Y i
  have he : ∀ i, ∃ ℓ : ℝ, 0 < ℓ ∧ P (i + 1) - P i = ℓ • (Complex.I * N i) := by
    intro i
    obtain ⟨ℓ, hℓ, heq⟩ := hf.edge_pos i
    exact ⟨ρ i * ℓ, mul_pos (hρ i) hℓ, by rw [hedge i, heq, smul_smul]⟩
  refine ⟨P, N, C, hρ, hp, hs, fun i ↦ hf.unit_normal (i + 1), he,
    normal_support_of_strictSupport hs he, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro i
    simpa only [ThreeLineCircle, N, C, sub_add_cancel] using
      threeLineCircle_equations (hf.inner_left i) (hf.inner_right i) (hf.inner_right (i + 1))
        (hedge i)
  · intro i D r hD
    have heq : ⟪U i, P i - D⟫_ℝ = r ∧ ⟪U (i + 1), P i - D⟫_ℝ = r ∧
        ⟪U (i + 1 + 1), P (i + 1) - D⟫_ℝ = r := by
      simpa only [ThreeLineCircle, N, sub_add_cancel] using hD
    exact threeLineCircle_unique (hf.normal_cross_pos i).ne'
      (hf.inner_left i) (hf.inner_right i) (hf.inner_right (i + 1)) (hf.next_strict hn i)
      (hedge i) heq.1 heq.2.1 heq.2.2
  · intro i
    have hc := prescribedContact_mem_openSegment (ρ i) (hedge i) (hf.contact_interior i)
    simpa only [C, N, smul_sub, sub_add_eq_add_sub, add_sub_assoc] using hc

deps.title: Positive closed edge scaling retains strict support
deps.label: st:scaled-support

deps.title: Balance is exactly the edge-closure equation
deps.label: st:scaled-closure

deps.title: Scaled tangential geometry realizes the radii
deps.label: st:scaled-realization

blocks.tex:
Cyclic summation by parts gives
$\sum_i r_i(Y_{i+1}-Y_i)=\sum_i(r_{i-1}-r_i)Y_i=0$, so the edges close.
Positive scaling preserves their ordered directions and their total turn
of $2\pi$. For any fixed edge, the projections of the subsequent edges on
its left normal are first positive and then negative. Every intermediate
partial sum is positive, using closure for the second part. Hence every
nonincident vertex is strictly to its left. This gives strict support and
simplicity.

The outward normals satisfy
$\langle N_{i-1},Y_i\rangle=\langle N_i,Y_i\rangle=1$ and
$\langle N_{i+1},Y_{i+1}\rangle=1$. Substituting
$C_i=P_i-r_iY_i=P_{i+1}-r_iY_{i+1}$ gives all three
signed-distance equations. The central contact is the image of $N_i$ under
the positive homothety $x\mapsto C_i+r_ix$, and therefore lies in its open
edge. Adjacent normals are linearly independent. The first two equations
force any other center with radius $s$ to equal $P_i-sY_i$; the third then
gives $s=r_i$, since $\langle N_{i+1},Y_i\rangle<1$. Finally, unit normals
turn the signed-distance equations into actual circle tangency.

\href{../figures/tabachnikov-side-tangent-construction.svg}{Illustration: tabachnikov-side-tangent-construction}

A balanced polygon circumscribed about the unit circle (left) and
its positive edge scaling (right). The prescribed cyclic radii are
$(1,2,1,3/2,1,2,1,3/2)$. Closure, strict support and all eight circles are
verified exactly. The highlighted upper edge is the central edge of the
circle in \ref{fig:side-tangent-circle}.

\textbf{Proof of \ref{thm:side-tangent-converse}.} 
For nonconstant data, apply \ref{lem:side-tangent-balance} to
$c_i=r_{i-1}-r_i$, whose sum is zero, and then
\ref{lem:side-tangent-scaling}. For constant $r_i=r$, take a regular
polygon circumscribed about the unit circle and scale its edges by $r$.

The forward implication uses the signed affine-balance argument of
\cite[Section~21.6]{Pak2010}, with zero coefficients included. It is
Wegner's four-edge theorem, including zero differences, for the supporting-line
circles of \ref{def:side-tangent-circle}.

blocks.label: lem:side-tangent-signs
blocks.title: lem:side-tangent-signs
blocks.body:
Let $Y_i$ be the cyclic vertices of a counterclockwise strictly convex polygon. If
$\sum_i c_i=0$ and $\sum_i c_iY_i=0$, then either every $c_i=0$ or the cyclic
coefficient sequence has at least four sign changes.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.sideTangentForward
lean.code:
theorem sideTangentForward [NeZero n] (hn : 3 ≤ n) {ρ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {P N C : ZMod n → ℂ} (h : IsSideTangentRealization ρ P N C) :
    SideTangentAdmissible ρ := by
  obtain ⟨Y, hY, hb⟩ := exists_strict_balanced_polygon_of_realization hn h
  refine ⟨h.radius_pos, ?_⟩
  rcases zero_or_dfv_of_strict_affine_balance hn hY (sum_radiusDifference ρ) hb with hz | hd
  · exact Or.inl (constant_of_radiusDifference_eq_zero hz)
  · exact Or.inr hd

deps.title: Wegner's condition for the actual radii
deps.label: st:forward

blocks.tex:
A nonzero zero-sum sequence has both signs. If it has no four alternating
signs, it has one nonpositive block and one nonnegative block, with zeros
allowed in either. Choose a negative entry $c_a$ beginning the first block
and a positive entry $c_b$ beginning the second, using cyclic lifts
$a<b<a+n$. The chord $Y_aY_b$ has strictly negative signed area against
vertices in $(a,b)$ and strictly positive signed area against those in
$(b,a+n)$. Thus
\[
 c_i[Y_a,Y_b,Y_i]\ge0\quad\hbox{for every }i,
 \qquad \sum_i c_i[Y_a,Y_b,Y_i]=0,
\]
where $[A,B,C]$ is the signed determinant. The equality follows from the
zero mass and zero vector sum, since the determinant is affine in its third
argument. Every summand vanishes. Strict chord separation forces all
coefficients except $c_a,c_b$ to vanish. The two balance equations then give
$c_a(Y_a-Y_b)=0$, contradicting $c_a<0$ and distinctness of the vertices.

blocks.label: cor:side-tangent-iff
blocks.title: cor:side-tangent-iff
blocks.body:
Let $n\ge4$ and $r_i>0$. The sequence $r$ is realized by the inward
three-line circles of a simple strictly convex polygon, with their central
contacts in the open edges, if and only if $r$ is constant or its cyclic
differences $r_{i-1}-r_i$ have at least four sign changes.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.realizesSideTangent_iff_admissible
lean.code:
theorem realizesSideTangent_iff_admissible [NeZero n] (hn : 4 ≤ n) (ρ : ZMod n → ℝ) :
    RealizesSideTangent ρ ↔ SideTangentAdmissible ρ := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨P, N, C, h⟩
    exact sideTangentForward (by omega) h
  · exact sideTangentConverse hn ρ

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.realizesSideTangent_iff_dfv
lean.code:
theorem realizesSideTangent_iff_dfv [NeZero n] (hn : 4 ≤ n) {ρ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (hρ : ∀ i, 0 < ρ i) (hnc : ¬ ∃ r, ∀ i, ρ i = r) :
    RealizesSideTangent ρ ↔ DFV (radiusDifference ρ) 0 := by
  rw [realizesSideTangent_iff_admissible hn]
  exact ⟨fun h ↦ h.2.resolve_left hnc, fun h ↦ ⟨hρ, Or.inr h⟩⟩

deps.title: Exact characterization of side-tangent radius words
deps.label: st:iff

blocks.tex:
Sufficiency is \ref{thm:side-tangent-converse}. For necessity, start
from the actual polygon and its circles, and set
$Y_i=(P_i-C_i)/r_i$. The two incident normal equations give
$\langle N_{i-1},Y_i\rangle=\langle N_i,Y_i\rangle=1$.
These normals are linearly independent, because the polygon is strictly
convex. The circle at the preceding edge satisfies the same two normalized
equations at $P_i$, so it gives the same $Y_i$. Consequently
\[
 Y_{i+1}-Y_i=\frac{P_{i+1}-P_i}{r_i}.
\]
This is a closed positive edge scaling of the original polygon; the strict
support argument in \ref{lem:side-tangent-scaling} therefore applies to
$Y$. Summation by parts gives
$\sum_i(r_{i-1}-r_i)Y_i=0$, and the differences themselves sum to zero.
\ref{lem:side-tangent-signs} supplies four sign changes unless every
difference vanishes. In the latter case the cyclic radius sequence is constant.

chapters.title: Turning-angle curvature and the mixed-sign problem

blocks.tex:
The choice of discrete curvature matters. Two elementary examples explain
why the results above neither extend to turning angles without further
hypotheses nor give a converse for arbitrary signed Menger profiles.

blocks.title: Turning angles need not have four extrema

blocks.tex:
If curvature is defined simply as the exterior turning angle, a strictly
convex polygon can have only one local maximum and one local minimum.

blocks.label: ex:turning-angle
blocks.title: ex:turning-angle
blocks.body:
Take the quadrilateral with counterclockwise vertices
\[
 A=(0,0),\qquad B=(3,0),\qquad C=(4,1),\qquad D=(0,2).
\]
It is strictly convex. Its exterior turns, in the same order, are
\[
 \theta_A=\frac{\pi}{2},\qquad
 \theta_B=\frac{\pi}{4},\qquad
 \theta_C=\frac{\pi}{2}+\arctan\frac35,\qquad
 \theta_D=\frac{\pi}{2}+\arctan\frac14.
\]
Thus $\theta_B<\theta_A<\theta_D<\theta_C$. Around the cycle
$A,B,C,D$, only $B$ is a local minimum and only $C$ is a local maximum.
All four readings are distinct, so plateau conventions do not affect the
example.

blocks.tex:
The construction is just a quadrilateral with unequal side lengths; there
is no limiting or degenerate configuration. It disproves the unrestricted
turning-angle version of the forward theorem. Additional assumptions can
restore such a statement: generic equilateral convex polygons with at least
four vertices satisfy an angle version of the discrete four-vertex theorem
\cite[Corollary~21.6]{Pak2010}.

blocks.title: Four extrema do not suffice for mixed-sign Menger curvature

blocks.tex:
For signed Menger curvature, the analogous difficulty concerns the
\emph{converse}. The strict four-vertex window alone does not guarantee
realizability once negative values are allowed.

blocks.label: ex:mixed-sign
blocks.title: ex:mixed-sign
blocks.body:
For any $M,\varepsilon>0$, consider the cyclic profile
\begin{equation}\label{eq:mixed-counterexample}
 \kappa=(M,-\varepsilon,M,-\varepsilon).\tag{9.1}\end{equation}
It has two strict maxima and two strict minima, and satisfies
$\DFV(\kappa,0)$: the two negative readings lie below zero and the two
positive readings above it. Nevertheless, no oriented simple quadrilateral
has this signed Menger profile.

blocks.tex:
For any counterclockwise simple polygon, let $\theta_i\in(-\pi,\pi)$ be its
principal exterior turns. They sum to $2\pi$. By~\eqref{eq:menger},
\[
 \kappa_i=\frac{2\sin\theta_i}{|P_{i+1}-P_{i-1}|},
\]
so $\kappa_i$ and $\theta_i$ have the same sign. There must therefore be at
least three positive curvature readings: with at most two positive turns,
\[
 2\pi=\sum_i\theta_i
 \le \sum_{\theta_i>0}\theta_i<2\pi,
\]
a contradiction. For a clockwise simple polygon the same argument with
signs reversed requires at least three negative readings. The profile
in~\eqref{eq:mixed-counterexample} has only two of each sign, so neither
orientation is possible.

This obstruction is independent of coherence or local regularity. Making
$M$ arbitrarily large or $\varepsilon$ arbitrarily small does not remove it:
each individual positive turn is still less than $\pi$. Its moderate-arc
form is proved in \texttt{Gluck/Discrete/Budget.lean}, by
\texttt{three\_le\_card\_pos\_of\_realizes} and
\texttt{killerProfile\_not\_realizes}. These Lean statements concern the
\texttt{RealizesR2} development model; the general polygon argument above
and Example~\ref{ex:turning-angle} are elementary arguments supplied here,
not separately formalized.

What additional conditions on a mixed-sign cyclic profile, beyond a strict
four-vertex window, characterize its realization as the signed Menger
curvature of a counterclockwise simple, locally regular polygon in the
sense of Dahlberg~\cite{Dahlberg2008}? The positive-support condition just
proved is necessary, but we do not claim it is sufficient. Thus the direct
mixed-sign extension is false, while finding the right strengthened
converse remains an open problem left by this work. \ref{thm:main}
settles the positive case; a mixed-sign characterization would be a further
discrete counterpart of Dahlberg's smooth converse.

We prove \ref{prop:acute}. Let $L=\hat L(u,v)$ be as there and
suppose that $D\Ctrl(L)$ is not onto. All polynomial identities below were
verified by computer algebra and are checked in Lean.


\emph{Projective coordinates.} By \ref{lem:core}(i),
$\cos\alpha_0=v\hat L_2$, $\cos\alpha_3=u\hat L_1$, $\cos\gamma_1=v\hat L_3$ and
$\cos\gamma_2=u\hat L_0$, hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tan}
  \tan\alpha_0\tan\gamma_2=\tan\alpha_3\tan\gamma_1=\frac{q}{uv}>1 .\tag{10.1}\end{equation}



Put $x=\tan\alpha_0/\tan\gamma_1$, $y=1/(\tan\gamma_1\tan\gamma_2)$,
$w=1/\tan\gamma_2$ and $m=w^2$. By~\eqref{eq:tan}, $\tan\alpha_0=xw/y$,
$\tan\alpha_3=x/w$, $\tan\gamma_1=w/y$ and $\tan\gamma_2=1/w$. Since
$T<\pi/2$, $\tan\gamma_1\tan\gamma_2<1$, so $y>1$; and
$x/y=\tan\alpha_0\tan\gamma_2>1$, so $x>y>1$. With
$\lambda_*=\cos\alpha_0\cos\alpha_3/y>0$ one finds
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cos}
  \cos S=\lambda_*\,(y-x^2),\qquad \frac{\cos T}{q}=\lambda_*\,x\,(y-1);\tag{10.2}\end{equation}
the first is $\cos S=\cos\alpha_0\cos\alpha_3(1-\tan\alpha_0\tan\alpha_3)$, and
the second uses $q\sin\alpha_3\cos\alpha_0=\cos\gamma_1\sin\gamma_2$, which
follows from the cosine relations above.



\emph{The equations.} By \ref{lem:rank}, $AD=BC$. Put $a=A/2$, $b=C/2$
and $\tau=A/B$. Then $B=2a/\tau$ and $D=2b/\tau$, and since $0<p,l<1$ and
$t,h<q$, all of $A,B,C,D$ lie in $(0,1)$:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ranges}
  0<a<\tfrac12,\quad 0<b<\tfrac12,\quad 2a<\tau,\quad 2b<\tau .\tag{10.3}\end{equation}

Substituting~\eqref{eq:cos} into the second equation of~\eqref{eq:minors}
and dividing by $\lambda_*B$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:affine}
  \mathcal A:=-(x+1)(x-y)(1+\tau)+2(x^2-y)b-2x(y-1)a=0 .\tag{10.4}\end{equation}

Since $\tan\arcsin(c\sin z)=\varsigma_c(z)\tan z$, the four mixed arcsines
have tangents $(1-2a)\,xw/y$, $(1-2b)\,w/y$, $(1-2b/\tau)/w$ and
$(1-2a/\tau)\,x/w$. The equations $\varepsilon_1=0$ and $\varepsilon_3=0$ say
that four angles with nonzero cosines sum to $\pi$, and for such angles
$(\tan z_1\tan z_2-1)(\tan z_3+\tan z_4)=(\tan z_1+\tan z_2)(1-\tan z_3\tan z_4)$.
Clearing denominators gives
\begin{align}
  \mathcal E_1&:=y(x-m)\bigl(x(1-2a)+(1-2b)\bigr)
     -(x+1)\bigl(y^2-xm(1-2a)(1-2b)\bigr)=0,\label{eq:E1}\tag{10.5}\\
  \mathcal E_2&:=(xm-y^2)\,\tau\bigl(\tau-2b+x(\tau-2a)\bigr)
     -y(x+1)\bigl(m\tau^2-x(\tau-2b)(\tau-2a)\bigr)=0.\label{eq:E2}\tag{10.6}\end{align}





So \ref{prop:acute} follows from the next lemma.

blocks.label: lem:elim
blocks.title: lem:elim
blocks.body:
There are no reals $x,y,m,a,b,\tau$ with $1<y<x$, $m>0$,
$a>0$, $0<b<\tfrac12$, $2a<\tau$ and $2b<\tau$ satisfying
\eqref{eq:affine}, \eqref{eq:E1} and~\eqref{eq:E2}.

blocks.tex:
Put
\[
  D_0=x(x+1)a-(x^2-y),\qquad N_0=(x+1)(x-y)+2x(y-1)a,\qquad
  \mathcal H=2bD_0+N_0 .
\]
\emph{Step 1: $\mathcal H=0$.} Write $\mathcal E_1=c_1m+d_1$ and
$\mathcal E_2=c_2m+d_2$; then $c_1d_2-d_1c_2=0$. Here
$c_1=-y(x(1-2a)+1-2b)+x(x+1)(1-2a)(1-2b)$,
$d_1=xy(x(1-2a)+1-2b)-(x+1)y^2$,
$c_2=x\tau(\tau-2b+x(\tau-2a))-y(x+1)\tau^2$ and
$d_2=-y^2\tau(\tau-2b+x(\tau-2a))+xy(x+1)(\tau-2b)(\tau-2a)$. Solving
\eqref{eq:affine} for $\tau$ (note $(x+1)(x-y)\ne0$) and substituting, one has
the identity of rational functions
\begin{equation}\label{eq:resultant}
  (x+1)(x-y)\,(c_1d_2-d_1c_2)\big|_{\tau=\tau(a,b)}
  =8xy\,(a-b)\,\bigl(b(x^2-y)+x^2a(y-1)\bigr)\,\mathcal H.\tag{10.7}\end{equation}


If $a=b$, then \eqref{eq:affine} reads $(x+1)(x-y)(2a-1-\tau)=0$, so
$\tau=2a-1<2a$, contradicting $\tau>2a$. Also $b(x^2-y)+x^2a(y-1)>0$. Hence
$\mathcal H=0$.

\emph{Step 2: two consequences.} The identities
\[
  (x+1)\bigl((x-y)\tau-2bxa\bigr)+\mathcal H+\mathcal A=0,
  \qquad
  D_0\,\mathcal E_1+(x+1)\,\mathcal C=c_H\,\mathcal H,
\]
with $c_H=2mx^2a-mx^2+2mxa-mx+my-xy$ and
$\mathcal C=m\,x\,\mathcal D(a)+y\,\mathcal P(a)$, where
\begin{align*}
  \mathcal P(a)&=2x^3a^2+(-3x^3+x^2y+x^2+xy)\,a+(x^3-x^2y-x^2+y^2),\\
  \mathcal D(a)&=2x(x+y-1)\,a^2+(-x^2-xy+3x-y)\,a+(y-x),
\end{align*}
give $(x-y)\tau=2bxa$ and $\mathcal C=0$.



\emph{Step 3: a forced interval.} $N_0>0$, and $2bD_0=-N_0$ gives $D_0<0$.
From $(x-y)\tau=2bxa$ and $\tau>2b$ we get $a>(x-y)/x$. From $\mathcal H=0$,
$N_0+D_0=(1-2b)D_0<0$, and $N_0+D_0=x\bigl(a(x+2y-1)-(y-1)\bigr)$. Thus
\begin{equation}\label{eq:interval}
  a_-:=\frac{x-y}{x}<a<a_+:=\frac{y-1}{x+2y-1},\tag{10.8}\end{equation}

and in particular $a_-<a_+$, which is equivalent to $x^2-2y^2+y<0$.

\emph{Step 4: a sign obstruction.} $\mathcal P$ and $\mathcal D$ are convex
quadratics in $a$, so it suffices that each is negative at two points
bracketing~\eqref{eq:interval}. Direct evaluation gives
\begin{align*}
  \mathcal P(a_-)&=-xy(x-y), &
  \mathcal P\Bigl(\tfrac{x^2-y}{x(x+1)}\Bigr)&=-\frac{x(x+y)(x^2-2y+1)}{(x+1)^2},\\
  \mathcal D(a_-)&=\frac{(x-y)(x^2-xy-2y^2+y)}{x}, &
  \mathcal D(a_+)&=-\frac{y(x+y)(x^2-2y+1)}{(x+2y-1)^2}.
\end{align*}
Here $x^2-2y+1>2x-2y>0$, $x^2-xy-2y^2+y<x^2-2y^2+y<0$, and
$a_+<\frac{x^2-y}{x(x+1)}$, which after cross-multiplying is
$(x+y)(x^2-2y+1)>0$. So $\mathcal P(a)<0$ and $\mathcal D(a)<0$, hence
$\mathcal C<0$, contradicting $\mathcal C=0$.
\part{Supporting proofs}

chapters.title: The coherent discrete converse for every \texorpdfstring{$n\ge4$}{n >= 4}: regular four-edge anchors

blocks.tex:
This chapter documents the proof, checked in Lean, of the coherent discrete
converse four-vertex theorem in its original form: for every $n\ge4$,
\emph{every} positive cyclic curvature word which is constant or has a strict
four-vertex window at a positive level is realized by a simple moderate-arc
Euclidean $n$-gon with exactly those curvatures, closing up exactly and
turning through the real angle $2\pi$.  The Lean statement is
\verb|Gluck.Discrete.tabachnikovProblem2_all|
(\cref{thm:tabachnikov_all}); it proves the unchanged proposition
\cref{def:tab_problem2}.

We recall the exact data (\cref{def:tab_problem2},
\cref{def:discrete_fourvertex_pos}, \cref{def:discrete_realizes}).  A
curvature word is $\kappa\colon\ZMod n\to\RR$; edge $i$ joins vertex $i$ to
vertex $i+1$ and has full length $\ell_i$.

\textbf{The hypothesis.} $\operatorname{DiscreteFourVertexPos}(\kappa)$
says: every reading is positive, $\kappa_i>0$, \emph{and} either $\kappa$ is
constant or $\operatorname{DFV}(\kappa;c)$ holds for some $c>0$.  The latter
(\cref{def:discrete_fourvertex}) asks for natural lifts
$i_1<i_2<i_3<i_4<i_1+n$ with $\kappa_{i_2},\kappa_{i_4}<c<\kappa_{i_1},
\kappa_{i_3}$.  Only these four positions are constrained.  Readings between
them are arbitrary positive numbers; in particular adjacent equal readings
(plateaus, constant runs) are allowed anywhere, and there is no bound on the
number of distinct values.  Positivity alone is \emph{not} a four-vertex
hypothesis, and a constant word has no strict window; the constant case is a
separate disjunct.

\textbf{The conclusion.} $\operatorname{RealizesR2}(\kappa)$ asks for lengths
$\ell\colon\ZMod n\to\RR$ with
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $\operatorname{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell$: every $\ell_i>0$ and
    both strict endpoint walls $|\kappa_i|\,\ell_{i-1}/2<1$ and
    $|\kappa_i|\,\ell_i/2<1$ hold at every vertex.  For positive $\kappa$
    this is the box $0<\ell_e<\operatorname{edgeCap}(\kappa)_e=
    2/\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})$ (\cref{def:edge_cap},
    \cref{lem:moderate_arc_edge});
  \item exact complex closure $E(\kappa,\ell)=\sum_{k<n}\ell_k
    e^{i\psi_k}=0$, where the heading $\psi_k=\sum_{m\le k}\theta_m$ is the
    lifted sum of the turning angles
    $\theta_m=\arcsin(\kappa_m\ell_{m-1}/2)+\arcsin(\kappa_m\ell_m/2)$;
  \item real total turn $T(\kappa,\ell)=\sum_{i}\theta_i=2\pi$ (a real
    equation, not an equation modulo $2\pi$);
  \item the resulting polygon is simple.
\end{enumerate}

It is convenient to regroup the turn by edges: the \emph{gap} of edge $e$ is
$\operatorname{gap}_e=\arcsin(\kappa_e\ell_e/2)+\arcsin(\kappa_{e+1}\ell_e/2)$,
and $T=\sum_e\operatorname{gap}_e$, since each arcsine term of a turning
angle belongs to exactly one incident edge.

blocks.title: Four actual edges and their controller

blocks.label: def:four_active_frame
blocks.title: four actual edges
blocks.body:
A \emph{frame} of size $n$ is a strictly increasing choice of natural
  numbers $0\le e_0<e_1<e_2<e_3<n$; write $r_j=e_j\bmod n\in\ZMod n$ for the
  corresponding original edges (they are pairwise distinct).  For
  half-lengths $L\in\RR^4$ the \emph{ambient lengths} are
  \[
    \ell(L)_i=\begin{cases}2L_j,& i=r_j,\\ 0,& i\notin\{r_0,r_1,r_2,r_3\},
    \end{cases}
  \]
  a linear map $\RR^4\to\RR^{\ZMod n}$.  For a word $\kappa$ the
  \emph{literal endpoint readings} of the selected edges are
  \[
    s_j=\operatorname{start}_j=\kappa(r_j),\qquad
    t_j=\operatorname{finish}_j=\kappa(r_j+1).
  \]
  These are actual readings of the original word at actual indices; no
  reading is replaced or merged.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.finish
lean.code: def finish (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (j : Fin 4) : ℝ := κ (F.residue j + 1)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.start
lean.code: def start (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (j : Fin 4) : ℝ := κ (F.residue j)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.lengths
lean.code:
noncomputable def lengths (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) (i : ZMod n) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j : Fin 4, if i = F.residue j then 2 * L j else 0

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame
lean.code:
structure Frame (n : ℕ) where
  edge : Fin 4 → ℕ
  strictMono : StrictMono edge
  lt_n : ∀ j, edge j < n

namespace Frame

variable {n : ℕ} (F : Frame n)

blocks.label: def:four_active_controller
blocks.title: the four-edge controller
blocks.body:
Put $\alpha_j=\arcsin(s_jL_j)$ and $\beta_j=\arcsin(t_jL_j)$, and define
  the grouped turns (subscripts of $\beta$ modulo four)
  \[
    \Theta_0=\beta_3+\alpha_0,\quad \Theta_1=\beta_0+\alpha_1,\quad
    \Theta_2=\beta_1+\alpha_2,\quad \Theta_3=\beta_2+\alpha_3 .
  \]
  With $u(x)=e^{ix}$ the controller is $C(L)=(C_1(L),C_2(L))\in\CC\times\RR$,
  \[
    C_1(L)=L_0+L_1u(\Theta_1)+L_2u(\Theta_1+\Theta_2)+
      L_3u(\Theta_1+\Theta_2+\Theta_3),\qquad
    C_2(L)=\Theta_0+\Theta_1+\Theta_2+\Theta_3-2\pi .
  \]
  Thus $C_1$ is the half-length closure of the four selected edges written in
  the heading gauge of edge $r_0$, and $C_2$ is the real turn defect.  The
  target $\CC\times\RR$ is three-dimensional, while there are four length
  variables: $C=0$ is three real equations in four unknowns.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.controller
lean.code:
noncomputable def controller (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) : ℂ × ℝ :=
  let θ := F.turns κ L
  ((L 0 : ℂ) + (L 1 : ℂ) * unitPhase (θ 1) +
    (L 2 : ℂ) * unitPhase (θ 1 + θ 2) +
    (L 3 : ℂ) * unitPhase (θ 1 + θ 2 + θ 3),
    θ 0 + θ 1 + θ 2 + θ 3 - 2 * Real.pi)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.turns
lean.code:
noncomputable def turns (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) : Fin 4 → ℝ :=
  ![F.finishArc κ L 3 + F.startArc κ L 0,
    F.finishArc κ L 0 + F.startArc κ L 1,
    F.finishArc κ L 1 + F.startArc κ L 2,
    F.finishArc κ L 2 + F.startArc κ L 3]

blocks.tex:
The block turn $\Theta_j$ is the whole turning between consecutive selected
edges: all intermediate readings are still present, but the zero lengths of
the intervening edges make their arcsine terms vanish.

blocks.label: lem:four_active_embedding
blocks.title: exact ambient embedding
blocks.body:
For every word $\kappa$ (with $n\neq0$ for the turn) and \emph{every}
  $L\in\RR^4$,
  \[
    T(\kappa,\ell(L))-2\pi=C_2(L),\qquad
    E(\kappa,\ell(L))=2\,u\bigl(\psi_{e_0}(\kappa,\ell(L))\bigr)\,C_1(L).
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.closureGap_eq_controller
lean.code:
theorem closureGap_eq_controller (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    closureGap κ (F.lengths L) =
      2 * unitPhase (heading κ (F.lengths L) (F.edge 0)) * (F.controller κ L).1 := by
  have hsum : closureGap κ (F.lengths L) =
      ∑ j : Fin 4, ((2 * L j : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        unitPhase (heading κ (F.lengths L) (F.edge j)) := by
    unfold closureGap vertexR2
    rw [F.sum_range_selected]
    · apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro j _
      change (F.lengths L (F.residue j) : ℂ) * _ = _
      rw [F.lengths_selected]
      rfl
    · intro k hk hne
      rw [F.lengths_unselected L (F.residue_ne_of_nat_ne hk hne)]
      simp
  rw [hsum]
  calc
    _ = ∑ j : Fin 4, ((2 * L j : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        (unitPhase (heading κ (F.lengths L) (F.edge 0)) *
          unitPhase (F.relativeHeading κ L j)) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro j _
      rw [F.heading_selected κ L j, unitPhase_add]
    _ = _ := by
      rw [Fin.sum_univ_four]
      have hzero : unitPhase 0 = 1 := by simp [unitPhase]
      simp only [F.relativeHeading_zero, F.relativeHeading_one, F.relativeHeading_two,
        F.relativeHeading_three, hzero, mul_one, controller,
        Complex.ofReal_mul, Complex.ofReal_ofNat]
      ring

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.turningSum_eq_controller
lean.code:
theorem turningSum_eq_controller [NeZero n] (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    turningSum κ (F.lengths L) - 2 * Real.pi = (F.controller κ L).2 := by
  rw [F.turningSum_lengths, Fin.sum_univ_four]
  simp only [controller, turns, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one,
    Matrix.cons_val, Fin.isValue]
  ring

blocks.tex:
Both identities are proved on the whole slice, before imposing closure or
  full turn, so they may be differentiated.

  \emph{Turn.}  Write $T=\sum_{k<n}\operatorname{gap}_k$.  An unselected
  edge has $\ell_k=0$, so its gap is $\arcsin 0+\arcsin 0=0$; the sparse sum
  over $k<n$ therefore reduces to the four selected natural indices
  $e_j$.  At a selected edge $\ell=2L_j$, so its gap is exactly
  $\alpha_j+\beta_j$.  Hence $T=\sum_j(\alpha_j+\beta_j)=\sum_j\Theta_j$,
  the last step being a regrouping of the same eight terms.

  \emph{Headings.}  Unfolding the lifted heading gives
  \[
    \psi_k=\arcsin(\kappa_0\ell_{-1}/2)+\sum_{k'<k}\operatorname{gap}_{k'}
      +\arcsin(\kappa_k\ell_k/2).
  \]
  For a selected $e_j$, the prefix of gaps below $e_j$ contains exactly the
  selected edges $e_k$ with $k<j$ (the frame is increasing), so
  \[
    \psi_{e_j}=\psi_{e_0}+\Bigl(\sum_{k<j}(\alpha_k+\beta_k)\Bigr)+\alpha_j-\alpha_0 ,
  \]
  and the relative headings $\psi_{e_j}-\psi_{e_0}$ are $0$, $\Theta_1$,
  $\Theta_1+\Theta_2$ and $\Theta_1+\Theta_2+\Theta_3$ for $j=0,1,2,3$.

  \emph{Closure.}  In $E=\sum_{k<n}\ell_ku(\psi_k)$ the unselected terms
  vanish, leaving $\sum_j2L_j\,u(\psi_{e_j})$.  Factor
  $u(\psi_{e_j})=u(\psi_{e_0})\,u(\psi_{e_j}-\psi_{e_0})$ and insert the
  relative headings: the result is $2u(\psi_{e_0})C_1(L)$.  The factor
  $2$ is the full/half-length convention, and $u(\psi_{e_0})$ is the heading
  gauge; both are nonzero.

blocks.label: lem:four_active_native_rank
blocks.title: native derivative surjectivity on the active edges
blocks.body:
Let $\kappa>0$, $L_j>0$, $s_jL_j<1$ and $t_jL_j<1$ for all $j$, and
  $C(L)=0$.  Then $0\le\ell(L)_i<\operatorname{edgeCap}(\kappa)_i$ for
  every $i$, and for all $v\in\RR^4$
  \[
    DG(\ell(L))\,\ell(v)=\bigl(2u(\psi_{e_0})\,DC_1(L)v,\;DC_2(L)v\bigr),
  \]
  where $G(\ell)=(E(\kappa,\ell),T(\kappa,\ell)-2\pi)$ is the ambient
  length-only closure map.  Consequently, if $DC(L)\colon\RR^4\to\CC\times\RR$
  is surjective, then every $y\in\CC\times\RR$ is $DG(\ell(L))\,b$ for some
  $b$ with $b_i=0$ at every $i$ where $\ell(L)_i=0$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.active_surj_of_controller_regular
lean.code:
theorem active_surj_of_controller_regular [NeZero n]
    {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {L : Fin 4 → ℝ}
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hL : ∀ j, 0 < L j)
    (hbounds : ∀ i, 0 ≤ F.lengths L i ∧ F.lengths L i < edgeCap κ i)
    (hzero : F.controller κ L = 0)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (F.controller κ) L)) :
    ∀ y : ℂ × ℝ, ∃ b : ZMod n → ℝ,
      fderiv ℝ (fun ell => closureMapR3 (κ, ell)) (F.lengths L) b = y ∧
        ∀ i, F.lengths L i = 0 → b i = 0 := by
  have hd : DifferentiableAt ℝ (F.controller κ) L := by
    by_contra hn
    rw [fderiv_zero_of_not_differentiableAt hn] at hsurj
    obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hsurj (0, 1)
    have := congrArg Prod.snd hv
    norm_num at this
  let g : ℂ := 2 * unitPhase (heading κ (F.lengths L) (F.edge 0))
  have hg : g ≠ 0 := mul_ne_zero (by norm_num) (Complex.exp_ne_zero _)
  intro y
  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hsurj (y.1 / g, y.2)
  refine ⟨F.lengths v, ?_, F.lengths_direction_supported L v hL⟩
  rw [F.fderiv_lengths_at_controller_zero hκ hbounds hd hzero, hv]
  change (g * (y.1 / g), y.2) = y
  rw [mul_div_cancel₀ _ hg]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.lengths_nonneg_lt_edgeCap
lean.code:
theorem lengths_nonneg_lt_edgeCap (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ)
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hL : ∀ j, 0 < L j)
    (hstart : ∀ j, F.start κ j * L j < 1)
    (hfinish : ∀ j, F.finish κ j * L j < 1) :
    ∀ i, 0 ≤ F.lengths L i ∧ F.lengths L i < edgeCap κ i := by
  intro i
  by_cases hi : ∃ j, i = F.residue j
  · obtain ⟨j, rfl⟩ := hi
    rw [F.lengths_selected]
    refine ⟨(mul_pos (by norm_num) (hL j)).le, ?_⟩
    have hm : 0 < max (κ (F.residue j)) (κ (F.residue j + 1)) :=
      lt_of_lt_of_le (hκ _) (le_max_left _ _)
    rw [edgeCap, lt_div_iff₀ hm]
    have hs := hstart j
    have hf := hfinish j
    change κ (F.residue j) * L j < 1 at hs
    change κ (F.residue j + 1) * L j < 1 at hf
    rcases le_total (κ (F.residue j)) (κ (F.residue j + 1)) with hh | hh
    · rw [max_eq_right hh]
      nlinarith
    · rw [max_eq_left hh]
      nlinarith
  · have hoff : ∀ j, i ≠ F.residue j := fun j he => hi ⟨j, he⟩
    rw [F.lengths_unselected L hoff]
    exact ⟨le_rfl, (edgeCap_pos (hκ _) (hκ _)).1⟩

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.fderiv_lengths_at_controller_zero
lean.code:
theorem fderiv_lengths_at_controller_zero [NeZero n]
    {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {L : Fin 4 → ℝ}
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i)
    (hbounds : ∀ i, 0 ≤ F.lengths L i ∧ F.lengths L i < edgeCap κ i)
    (hd : DifferentiableAt ℝ (F.controller κ) L)
    (hzero : F.controller κ L = 0) (v : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun ell => closureMapR3 (κ, ell)) (F.lengths L) (F.lengths v) =
      (2 * unitPhase (heading κ (F.lengths L) (F.edge 0)) *
        (fderiv ℝ (F.controller κ) L v).1,
        (fderiv ℝ (F.controller κ) L v).2) := by
  let g : (Fin 4 → ℝ) → ℂ := fun X =>
    2 * unitPhase (heading κ (F.lengths X) (F.edge 0))
  have hw := strict_arc_walls_of_nonneg_lt_edgeCap hκ hbounds
  have hheading := contDiffAt_heading_lengths (F.edge 0)
    (fun j _ => hw (j : ZMod n))
  have hheading' : DifferentiableAt ℝ
      (fun X : Fin 4 → ℝ => heading κ (F.lengths X) (F.edge 0)) L := by
    exact (hheading.differentiableAt one_ne_zero).comp L F.lengthsCLM.differentiableAt
  have hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g L := by
    dsimp [g, unitPhase]
    fun_prop
  have hprod := (hg.hasFDerivAt.mul hd.hasFDerivAt.fst).prodMk hd.hasFDerivAt.snd
  have hfun : (fun X : Fin 4 → ℝ => (g X * (F.controller κ X).1,
      (F.controller κ X).2)) = (fun X => closureMapR3 (κ, F.lengths X)) := by
    funext X
    apply Prod.ext
    · exact (F.closureGap_eq_controller κ X).symm
    · exact (F.turningSum_eq_controller κ X).symm
  change HasFDerivAt (fun X : Fin 4 → ℝ =>
    (g X * (F.controller κ X).1, (F.controller κ X).2)) _ L at hprod
  rw [hfun] at hprod
  have hamb := (lengthClosureMap_hasStrictFDerivAt_of_nonneg_lt_edgeCap hκ hbounds).hasFDerivAt
  have hcomp := hamb.comp L F.lengthsCLM.hasFDerivAt
  have heq := hcomp.unique hprod
  have hv := congrArg (fun A : (Fin 4 → ℝ) →L[ℝ] (ℂ × ℝ) => A v) heq
  simpa [g, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, hzero, smul_eq_mul] using hv

deps.title: sub-cap lengths satisfy the arcsine walls
deps.label: lem:wc_dormant_walls

deps.title: the length controller is strictly differentiable at zero lengths
deps.label: thm:wc_dormant_deriv

blocks.tex:
\emph{Caps.}  At a selected edge, $\ell=2L_j<2/\max(s_j,t_j)$ is
  equivalent to $\max(s_j,t_j)L_j<1$, i.e.\ to the two strict endpoint
  bounds.  At an unselected edge $\ell=0<\operatorname{edgeCap}$ because
  $\kappa>0$.  So the hypotheses of \cref{lem:wc_dormant_walls} and
  \cref{thm:wc_dormant_deriv} hold and $G$ is strictly differentiable at
  $\ell(L)$; in particular the heading $\psi_{e_0}$ is differentiable along
  the slice.

  \emph{Derivative.}  By \cref{lem:four_active_embedding},
  $G(\ell(X))=(g(X)\,C_1(X),C_2(X))$ with
  $g(X)=2u(\psi_{e_0}(\kappa,\ell(X)))$, for all $X$.  Surjectivity of
  $DC(L)$ forces $C$ to be differentiable at $L$ (otherwise its derivative is
  zero by convention).  The product rule gives
  $D(gC_1)(L)v=(Dg(L)v)\,C_1(L)+g(L)\,DC_1(L)v$, and the first term vanishes
  because $C_1(L)=0$: at a zero, differentiating the variable heading
  rotation contributes nothing.  Since $\ell$ is linear, the chain rule and
  uniqueness of derivatives give the displayed formula.

  \emph{Active rank.}  Given $y=(y_1,y_2)$, choose $v$ with
  $DC(L)v=(y_1/g(L),y_2)$, possible because $g(L)=2u(\psi_{e_0})\ne0$, and
  set $b=\ell(v)$.  Then $DG(\ell(L))b=y$.  The correction $b$ is supported
  on the four selected edges, where $\ell(L)=2L_j>0$; hence $b_i=0$ wherever
  $\ell(L)_i=0$.  No dormant direction is used to supply rank.

blocks.label: def:regular_four_anchor
blocks.title: regular four-edge anchor

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor
lean.code:
structure RegularFourAnchor {n : ℕ} (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) where
  frame : FourActiveSlots.Frame n
  halfLengths : Fin 4 → ℝ
  positive : ∀ j, 0 < halfLengths j
  start_lt : ∀ j, frame.start κ j * halfLengths j < 1
  finish_lt : ∀ j, frame.finish κ j * halfLengths j < 1
  zero : frame.controller κ halfLengths = 0
  regular : Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (frame.controller κ) halfLengths)

blocks.label: lem:regular_four_reembed
blocks.title: endpoint-preserving reembedding
blocks.body:
Let $F$ be a frame of size $m$ for a word $\mu$ and $G$ a frame of size
  $n$ for a word $\kappa$, with the same literal readings:
  $\operatorname{start}^G_\kappa=\operatorname{start}^F_\mu$ and
  $\operatorname{finish}^G_\kappa=\operatorname{finish}^F_\mu$.  Then
  $C^G_\kappa=C^F_\mu$ as functions on $\RR^4$.  Hence a regular anchor
  $(F,L)$ for $\mu$ yields the regular anchor $(G,L)$ for $\kappa$, with the
  same half-lengths.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.reembed
lean.code:
noncomputable def reembed {m n : ℕ} {μ : ZMod m → ℝ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (A : RegularFourAnchor μ) (G : FourActiveSlots.Frame n)
    (hstart : G.start κ = A.frame.start μ) (hfinish : G.finish κ = A.frame.finish μ) :
    RegularFourAnchor κ where
  frame := G
  halfLengths := A.halfLengths
  positive := A.positive
  start_lt := by simpa only [hstart] using A.start_lt
  finish_lt := by simpa only [hfinish] using A.finish_lt
  zero := by rw [controller_eq_of_endpoints hstart hfinish]; exact A.zero
  regular := by rw [controller_eq_of_endpoints hstart hfinish]; exact A.regular

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.controller_eq_of_endpoints
lean.code:
theorem controller_eq_of_endpoints {m n : ℕ} {μ : ZMod m → ℝ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {F : FourActiveSlots.Frame m} {G : FourActiveSlots.Frame n}
    (hstart : G.start κ = F.start μ) (hfinish : G.finish κ = F.finish μ) :
    G.controller κ = F.controller μ := by
  funext L
  simp only [FourActiveSlots.Frame.controller, FourActiveSlots.Frame.turns,
    FourActiveSlots.Frame.startArc, FourActiveSlots.Frame.finishArc, hstart, hfinish]

blocks.tex:
The controller depends on the word and the frame only through the eight
  numbers $s_j,t_j$, which enter through $\alpha_j,\beta_j$.  Equal endpoint
  functions give literally equal turns and equal controllers, as functions.
  Therefore the same $L$ satisfies positivity, the eight strict bounds (they
  are the same inequalities), $C(L)=0$, and the derivative at $L$ is the
  same linear map, so surjectivity transfers.  The number $n-4$ and the
  values of all unselected readings are irrelevant.  This is an exact
  identification, not a limiting argument.

blocks.title: Opening an anchor: every curvature fixed

blocks.label: thm:regular_four_anchor_realizes
blocks.title: a regular anchor realizes the whole word
blocks.body:
Let $n\neq0$, let $\kappa\colon\ZMod n\to\RR$ be positive, and let
  $\kappa$ have a regular four-edge anchor.  Then
  $\operatorname{RealizesR2}(\kappa)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.realizesR2
Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.realizesR2_of_controller_regular
lean.code:
theorem realizesR2_of_controller_regular [NeZero n]
    {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {L : Fin 4 → ℝ}
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hL : ∀ j, 0 < L j)
    (hstart : ∀ j, F.start κ j * L j < 1)
    (hfinish : ∀ j, F.finish κ j * L j < 1)
    (hzero : F.controller κ L = 0)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (F.controller κ) L)) :
    RealizesR2 κ := by
  have hbounds := F.lengths_nonneg_lt_edgeCap κ L hκ hL hstart hfinish
  have h01 := F.strictMono (show (0 : Fin 4) < 1 by decide)
  have h12 := F.strictMono (show (1 : Fin 4) < 2 by decide)
  have h23 := F.strictMono (show (2 : Fin 4) < 3 by decide)
  have h3n := F.lt_n 3
  have hn : 3 ≤ n := by omega
  have hambzero : closureMapR3 (κ, F.lengths L) = 0 := by
    unfold closureMapR3
    rw [F.closureGap_eq_controller, F.turningSum_eq_controller, hzero]
    simp
  exact realizesR2_of_regular_dormant_anchor_of_active_surj hn hκ hbounds hambzero
    (F.active_surj_of_controller_regular hκ hL hbounds hzero hsurj)

deps.title: surjectivity away from the collapsed coordinates suffices
deps.label: cor:wc_dormant_active_surj

deps.title: native derivative surjectivity on the active edges
deps.label: lem:four_active_native_rank

blocks.tex:
Let $\ell^0=\ell(L)$.  By \cref{lem:four_active_native_rank},
  $0\le\ell^0<\operatorname{edgeCap}$ coordinatewise.  By
  \cref{lem:four_active_embedding} and $C(L)=0$, both $E(\kappa,\ell^0)=0$
  and $T(\kappa,\ell^0)=2\pi$: the ambient map $G$ vanishes at $\ell^0$.
  The frame has four distinct natural indices below $n$, so $n\ge4\ge3$.
  By \cref{lem:four_active_native_rank} every target of $DG(\ell^0)$ is
  reached by a correction vanishing on the collapsed coordinates
  $Z=\{i:\ell^0_i=0\}$.  This is the hypothesis of
  \cref{cor:wc_dormant_active_surj}, which gives $\operatorname{RealizesR2}$.

  For the reader we unwind that corollary.  Let $d_i=1$ for $i\in Z$ and
  $d_i=0$ otherwise.  Choose $b$ vanishing on $Z$ with
  $DG(\ell^0)b=-DG(\ell^0)d$.  Then $v=d+b$ lies in $\ker DG(\ell^0)$ and
  $v_i=1>0$ at every dormant coordinate: it points strictly into every
  collapsed face $\{\ell_i\ge0\}$.  Since $G$ is strictly differentiable with
  surjective derivative (\cref{thm:wc_dormant_deriv}), the purification
  theorem behind \cref{thm:wc_dormant_opens} provides a curve $\gamma$ in
  the length space alone --- the word $\kappa$ is never changed --- with
  $G(\gamma(\tau))=0$ and $\gamma(\tau)$ strictly inside all $2n$ slacks
  $\ell_i>0$, $\operatorname{edgeCap}_i-\ell_i>0$ for small $\tau>0$.  The
  upper slacks were already strict at $\ell^0$ and stay strict; the active
  edges were already positive; the dormant ones become positive along $v$.
  So $\ell=\gamma(\tau)$ is strictly moderate, closes exactly and has real
  total turn $2\pi$.  With $\kappa>0$ every turning angle is positive, and
  the collar realization lemma \cref{lem:collar_realizes_of_mem}, via the
  convexity theorem \cref{thm:convex_simple}, gives simplicity.

  If $n=4$ the frame is all four edges, $Z=\varnothing$, $d=0$, and the
  anchor itself is already a strictly moderate closed configuration; the same
  argument applies with a vacuous inward condition.  The opening parameter
  $\tau$ depends on the particular word; no radius uniform in $\kappa$ is
  claimed or needed.

blocks.label: lem:four_active_dfv_collapse
blocks.title: DFV survives a monotone periodic collapse
blocks.body:
Let $r\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be monotone with $r(i+n)=r(i)+m$ and
  $\mu(r(i))=\kappa(i)$ for all $i$.  If $\operatorname{DFV}(\kappa;c)$
  then $\operatorname{DFV}(\mu;c)$.  Moreover any DFV word has length at
  least $4$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.DFV.four_le_period
lean.code:
theorem DFV.four_le_period {n : ℕ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
    (hdfv : DFV κ c) : 4 ≤ n := by
  obtain ⟨i₁, i₂, i₃, i₄, h12, h23, h34, h41, _⟩ := hdfv
  omega

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.DFV.of_monotone_periodic_collapse
lean.code:
theorem DFV.of_monotone_periodic_collapse
    {n m : ℕ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {μ : ZMod m → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
    {r : ℕ → ℕ} (hr : Monotone r)
    (hperiod : ∀ i, r (i + n) = r i + m)
    (hreading : ∀ i, μ (r i : ZMod m) = κ (i : ZMod n))
    (hdfv : DFV κ c) : DFV μ c := by
  obtain ⟨i₁, i₂, i₃, i₄, h12, h23, h34, h41, h1, h2, h3, h4⟩ := hdfv
  have hm1 : c < μ (r i₁ : ZMod m) := by rwa [hreading]
  have hm2 : μ (r i₂ : ZMod m) < c := by rwa [hreading]
  have hm3 : c < μ (r i₃ : ZMod m) := by rwa [hreading]
  have hm4 : μ (r i₄ : ZMod m) < c := by rwa [hreading]
  have hr12 : r i₁ < r i₂ := by
    have hle := hr h12.le
    by_contra hnot
    have he : r i₁ = r i₂ := by omega
    rw [he] at hm1
    linarith
  have hr23 : r i₂ < r i₃ := by
    have hle := hr h23.le
    by_contra hnot
    have he : r i₂ = r i₃ := by omega
    rw [he] at hm2
    linarith
  have hr34 : r i₃ < r i₄ := by
    have hle := hr h34.le
    by_contra hnot
    have he : r i₃ = r i₄ := by omega
    rw [he] at hm3
    linarith
  have hr41 : r i₄ < r i₁ + m := by
    have hle : r i₄ ≤ r i₁ + m := by
      simpa [hperiod] using hr h41.le
    by_contra hnot
    have he : r i₄ = r i₁ + m := by omega
    rw [he] at hm4
    simp only [Nat.cast_add, ZMod.natCast_self, add_zero] at hm4
    linarith
  exact ⟨r i₁, r i₂, r i₃, r i₄, hr12, hr23, hr34, hr41, hm1, hm2, hm3, hm4⟩

blocks.tex:
Push the four window witnesses forward by $r$.  Monotonicity gives
  $r(i_1)\le r(i_2)\le r(i_3)\le r(i_4)\le r(i_1)+m$.  No two consecutive
  images can coincide: their readings are $\mu(r(i_k))=\kappa(i_k)$, which
  lie strictly on opposite sides of $c$.  The same holds across the period,
  since $\mu(r(i_1)+m)=\mu(r(i_1))>c>\mu(r(i_4))$.  So all inequalities are
  strict and the images are a window at the same level.  Four strictly
  increasing naturals below $i_1+n$ force $n\ge4$.

blocks.label: lem:four_active_erase_restore
blocks.title: erase a repeated reading and restore the frame
blocks.body:
Let $w\colon\ZMod(m+1)\to\RR$ with $m\ne0$ and $w_a=w_{a+1}$ for some
  $0\le a\le m$.  Let $\operatorname{skip}_a(j)=j$ for $j<a$ and $j+1$
  otherwise, and let $w'\colon\ZMod m\to\RR$, $w'_j=w_{\operatorname{skip}_a(j)}$
  (delete entry $a$).  Then $w'$ is positive when $w$ is, and
  $\operatorname{DFV}(w;c)\Rightarrow\operatorname{DFV}(w';c)$.  Every
  frame $e_0<\dots<e_3<m$ of $w'$ gives the frame
  $\operatorname{skip}_a(e_0)<\dots<\operatorname{skip}_a(e_3)<m+1$ of $w$
  with identical start and finish functions; hence every regular anchor of
  $w'$ reembeds as a regular anchor of $w$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ConstantRun.restoreFrame
lean.code:
def restoreFrame {m : ℕ} (F : FourActiveSlots.Frame m) (a : Fin (m + 1)) :
    FourActiveSlots.Frame (m + 1) where
  edge := fun j => skip a.val (F.edge j)
  strictMono := (skip_strictMono a.val).comp F.strictMono
  lt_n := fun j => skip_lt (F.lt_n j)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ConstantRun.eraseWord_dfv
lean.code:
theorem eraseWord_dfv {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] {κ : ZMod (m + 1) → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
    (a : Fin (m + 1))
    (hdup : κ (a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) = κ ((a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) + 1))
    (hdfv : DFV κ c) : DFV (eraseWord κ a) c :=
  hdfv.of_monotone_periodic_collapse (collapse_mono m a.val)
    (collapse_add_period m a.val) (eraseWord_collapse a hdup)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ConstantRun.restoreFrame_finish
lean.code:
theorem restoreFrame_finish {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] (F : FourActiveSlots.Frame m)
    {κ : ZMod (m + 1) → ℝ} (a : Fin (m + 1))
    (hdup : κ (a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) = κ ((a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) + 1)) :
    (restoreFrame F a).finish κ = F.finish (eraseWord κ a) := by
  funext j
  exact (eraseWord_finish a hdup (F.lt_n j)).symm

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ConstantRun.restoreAnchor
lean.code:
noncomputable def restoreAnchor {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] {κ : ZMod (m + 1) → ℝ}
    (a : Fin (m + 1))
    (hdup : κ (a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) = κ ((a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) + 1))
    (A : RegularFourAnchor (eraseWord κ a)) : RegularFourAnchor κ :=
  A.reembed (restoreFrame A.frame a) (restoreFrame_start A.frame κ a)
    (restoreFrame_finish A.frame a hdup)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ConstantRun.eraseWord
lean.code:
def eraseWord {m : ℕ} (κ : ZMod (m + 1) → ℝ) (a : Fin (m + 1)) :
    ZMod m → ℝ := fun i => κ (skip a.val i.val : ZMod (m + 1))

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ConstantRun.restoreFrame_start
lean.code:
theorem restoreFrame_start {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] (F : FourActiveSlots.Frame m)
    (κ : ZMod (m + 1) → ℝ) (a : Fin (m + 1)) :
    (restoreFrame F a).start κ = F.start (eraseWord κ a) := by
  funext j
  simp [FourActiveSlots.Frame.start, FourActiveSlots.Frame.residue,
    restoreFrame, eraseWord, ZMod.val_natCast_of_lt (F.lt_n j)]

deps.title: DFV survives a monotone periodic collapse
deps.label: lem:four_active_dfv_collapse

blocks.tex:
Let $\operatorname{merge}_a(j)=j$ for $j\le a$ and $j-1$ for $j>a$, and
  extend periodically:
  $\rho(i)=\lfloor i/(m+1)\rfloor m+\operatorname{merge}_a(i\bmod(m+1))$.
  Then $\rho$ is monotone, $\rho(i+m+1)=\rho(i)+m$, and
  $w'(\rho(i))=w(i)$: away from $a$ this is the definition of deletion, and
  at $a$ it is the hypothesis $w_a=w_{a+1}$ (for $a=m$ it reads
  $w_m=w_0$, the cyclic successor).  \Cref{lem:four_active_dfv_collapse}
  transfers the window.  Start readings agree by definition,
  $w(\operatorname{skip}_a e_j)=w'(e_j)$.  For finish readings,
  $\rho(\operatorname{skip}_a(e_j)+1)=e_j+1$, so
  $w(\operatorname{skip}_a(e_j)+1)=w'(\rho(\operatorname{skip}_a(e_j)+1))
  =w'(e_j+1)$; this includes the wrap $e_j=m-1$.  Since $\operatorname{skip}_a$
  is strictly increasing and maps $[0,m)$ into $[0,m+1)$, the restored frame
  is a frame.  Now apply \cref{lem:regular_four_reembed}.

blocks.label: thm:four_active_restore_runs
blocks.title: finite restoration of constant runs
blocks.body:
Assume the \emph{producer statement}: for every $m$ and every
  $\mu\colon\ZMod m\to\RR$ with $4\le m$, $\mu>0$, $\operatorname{DFV}(\mu;c)$
  and $\mu_i\ne\mu_{i+1}$ for all $i$, $\mu$ has a regular four-edge anchor.
  Then every positive word $\kappa$ with $\operatorname{DFV}(\kappa;c)$ has a
  regular four-edge anchor.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ConstantRun.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_adjacent_unequal_producer
lean.code:
theorem nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_adjacent_unequal_producer
    (hbase : ∀ (m : ℕ) (μ : ZMod m → ℝ) (c : ℝ),
      4 ≤ m → (∀ i, 0 < μ i) → DFV μ c →
      (∀ i, μ i ≠ μ (i + 1)) → Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor μ))
    {n : ℕ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hdfv : DFV κ c) : Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  classical
  suffices hall : ∀ (k : ℕ) (w : ZMod k → ℝ) (c : ℝ),
      (∀ i, 0 < w i) → DFV w c → Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor w) by
    exact hall n κ c hκ hdfv
  intro k
  induction k using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | h k ih =>
    intro w c hw hd
    by_cases hne : ∀ i, w i ≠ w (i + 1)
    · exact hbase k w c hd.four_le_period hw hd hne
    · push Not at hne
      obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hne
      have hk := hd.four_le_period
      cases k with
      | zero => omega
      | succ m =>
        have hm : 0 < m := by omega
        let : NeZero m := ⟨by omega⟩
        let a : Fin (m + 1) := ⟨i.val, ZMod.val_lt i⟩
        have hdup : w (a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) = w ((a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) + 1) := by
          simpa only [a, ZMod.natCast_zmod_val] using hi
        have hd' := eraseWord_dfv a hdup hd
        obtain ⟨A⟩ := ih m (by omega) (eraseWord w a) c (eraseWord_positive hw a) hd'
        exact ⟨restoreAnchor a hdup A⟩

deps.title: DFV survives a monotone periodic collapse
deps.label: lem:four_active_dfv_collapse

deps.title: erase a repeated reading and restore the frame
deps.label: lem:four_active_erase_restore

blocks.tex:
Strong induction on the length $k$, for all positive DFV words of that
  length.  If the word is adjacent-unequal, apply the producer; its size
  hypothesis $k\ge4$ is supplied by \cref{lem:four_active_dfv_collapse}.
  Otherwise some $w_i=w_{i+1}$.  Since $k\ge4$, write $k=m+1$ with $m\ge3$,
  delete entry $i$ as in \cref{lem:four_active_erase_restore}: the shorter
  word is positive and DFV at the same level, so it has an anchor by the
  induction hypothesis, and the lemma restores it to $w$.  The producer
  premise remains explicit in this theorem; it is discharged in
  \cref{thm:four_active_anchor_dfv}.

This section states the producer and explains its global case partition.
The first-transition producer, with its physical roots and native rank, is
proved in full in \cref{chap:discrete_native_first_pair}.  The
repeated-maximum (equal-pure) and negative-corner producers, with their
roots, incident rank and algebraic exclusion, are proved in full in
\cref{chap:discrete_native_repeated_negative}.  The mountain selection and
the transport of anchors under scaling, cyclic shift and reflection are
proved in full in \cref{chap:discrete_mountain_anchor_transport}; this
section records their interface statements.

\textbf{Normalization and transport.}  If $\kappa>0$ has a regular anchor
then so does $s\kappa$ for $s>0$ (same frame, half-lengths $L/s$;
\cref{lem:mt_anchor_scale}), so do all cyclic shifts $i\mapsto\kappa(i+a)$
(the frame is re-sorted, and when an edge crosses the origin the four slots
are rotated; \cref{thm:mt_cyclic_anchor}), and so does the reflection
$i\mapsto\kappa(-i)$ (slots reversed and start/finish swapped;
\cref{thm:mt_reflected_anchor}); in each case the zero and the derivative
surjectivity are transported as well.  For $\kappa>0$ and an index $q$ put
$\operatorname{normalizedAt}(\kappa,q)_i=\kappa_{i+q}/\kappa_q$
(\cref{def:mt_normalized}), which has value $1$ at $0$.
