blocks.tex:
Apply the implicit function theorem to
$f(p,x+Ra)=f(p_0,x_0)$ with unknown $a\in F$. Its derivative in $a$ at
$((p_0,x_0),0)$ is the identity. The implicit solution $a=\psi(p,x)$ gives
$Q(p,x)=x+R\psi(p,x)$. Local uniqueness gives the fixed-point assertion.

blocks.label: thm:discrete_positive_section
blocks.title: Positive sections from active-supported surjectivity
blocks.body:
Let $P$ be a real Banach space and $F$ a finite-dimensional real normed
space. Suppose $f\colon P\times\RR^N\to F$ is $C^1$ near $(p_0,x_0)$,
where every coordinate of $x_0$ is nonnegative. Suppose that for every
$y\in F$ there is $b\in\RR^N$ with
\[
 D_x f(p_0,x_0)b=y,\qquad b_i=0\text{ whenever }(x_0)_i=0.
\]
For every open set $V\subseteq P\times\RR^N$ containing $(p_0,x_0)$,
there is an open neighborhood $U$ of $p_0$ and a $C^1$ map
$s\colon U\to\RR^N$ such that, for all $p\in U$,
\[
 (p,s(p))\in V,\qquad s_i(p)>0\ (1\le i\le N),\qquad
 f(p,s(p))=f(p_0,x_0).
\]
No equality $s(p_0)=x_0$ is asserted when $x_0$ has zero coordinates.

lean.name: ContDiffAt.exists_localSection_pos_of_active_surjective
lean.code:
theorem ContDiffAt.exists_localSection_pos_of_active_surjective
    {f : P × (ι → ℝ) → F} {p₀ : P} {x₀ : ι → ℝ}
    (hf : ContDiffAt ℝ 1 f (p₀, x₀)) (hx₀ : ∀ i, 0 ≤ x₀ i)
    (hactive : ∀ y : F, ∃ b : ι → ℝ,
      (fderiv ℝ f (p₀, x₀) ∘L ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ P (ι → ℝ)) b = y ∧
        ∀ i, x₀ i = 0 → b i = 0)
    {V : Set (P × (ι → ℝ))} (hV : IsOpen V) (hV₀ : (p₀, x₀) ∈ V) :
    ∃ (U : Set P) (s : P → (ι → ℝ)), IsOpen U ∧ p₀ ∈ U ∧
      ContDiffOn ℝ 1 s U ∧
      ∀ p ∈ U, (p, s p) ∈ V ∧ (∀ i, 0 < s p i) ∧ f (p, s p) = f (p₀, x₀) := by
  classical
  have : CompleteSpace F := FiniteDimensional.complete ℝ F
  let D : Submodule ℝ (ι → ℝ) :=
    { carrier := {b | ∀ i, x₀ i = 0 → b i = 0}
      zero_mem' := by simp
      add_mem' := by intro a b ha hb i hi; simp [ha i hi, hb i hi]
      smul_mem' := by intro c b hb i hi; simp [hb i hi] }
  let A := fderiv ℝ f (p₀, x₀) ∘L ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ P (ι → ℝ)
  let B : D →L[ℝ] F := A ∘L D.subtypeL
  have hB : B.range = ⊤ := by
    rw [LinearMap.range_eq_top]
    intro y
    obtain ⟨b, hb, hbs⟩ := hactive y
    exact ⟨⟨b, hbs⟩, hb⟩
  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := B.exists_rightInverse_of_surjective hB
  let R : F →L[ℝ] (ι → ℝ) := D.subtypeL ∘L g
  have hR : A ∘L R = ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ F := by
    rw [show A ∘L R = B ∘L g from rfl]
    exact hg
  obtain ⟨Q, hQcd, hQ₀, hQrange, hQeq, -⟩ :=
    hf.exists_parametricConstraintCorrection one_ne_zero R hR
  have hfixed : ∀ q i, x₀ i = 0 → Q q i = q.2 i := by
    intro q i hi
    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hQrange q
    have hz : (R a) i = 0 := (g a).property i hi
    have hai : R a i = Q q i - q.2 i := congrFun ha i
    exact sub_eq_zero.mp (hai.symm.trans hz)
  have hQpair : ContinuousAt (fun q : P × (ι → ℝ) => (q.1, Q q)) (p₀, x₀) :=
    continuousAt_fst.prodMk hQcd.continuousAt
  have hQV : ∀ᶠ q in 𝓝 (p₀, x₀), (q.1, Q q) ∈ V := by
    apply hQpair.preimage_mem_nhds
    simpa [hQ₀] using hV.mem_nhds hV₀
  have hQpos : ∀ᶠ q in 𝓝 (p₀, x₀), ∀ i, x₀ i ≠ 0 → 0 < Q q i := by
    apply eventually_all.mpr
    intro i
    by_cases hi : x₀ i = 0
    · exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall (by simp [hi])
    · have hp : 0 < Q (p₀, x₀) i := by rw [hQ₀]; exact lt_of_le_of_ne (hx₀ i) (Ne.symm hi)
      have hc := (continuous_apply i).continuousAt.comp hQcd.continuousAt
      exact (hc.eventually (isOpen_Ioi.mem_nhds hp)).mono (fun _ h _ => h)
  have hgood : ∀ᶠ q in 𝓝 (p₀, x₀), ContDiffAt ℝ 1 Q q ∧
      (q.1, Q q) ∈ V ∧ (∀ i, x₀ i ≠ 0 → 0 < Q q i) ∧
        f (q.1, Q q) = f (p₀, x₀) := by
    filter_upwards [hQcd.eventually (by norm_num), hQV, hQpos, hQeq] with q h1 h2 h3 h4
    exact ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4⟩
  obtain ⟨W, hWgood, hWopen, hW₀⟩ := mem_nhds_iff.mp hgood
  let d : ι → ℝ := fun i => if x₀ i = 0 then 1 else 0
  have ht : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => (p₀, x₀ + t • d)) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 (p₀, x₀)) := by
    have hc : Continuous (fun t : ℝ => (p₀, x₀ + t • d)) := by fun_prop
    simpa using hc.tendsto 0
  -- … (truncated)

blocks.tex:
Let $D$ be the linear subspace of vectors vanishing on the zero coordinates
of $x_0$. The restriction $D_xf(p_0,x_0)|_D$ is onto. Since $F$ is finite
dimensional, choose a continuous linear right inverse $R$ taking values in
$D$. Apply \cref{lem:discrete_parametric_correction} with this $R$.

Let $d_i=1$ on the zero coordinates of $x_0$ and $d_i=0$ elsewhere.
Because $Q(p,x)-x\in D$, the zero-coordinate readouts of
$Q(p,x_0+\varepsilon d)$ are exactly $\varepsilon$, for every $p$.
At the other coordinates $Q(p_0,x_0)=x_0$ is strictly positive.
Continuity and the openness of $V$ therefore allow a fixed sufficiently
small $\varepsilon>0$ for which $Q(p_0,x_0+\varepsilon d)$ is positive
and lies in $V$ with its parameter. Choose the neighborhood small enough
that the correction equation, these inequalities, and the $C^1$ property
all hold. Taking its slice at $x_0+\varepsilon d$ gives the desired
$s(p)=Q(p,x_0+\varepsilon d)$ on an open neighborhood of $p_0$.

blocks.label: lem:discrete_joint_smoothness
blocks.title: Joint smoothness inside the strict walls
blocks.body:
The turning angles, headings, labelled vertices and closure controller
\[
 G(\kappa,\ell)=(E(\kappa,\ell),T(\kappa,\ell)-2\pi)
\]
are smooth jointly in the curvature and length vectors whenever
$|\kappa_i\ell_{i-1}/2|<1$ and $|\kappa_i\ell_i/2|<1$ at every index.
Zero lengths are permitted in this assertion. The length partial
derivative of $G$ equals the derivative of the native length-only map.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.contDiffAt_closureMapR3_joint
lean.code:
theorem contDiffAt_closureMapR3_joint
    (hw : ∀ i, |κ i * (ℓ (i - 1) / 2)| < 1 ∧ |κ i * (ℓ i / 2)| < 1) :
    ContDiffAt ℝ r closureMapR3 (κ, ℓ) := by
  have ht : ContDiffAt ℝ r (fun p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ) =>
      turningSum p.1 p.2) (κ, ℓ) := by
    unfold turningSum
    exact ContDiffAt.sum fun i _ => contDiffAt_turningAngle_joint _ (hw i).1 (hw i).2
  exact (contDiffAt_vertexR2_joint n hw).prodMk (ht.sub contDiffAt_const)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.contDiffAt_turningAngle_joint
lean.code:
theorem contDiffAt_turningAngle_joint (i : ZMod n)
    (hw₁ : |κ i * (ℓ (i - 1) / 2)| < 1)
    (hw₂ : |κ i * (ℓ i / 2)| < 1) :
    ContDiffAt ℝ r (fun p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ) =>
      turningAngle 0 p.1 p.2 i) (κ, ℓ) := by
  rw [abs_lt] at hw₁ hw₂
  have h₁ : ContDiffAt ℝ r
      (fun p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ) => p.1 i * (p.2 (i - 1) / 2))
      (κ, ℓ) := by fun_prop
  have h₂ : ContDiffAt ℝ r
      (fun p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ) => p.1 i * (p.2 i / 2))
      (κ, ℓ) := by fun_prop
  simpa only [Function.comp_apply, turningAngle, tK_zero] using
    ((Real.contDiffAt_arcsin (ne_of_gt hw₁.1) (ne_of_lt hw₁.2)).comp (κ, ℓ) h₁).add
      ((Real.contDiffAt_arcsin (ne_of_gt hw₂.1) (ne_of_lt hw₂.2)).comp (κ, ℓ) h₂)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.fderiv_closureMapR3_inr
lean.code:
theorem fderiv_closureMapR3_inr
    (hw : ∀ i, |κ i * (ℓ (i - 1) / 2)| < 1 ∧ |κ i * (ℓ i / 2)| < 1) :
    fderiv ℝ closureMapR3 (κ, ℓ) ∘L
        ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ (ZMod n → ℝ) (ZMod n → ℝ) =
      fderiv ℝ (fun L => closureMapR3 (κ, L)) ℓ := by
  have hf := (contDiffAt_closureMapR3_joint (r := 1) hw).hasStrictFDerivAt one_ne_zero
  have hi : HasFDerivAt (fun L : ZMod n → ℝ => (κ, L))
      (ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ (ZMod n → ℝ) (ZMod n → ℝ)) ℓ := by
    rw [show ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ (ZMod n → ℝ) (ZMod n → ℝ) =
        (0 : (ZMod n → ℝ) →L[ℝ] (ZMod n → ℝ)).prod
          (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (ZMod n → ℝ)) by ext L <;> rfl]
    exact (hasFDerivAt_const κ ℓ).prodMk (hasFDerivAt_id ℓ)
  exact (hf.hasFDerivAt.comp ℓ hi).fderiv.symm

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.contDiffAt_polygonR2_joint
lean.code:
theorem contDiffAt_polygonR2_joint
    (hw : ∀ i, |κ i * (ℓ (i - 1) / 2)| < 1 ∧ |κ i * (ℓ i / 2)| < 1) :
    ContDiffAt ℝ r (fun p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ) => polygonR2 p.1 p.2)
      (κ, ℓ) :=
  contDiffAt_pi.mpr fun i => contDiffAt_vertexR2_joint i.val hw

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.contDiffAt_vertexR2_joint
lean.code:
theorem contDiffAt_vertexR2_joint (j : ℕ)
    (hw : ∀ i, |κ i * (ℓ (i - 1) / 2)| < 1 ∧ |κ i * (ℓ i / 2)| < 1) :
    ContDiffAt ℝ r (fun p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ) => vertexR2 p.1 p.2 j)
      (κ, ℓ) := by
  unfold vertexR2
  apply ContDiffAt.sum
  intro k _
  have hl : ContDiffAt ℝ r (fun p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ) =>
      (p.2 (k : ZMod n) : ℂ)) (κ, ℓ) :=
    Complex.ofRealCLM.contDiff.contDiffAt.comp (κ, ℓ) (by fun_prop)
  have hh : ContDiffAt ℝ r (fun p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ) =>
      (heading p.1 p.2 k : ℂ)) (κ, ℓ) :=
    Complex.ofRealCLM.contDiff.contDiffAt.comp (κ, ℓ) (contDiffAt_heading_joint k hw)
  exact hl.mul ((hh.mul contDiffAt_const).cexp)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.contDiffAt_heading_joint
lean.code:
theorem contDiffAt_heading_joint (j : ℕ)
    (hw : ∀ i, |κ i * (ℓ (i - 1) / 2)| < 1 ∧ |κ i * (ℓ i / 2)| < 1) :
    ContDiffAt ℝ r (fun p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ) => heading p.1 p.2 j)
      (κ, ℓ) := by
  unfold heading
  exact ContDiffAt.sum fun i _ => contDiffAt_turningAngle_joint _ (hw _).1 (hw _).2

blocks.tex:
The maps are finite sums and compositions of coordinate maps,
products, complex exponentials and arcsines. The strict walls keep the
arcsine arguments away from $-1$ and $1$. The chain rule for
$\ell\mapsto(\kappa,\ell)$ identifies the partial derivative.

blocks.label: def:discrete_local_family
blocks.title: A local coherent realization family
blocks.body:
A local family at $\kappa_0$ consists of an open neighborhood
$U\subseteq\RR^n$ containing $\kappa_0$ and a $C^1$ length map
$\ell\colon U\to\RR^n$ such that every $\kappa\in U$ is positive,
$\operatorname{ModerateArc}(0,\kappa,\ell(\kappa))$ holds,
$E(\kappa,\ell(\kappa))=0$, $T(\kappa,\ell(\kappa))=2\pi$,
and the developed polygon is simple. The same developed labelled vertex
tuple depends $C^1$ on $\kappa$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.LocalDiscreteRealizationFamily
lean.code:
structure LocalDiscreteRealizationFamily (κ₀ : ZMod n → ℝ) where
  neighborhood : Set (ZMod n → ℝ)
  isOpen_neighborhood : IsOpen neighborhood
  base_mem : κ₀ ∈ neighborhood
  lengths : (ZMod n → ℝ) → (ZMod n → ℝ)
  contDiffOn_lengths : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 lengths neighborhood
  positive : ∀ κ ∈ neighborhood, ∀ i, 0 < κ i
  moderate : ∀ κ ∈ neighborhood, ModerateArc 0 κ (lengths κ)
  closure : ∀ κ ∈ neighborhood, closureGap κ (lengths κ) = 0
  fullTurn : ∀ κ ∈ neighborhood, turningSum κ (lengths κ) = 2 * Real.pi
  simple : ∀ κ ∈ neighborhood, IsSimplePolygon (polygonR2 κ (lengths κ))
  contDiffOn_vertices : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (fun κ => polygonR2 κ (lengths κ)) neighborhood

namespace LocalDiscreteRealizationFamily

variable {κ₀ : ZMod n → ℝ} (S : LocalDiscreteRealizationFamily κ₀)

blocks.label: thm:tabachnikov_local_continuity
blocks.title: Local coherent choice at every nonconstant admissible profile
blocks.body:
Let $n\ge4$ and let $\kappa_0$ satisfy
$\operatorname{DiscreteFourVertexPos}(\kappa_0)$ and be nonconstant.
Then there is a local coherent realization family at $\kappa_0$.
Equivalently, positivity and any strict four-vertex window suffice;
there is no regularity hypothesis on the profile, and adjacent equal
readings are permitted.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.tabachnikovProblem2_local_continuity
lean.code:
theorem tabachnikovProblem2_local_continuity (_hn : 4 ≤ n)
    {κ₀ : ZMod n → ℝ} (hκ₀ : DiscreteFourVertexPos κ₀)
    (hnonconstant : ¬ ∃ c, ∀ i, κ₀ i = c) :
    Nonempty (LocalDiscreteRealizationFamily κ₀) := by
  obtain ⟨hp, hc | ⟨c, _, hd⟩⟩ := hκ₀
  · exact (hnonconstant hc).elim
  · exact localContinuousRealization_of_dfv hp hd

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.nonempty_localDiscreteRealizationFamily
lean.code:
theorem RegularFourAnchor.nonempty_localDiscreteRealizationFamily
    {κ₀ : ZMod n → ℝ} (A : RegularFourAnchor κ₀) (hκ₀ : ∀ i, 0 < κ₀ i) :
    Nonempty (LocalDiscreteRealizationFamily κ₀) := by
  have hb := A.frame.lengths_nonneg_lt_edgeCap κ₀ A.halfLengths hκ₀
    A.positive A.start_lt A.finish_lt
  have hzero : closureMapR3 (κ₀, A.frame.lengths A.halfLengths) = 0 := by
    unfold closureMapR3
    rw [A.frame.closureGap_eq_controller, A.frame.turningSum_eq_controller, A.zero]
    simp
  have h01 := A.frame.strictMono (show (0 : Fin 4) < 1 by decide)
  have h12 := A.frame.strictMono (show (1 : Fin 4) < 2 by decide)
  have h23 := A.frame.strictMono (show (2 : Fin 4) < 3 by decide)
  have h3n := A.frame.lt_n 3
  exact nonempty_localDiscreteRealizationFamily_of_active_surjective (by omega)
    hκ₀ hb hzero (A.frame.active_surj_of_controller_regular hκ₀ A.positive hb A.zero A.regular)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.localContinuousRealization_of_dfv
lean.code:
theorem localContinuousRealization_of_dfv
    {κ₀ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ} (hκ₀ : ∀ i, 0 < κ₀ i) (hdfv : DFV κ₀ c) :
    Nonempty (LocalDiscreteRealizationFamily κ₀) := by
  obtain ⟨A⟩ := nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_dfv hκ₀ hdfv
  exact A.nonempty_localDiscreteRealizationFamily hκ₀

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.nonempty_localDiscreteRealizationFamily_of_active_surjective
lean.code:
theorem nonempty_localDiscreteRealizationFamily_of_active_surjective
    (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ₀ ℓ₀ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (hκ₀ : ∀ i, 0 < κ₀ i)
    (hℓ₀ : ∀ i, 0 ≤ ℓ₀ i ∧ ℓ₀ i < edgeCap κ₀ i)
    (hzero : closureMapR3 (κ₀, ℓ₀) = 0)
    (hactive : ∀ y : ℂ × ℝ, ∃ b : ZMod n → ℝ,
      fderiv ℝ (fun L => closureMapR3 (κ₀, L)) ℓ₀ b = y ∧
        ∀ i, ℓ₀ i = 0 → b i = 0) :
    Nonempty (LocalDiscreteRealizationFamily κ₀) := by
  let V : Set ((ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ)) :=
    {p | ∀ i, 0 < p.1 i ∧
      |p.1 i * (p.2 (i - 1) / 2)| < 1 ∧ |p.1 i * (p.2 i / 2)| < 1}
  have hV : IsOpen V := by
    have hVe : V = ⋂ i : ZMod n, {p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ) |
      0 < p.1 i ∧ |p.1 i * (p.2 (i - 1) / 2)| < 1 ∧
        |p.1 i * (p.2 i / 2)| < 1} := by ext p; simp [V]
    rw [hVe]
    apply isOpen_iInter_of_finite
    intro i
    have hk : Continuous (fun p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ) => p.1 i) := by fun_prop
    have hl : Continuous (fun p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ) =>
        |p.1 i * (p.2 (i - 1) / 2)|) := by fun_prop
    have hr : Continuous (fun p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ) =>
        |p.1 i * (p.2 i / 2)|) := by fun_prop
    exact (isOpen_lt continuous_const hk).inter
      ((isOpen_lt hl continuous_const).inter (isOpen_lt hr continuous_const))
  have hw := strict_arc_walls_of_nonneg_lt_edgeCap hκ₀ hℓ₀
  have hpartial := fderiv_closureMapR3_inr hw
  obtain ⟨U, s, hUopen, hU₀, hscd, hgood⟩ :=
    (contDiffAt_closureMapR3_joint (r := 1) hw).exists_localSection_pos_of_active_surjective
      (fun i => (hℓ₀ i).1) (by simpa only [hpartial] using hactive) hV
      (fun i => ⟨hκ₀ i, hw i⟩)
  have hpos : ∀ κ ∈ U, ∀ i, 0 < κ i := fun κ hκ i => (hgood κ hκ).1 i |>.1
  have hmod : ∀ κ ∈ U, ModerateArc 0 κ (s κ) := by
    intro κ hκ
    apply moderateArc_zero_iff.mpr
    intro i
    have hi := (hgood κ hκ).1 i
    have hl := (hgood κ hκ).2.1
    refine ⟨hl i, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simpa only [abs_mul, abs_of_pos (half_pos (hl (i - 1)))] using hi.2.1
    · simpa only [abs_mul, abs_of_pos (half_pos (hl i))] using hi.2.2
  have heq : ∀ κ ∈ U, closureMapR3 (κ, s κ) = 0 :=
    fun κ hκ => (hgood κ hκ).2.2.trans hzero
  have hclose : ∀ κ ∈ U, closureGap κ (s κ) = 0 :=
    fun κ hκ => congrArg Prod.fst (heq κ hκ)
  have hturn : ∀ κ ∈ U, turningSum κ (s κ) = 2 * Real.pi := by
    intro κ hκ
    have ht := congrArg Prod.snd (heq κ hκ)
    exact sub_eq_zero.mp ht
  refine ⟨⟨U, hUopen, hU₀, s, hscd, hpos, hmod, hclose, hturn,
    fun κ hκ => isSimplePolygon_of_turningPositive hn (hmod κ hκ) (hpos κ hκ)
      (hclose κ hκ) (hturn κ hκ), ?_⟩⟩
  intro κ hκ
  exact (contDiffAt_polygonR2_joint (fun i => ((hgood κ hκ).1 i).2)).comp_contDiffWithinAt κ
    (contDiffWithinAt_id.prodMk (hscd κ hκ))

blocks.tex:
The nonconstant hypothesis selects the strict-DFV branch. The anchor
producer from \cref{chap:discrete_four_active} supplies a regular
four-edge anchor $\ell_0$ for this literal profile. The full ambient
controller vanishes at $(\kappa_0,\ell_0)$. Its length derivative is
onto using directions supported on the four positive edges: the
four-coordinate controller and ambient controller differ, at a zero,
by an invertible output scaling and rotation.

Apply \cref{thm:discrete_positive_section} to $G$, taking $V$ to impose
positive curvature and both strict arcsine walls, but not positivity of
lengths. This is open and contains the anchor. The resulting length
section is strictly positive and has $G=0$, so moderate arcs, exact
closure and the real full turn hold for the same section. The existing
positive-turning convexity theorem supplies simplicity. Joint smoothness
of reconstruction and the chain rule give $C^1$ dependence of the vertices.
The combinatorial selection of a frame occurs only at $\kappa_0$;
nearby profiles are treated by this one correction map, even if their
peak orderings or adjacent equalities change.

chapters.title: Topology interfaces imported by the discrete book

blocks.tex:
This is a partial catalog of existing interfaces in
\texttt{ForMathlib/Analysis/Complex/WindingNumber.lean},
\texttt{ForMathlib/Analysis/Complex/PoincareMiranda.lean}, and
\texttt{Gluck/Winding.lean}.  The statements and sketches below were read
from those project sources.  In particular the \texttt{Complex} names below
belong to the project's \texttt{ForMathlib} library, not an asserted upstream
Mathlib API.  This catalog neither replaces their full smooth-book chapters
nor certifies compilation.  It contains no new producer for the discrete
converse.  All labels are local to the discrete book.

Put $I=[0,1]$ and write $C(I,X)$ for bundled continuous maps.
Private normalization and covering-lift helpers are described inside the
sketches; only the listed public interfaces are pinned here.

blocks.label: def:discrete_import_winding_at
blocks.title: Winding about an avoided point
blocks.body:
For $w\in\mathbb C$, $\gamma\in C(I,\mathbb C)$, and a proof that
$\gamma(t)\ne w$ for every $t$, radially normalize $\gamma-w$ to the unit
circle.  Lift that path along $\operatorname{Circle.exp}$ to a continuous
real angle $\phi$, using the chosen initial preimage.  Define
$W_w(\gamma)=(\phi(1)-\phi(0))/(2\pi)$.
The definition allows open paths; it does not assume $\gamma(0)=\gamma(1)$.

lean.name: Complex.windingNumberAt
lean.code:
noncomputable def windingNumberAt (w : ℂ) (γ : C(I, ℂ)) (hγ : ∀ t, γ t ≠ w) : ℝ :=
  windingNumber (normLoopAt w γ hγ)

blocks.label: lem:discrete_import_winding_congr
blocks.title: Pointwise congruence
blocks.body:
Pointwise equal continuous paths avoiding the same $w$ have equal $W_w$,
regardless of the proofs of avoidance used in the definition.

lean.name: Complex.windingNumberAt_congr
lean.code:
theorem windingNumberAt_congr {w : ℂ} {γ γ' : C(I, ℂ)} {hγ : ∀ t, γ t ≠ w}
    {hγ' : ∀ t, γ' t ≠ w} (he : ∀ t, γ t = γ' t) :
    windingNumberAt w γ hγ = windingNumberAt w γ' hγ' := by
  obtain rfl : γ = γ' := ContinuousMap.ext he
  rfl

blocks.tex:
Continuous-map extensionality identifies the paths; proof irrelevance
identifies their avoidance arguments.

blocks.label: lem:discrete_import_winding_lift
blocks.title: Evaluation from a polar lift
blocks.body:
If $\phi\in C(I,\mathbb R)$ and
$\gamma(t)-w=\|\gamma(t)-w\|e^{i\phi(t)}$ for every $t$, with
$\gamma(t)\ne w$, then $W_w(\gamma)=(\phi(1)-\phi(0))/(2\pi)$.

lean.name: Complex.windingNumberAt_eq_div_of_lift
lean.code:
theorem windingNumberAt_eq_div_of_lift {w : ℂ} {γ : C(I, ℂ)} (hγ : ∀ t, γ t ≠ w) (φ : C(I, ℝ))
    (hφ : ∀ t, γ t - w = ‖γ t - w‖ * exp (φ t * Complex.I)) :
    windingNumberAt w γ hγ = (φ 1 - φ 0) / (2 * π) := by
  refine windingNumber_eq_div_of_lift _ φ fun t ↦ ?_
  apply Subtype.ext
  rw [Circle.coe_exp]
  change exp ((φ t : ℂ) * Complex.I) = (γ t - w) / (‖γ t - w‖ : ℂ)
  rw [eq_div_iff (by exact_mod_cast norm_ne_zero_iff.2 (sub_ne_zero.2 (hγ t)))]
  linear_combination -hφ t

/-- A constant curve has winding number `0` about any point it avoids. -/
@[simp]

blocks.tex:
Divide the polar identity by its nonzero norm.  This makes $\phi$ a lift of
the normalized path.  Two lifts differ by a constant multiple of $2\pi$,
so their endpoint increments agree.

blocks.label: lem:discrete_import_winding_const
blocks.title: Constant paths
blocks.body: For $z\ne w$, the constant path with value $z$ has $W_w=0$.

lean.name: Complex.windingNumberAt_const
lean.code:
theorem windingNumberAt_const (w z : ℂ) (h : ∀ t : I, (ContinuousMap.const I z) t ≠ w) :
    windingNumberAt w (ContinuousMap.const I z) h = 0 := by
  have hnl : normLoopAt w (ContinuousMap.const I z) h
      = ContinuousMap.const I (circleProjAt w z (h 0)) :=
    ContinuousMap.ext fun t ↦ circleProjAt_congr (h t) (h 0) rfl
  rw [windingNumberAt, hnl, windingNumber_const]

blocks.tex: Its normalized path has a constant angle lift, hence zero increment.

blocks.label: thm:discrete_import_winding_homotopy
blocks.title: Free homotopy through avoiding loops
blocks.body:
Let $\gamma_0,\gamma_1\in C(I,\mathbb C)$ avoid $w$.  Let
$H\in C(I\times I,\mathbb C)$ avoid $w$ everywhere, with
$H(0,t)=\gamma_0(t)$, $H(1,t)=\gamma_1(t)$, and
$H(s,0)=H(s,1)$ for all $s$.  Then $W_w(\gamma_0)=W_w(\gamma_1)$.
No common fixed base point of the loops is required.

lean.name: Complex.windingNumberAt_eq_of_homotopy
lean.code:
theorem windingNumberAt_eq_of_homotopy (w : ℂ) (γ₀ γ₁ : C(I, ℂ))
    (hγ₀ : ∀ t, γ₀ t ≠ w) (hγ₁ : ∀ t, γ₁ t ≠ w)
    (H : C(I × I, ℂ)) (hH : ∀ st, H st ≠ w)
    (h0 : ∀ t, H (0, t) = γ₀ t) (h1 : ∀ t, H (1, t) = γ₁ t)
    (hloop : ∀ s, H (s, 0) = H (s, 1)) :
    windingNumberAt w γ₀ hγ₀ = windingNumberAt w γ₁ hγ₁ := by
  set Hn : C(I × I, Circle) :=
    ⟨fun st ↦ circleProjAt w (H st) (hH st),
      continuous_circleProjAt H.continuous hH⟩ with hHndef
  have h0' : ∀ t : I, Hn (0, t) = normLoopAt w γ₀ hγ₀ t := by
    intro t
    change circleProjAt w (H (0, t)) (hH (0, t)) =
      circleProjAt w (γ₀ t) (hγ₀ t)
    exact circleProjAt_congr _ _ (h0 t)
  have h1' : ∀ t : I, Hn (1, t) = normLoopAt w γ₁ hγ₁ t := by
    intro t
    change circleProjAt w (H (1, t)) (hH (1, t)) =
      circleProjAt w (γ₁ t) (hγ₁ t)
    exact circleProjAt_congr _ _ (h1 t)
  have hloop' : ∀ s : I, Hn (s, 0) = Hn (s, 1) := by
    intro s
    change circleProjAt w (H (s, 0)) (hH (s, 0)) =
      circleProjAt w (H (s, 1)) (hH (s, 1))
    exact circleProjAt_congr _ _ (hloop s)
  exact windingNumber_eq_of_homotopy Hn h0' h1' hloop'

blocks.tex:
Radially normalize the whole homotopy and lift it along the circle
covering.  The endpoint increment divided by $2\pi$ varies continuously
with $s$ and is integer-valued because every row is closed.  It is constant
on the connected interval.  Lift uniqueness identifies the endpoint values
with the winding numbers in the statement.

blocks.label: lem:discrete_import_winding_mul
blocks.title: Product of nonvanishing paths
blocks.body:
For paths $\gamma,\gamma'$ avoiding zero,
$W_0(\gamma\gamma')=W_0(\gamma)+W_0(\gamma')$.

lean.name: Complex.windingNumberAt_mul
lean.code:
theorem windingNumberAt_mul (γ γ' : C(I, ℂ)) (hγ : ∀ t, γ t ≠ 0) (hγ' : ∀ t, γ' t ≠ 0) :
    windingNumberAt 0 (γ * γ') (fun t ↦ mul_ne_zero (hγ t) (hγ' t))
      = windingNumberAt 0 γ hγ + windingNumberAt 0 γ' hγ' := by
  have hnl : normLoopAt 0 (γ * γ') (fun t ↦ mul_ne_zero (hγ t) (hγ' t))
      = normLoopAt 0 γ hγ * normLoopAt 0 γ' hγ' :=
    ContinuousMap.ext fun t ↦ circleProjAt_zero_mul (hγ t) (hγ' t)
  rw [windingNumberAt, hnl, windingNumber_mul, windingNumberAt, windingNumberAt]

blocks.tex:
Radial normalization commutes with multiplication, and the sum of two
angle lifts lifts the product.  Endpoint increments add.

blocks.label: lem:discrete_import_winding_const_mul
blocks.title: Constant complex scaling
blocks.body: For $c\ne0$ and a path $\gamma$ avoiding zero, $W_0(c\gamma)=W_0(\gamma)$.

lean.name: Complex.windingNumberAt_const_mul
lean.code:
theorem windingNumberAt_const_mul (c : ℂ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (γ : C(I, ℂ)) (hγ : ∀ t, γ t ≠ 0) :
    windingNumberAt 0 (ContinuousMap.const I c * γ) (fun t ↦ mul_ne_zero hc (hγ t))
      = windingNumberAt 0 γ hγ := by
  have h := windingNumberAt_mul (ContinuousMap.const I c) γ (fun _ ↦ hc) hγ
  rw [windingNumberAt_const 0 c fun _ ↦ hc, zero_add] at h
  exact h

/-! ### The continuous Rouché theorem ("dog-on-a-leash") -/

blocks.tex: Apply product additivity and the zero winding of the constant path $c$.

blocks.label: lem:discrete_import_winding_exp_int
blocks.title: Integer exponential loop
blocks.body:
For every integer $k$, the path $t\mapsto e^{2\pi i k t}$ avoids zero
and has $W_0=k$.

lean.name: Complex.windingNumberAt_exp_int_mul
lean.code:
theorem windingNumberAt_exp_int_mul (n : ℤ) :
    windingNumberAt 0
      ⟨fun t : I ↦ exp ((2 * π * n * t : ℝ) * Complex.I), by fun_prop⟩
      (fun _ ↦ exp_ne_zero _) = n := by
  rw [windingNumberAt_eq_div_of_lift (fun _ ↦ exp_ne_zero _)
    ⟨fun t : I ↦ 2 * π * n * t, by fun_prop⟩ fun t ↦ by
      change exp ((2 * π * n * t : ℝ) * Complex.I) - 0
        = (‖exp (((2 * π * n * t : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) - 0‖ : ℂ)
          * exp (((2 * π * n * t : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
      rw [sub_zero, norm_exp_ofReal_mul_I, ofReal_one, one_mul]]
  have h2pi : (2 * π : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by positivity
  change (2 * π * n * ((1 : I) : ℝ) - 2 * π * n * ((0 : I) : ℝ)) / (2 * π) = n
  rw [Set.Icc.coe_one, Set.Icc.coe_zero, mul_one, mul_zero, sub_zero,
    mul_div_cancel_left₀ _ h2pi]

/-! ### The planar degree existence principle -/

blocks.tex:
Use the explicit real lift $2\pi kt$ and its unit modulus, then evaluate
the endpoint increment.

blocks.label: thm:discrete_import_winding_perturb
blocks.title: Symmetric perturbation criterion
blocks.body:
For closed continuous paths $\gamma,\gamma'$ and $w\in\mathbb C$, assume
$\|\gamma'(t)-\gamma(t)\|<\|\gamma(t)-w\|+\|\gamma'(t)-w\|$
at every $t$.  Both paths avoid $w$, and $W_w(\gamma)=W_w(\gamma')$.

lean.name: Complex.windingNumberAt_eq_of_norm_sub_lt
lean.code:
theorem windingNumberAt_eq_of_norm_sub_lt (w : ℂ) (γ γ' : C(I, ℂ))
    (hloopγ : γ 0 = γ 1) (hloopγ' : γ' 0 = γ' 1)
    (hpert : ∀ t, ‖γ' t - γ t‖ < ‖γ t - w‖ + ‖γ' t - w‖) :
    windingNumberAt w γ (ne_of_norm_sub_lt_left hpert) =
      windingNumberAt w γ' (ne_of_norm_sub_lt_right hpert) := by
  have hγ : ∀ t, γ t ≠ w := ne_of_norm_sub_lt_left hpert
  have hγ' : ∀ t, γ' t ≠ w := ne_of_norm_sub_lt_right hpert
  set Hc : I × I → ℂ := fun st ↦ γ st.2 + (st.1 : ℝ) • (γ' st.2 - γ st.2) with hHcdef
  have hHccont : Continuous Hc := by
    rw [hHcdef]
    exact (γ.continuous.comp continuous_snd).add
      ((continuous_subtype_val.comp continuous_fst).smul
        ((γ'.continuous.comp continuous_snd).sub (γ.continuous.comp continuous_snd)))
  have hHcne : ∀ st : I × I, Hc st ≠ w := by
    intro st
    have hs0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (st.1 : ℝ) := st.1.2.1
    have hs1 : (st.1 : ℝ) ≤ 1 := st.1.2.2
    have hkey : Hc st - w =
        (γ st.2 - w) + (st.1 : ℝ) • ((γ' st.2 - w) - (γ st.2 - w)) := by
      simp only [hHcdef]
      rw [sub_sub_sub_cancel_right]
      abel
    have hpert' : ‖(γ st.2 - w) - (γ' st.2 - w)‖ < ‖γ st.2 - w‖ + ‖γ' st.2 - w‖ := by
      have he : (γ st.2 - w) - (γ' st.2 - w) = γ st.2 - γ' st.2 := by ring
      rw [he, norm_sub_rev]
      exact hpert st.2
    intro hcon
    apply segment_ne_zero hpert' hs0 hs1
    rw [← hkey, hcon, sub_self]
  set H : C(I × I, Circle) :=
    ⟨fun st ↦ circleProjAt w (Hc st) (hHcne st), continuous_circleProjAt hHccont hHcne⟩
  have h0 : ∀ t : I, H (0, t) = normLoopAt w γ hγ t := by
    intro t
    change circleProjAt w (Hc (0, t)) (hHcne (0, t)) = circleProjAt w (γ t) (hγ t)
    apply circleProjAt_congr
    change γ t + ((0 : I) : ℝ) • (γ' t - γ t) = γ t
    rw [Set.Icc.coe_zero, zero_smul, add_zero]
  have h1 : ∀ t : I, H (1, t) = normLoopAt w γ' hγ' t := by
    intro t
    change circleProjAt w (Hc (1, t)) (hHcne (1, t)) = circleProjAt w (γ' t) (hγ' t)
    apply circleProjAt_congr
    change γ t + ((1 : I) : ℝ) • (γ' t - γ t) = γ' t
    rw [Set.Icc.coe_one, one_smul, add_sub_cancel]
  have hloop : ∀ s : I, H (s, 0) = H (s, 1) := by
    intro s
    change circleProjAt w (Hc (s, 0)) (hHcne (s, 0)) = circleProjAt w (Hc (s, 1)) (hHcne (s, 1))
    apply circleProjAt_congr
    change γ (0 : I) + (s : ℝ) • (γ' (0 : I) - γ (0 : I))
      = γ (1 : I) + (s : ℝ) • (γ' (1 : I) - γ (1 : I))
    rw [hloopγ, hloopγ']
  have hinv := windingNumber_eq_of_homotopy H h0 h1 hloop
  rw [windingNumberAt, windingNumberAt, hinv]

/-! ### The boundary loop of a circle -/

blocks.tex:
If either endpoint were $w$, the strict inequality would fail.  If a point
of the segment joining their translated values were zero, the segment
equation would imply equality in this triangle inequality.  Thus the
straight-line homotopy avoids $w$ and remains a homotopy of loops.  Apply
the normalized-loop homotopy argument of the preceding theorem.

blocks.label: def:discrete_import_circle_loop
blocks.title: Circle boundary path
blocks.body:
For $c\in\mathbb C$, $R\in\mathbb R$, and $F$ continuous on
the sphere of center $c$ and radius $|R|$, define the bundled path
$t\mapsto F(c+R e^{2\pi it})$ on $I$.

lean.name: Complex.circleLoop
lean.code:
noncomputable def circleLoop (F : ℂ → ℂ) (c : ℂ) (R : ℝ)
    (hF : ContinuousOn F (sphere c |R|)) : C(I, ℂ) :=
  ⟨fun t ↦ F (circleMap c R (2 * π * t)), by
    apply hF.comp_continuous
    · exact (continuous_circleMap c R).comp (continuous_const.mul continuous_subtype_val)
    · exact fun t ↦ circleMap_mem_sphere' c R _⟩

/-- Evaluation of the boundary loop: `circleLoop F c R hF t = F (circleMap c R (2 * π * t))`. -/
@[simp]

blocks.label: lem:discrete_import_winding_circle
blocks.title: The positively oriented circle
blocks.body:
For $R>0$, the circle boundary path of the identity with center $c$ and
radius $R$ avoids $c$ and has winding $1$ about $c$.

lean.name: Complex.windingNumberAt_circleLoop_id
lean.code:
theorem windingNumberAt_circleLoop_id (c : ℂ) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) :
    windingNumberAt c (circleLoop id c R continuous_id.continuousOn)
      (circleLoop_id_ne c hR.ne') = 1 := by
  have hlift : ∀ t : I,
      Circle.exp ((⟨fun t : I ↦ 2 * π * (t : ℝ), by fun_prop⟩ : C(I, ℝ)) t) =
        normLoopAt c (circleLoop id c R continuous_id.continuousOn)
          (circleLoop_id_ne c hR.ne') t := by
    intro t
    have hsub : circleLoop id c R continuous_id.continuousOn t - c =
        (R : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((2 * π * (t : ℝ) : ℝ) * Complex.I) := by
      change circleMap c R (2 * π * (t : ℝ)) - c = _
      rw [circleMap, add_sub_cancel_left]
    have hnorm : ‖circleLoop id c R continuous_id.continuousOn t - c‖ = R := by
      rw [hsub, norm_mul, norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos hR,
        norm_exp_ofReal_mul_I, mul_one]
    apply Subtype.ext
    rw [Circle.coe_exp]
    change Complex.exp (((2 * π * (t : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) =
        (circleLoop id c R continuous_id.continuousOn t - c) /
          (‖circleLoop id c R continuous_id.continuousOn t - c‖ : ℂ)
    rw [hnorm, hsub, mul_div_cancel_left₀ _ (ofReal_ne_zero.2 hR.ne')]
  rw [windingNumberAt, windingNumber_eq_div_of_lift _ _ hlift]
  have h2pi : (2 * π : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by positivity
  change (2 * π * ((1 : I) : ℝ) - 2 * π * ((0 : I) : ℝ)) / (2 * π) = 1
  rw [Set.Icc.coe_one, Set.Icc.coe_zero, mul_one, mul_zero, sub_zero, div_self h2pi]

blocks.tex: Normalize $R e^{2\pi it}$ by its norm $R$ and use the lift $2\pi t$.

blocks.label: thm:discrete_import_degree
blocks.title: Nonzero boundary winding attains the avoided value
blocks.body:
Let $R>0$, let $F:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ be continuous on the closed
ball of center $c$ and radius $R$, and suppose $F(z)\ne w$ on its sphere.
If the circle boundary path of $F$ has nonzero winding about $w$, then
there exists $z$ in the open ball with $F(z)=w$.

lean.name: Complex.exists_eq_of_windingNumberAt_ne_zero
lean.code:
theorem exists_eq_of_windingNumberAt_ne_zero (F : ℂ → ℂ) (c : ℂ) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (w : ℂ)
    (hF : ContinuousOn F (closedBall c R)) (hbd : ∀ z ∈ sphere c R, F z ≠ w)
    (hw : windingNumberAt w
      (circleLoop F c R (hF.mono (sphere_subset_closedBall.trans
        (closedBall_subset_closedBall (abs_of_pos hR).le))))
      (circleLoop_ne F c R w _
        fun z hz ↦ hbd z (mem_sphere.2 ((mem_sphere.1 hz).trans (abs_of_pos hR)))) ≠ 0) :
    ∃ z ∈ ball c R, F z = w := by
  by_contra hcon
  simp only [not_exists, not_and] at hcon
  have hFs : ContinuousOn F (sphere c |R|) :=
    hF.mono (sphere_subset_closedBall.trans (closedBall_subset_closedBall (abs_of_pos hR).le))
  have hbd' : ∀ z ∈ sphere c |R|, F z ≠ w :=
    fun z hz ↦ hbd z (mem_sphere.2 ((mem_sphere.1 hz).trans (abs_of_pos hR)))
  have hne : ∀ z ∈ closedBall c R, F z ≠ w := by
    intro z hz
    rcases (mem_closedBall.1 hz).lt_or_eq with h | h
    · exact hcon z (mem_ball.2 h)
    · exact hbd z (mem_sphere.2 h)
  have hFc : F c ≠ w := hne c (mem_closedBall_self hR.le)
  set pt : I × I → ℂ := fun st ↦ c + ((st.1 : ℝ) : ℂ) * circleMap 0 R (2 * π * st.2)
    with hptdef
  have hptcont : Continuous pt := by
    rw [hptdef]
    exact continuous_const.add ((continuous_ofReal.comp
      (continuous_subtype_val.comp continuous_fst)).mul ((continuous_circleMap 0 R).comp
        (continuous_const.mul (continuous_subtype_val.comp continuous_snd))))
  have hptmem : ∀ st : I × I, pt st ∈ closedBall c R := by
    intro st
    have hnorm : ‖pt st - c‖ = (st.1 : ℝ) * R := by
      rw [hptdef]
      simp only [add_sub_cancel_left, norm_mul, norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs,
        norm_circleMap_zero, abs_of_nonneg st.1.2.1, abs_of_pos hR]
    rw [mem_closedBall, dist_eq_norm, hnorm]
    nlinarith [st.1.2.2, hR.le]
  have hFptcont : Continuous fun st ↦ F (pt st) := hF.comp_continuous hptcont hptmem
  have hFptne : ∀ st, F (pt st) ≠ w := fun st ↦ hne _ (hptmem st)
  set Hmap : C(I × I, Circle) :=
    ⟨fun st ↦ circleProjAt w (F (pt st)) (hFptne st), continuous_circleProjAt hFptcont hFptne⟩
  have h0 : ∀ t, Hmap (0, t) = (ContinuousMap.const I (circleProjAt w (F c) hFc)) t := by
    intro t
    change circleProjAt w (F (pt (0, t))) (hFptne (0, t)) = circleProjAt w (F c) hFc
    apply circleProjAt_congr
    have hpt0 : pt (0, t) = c := by simp [hptdef]
    rw [hpt0]
  have h1 : ∀ t, Hmap (1, t) =
      normLoopAt w (circleLoop F c R hFs) (circleLoop_ne F c R w hFs hbd') t := by
    intro t
    change circleProjAt w (F (pt (1, t))) (hFptne (1, t)) =
      circleProjAt w (circleLoop F c R hFs t) (circleLoop_ne F c R w hFs hbd' t)
    apply circleProjAt_congr
    change F (pt (1, t)) = F (circleMap c R (2 * π * t))
    congr 1
    simp [hptdef, circleMap]
  have hloop : ∀ s, Hmap (s, 0) = Hmap (s, 1) := by
    intro s
    change circleProjAt w (F (pt (s, 0))) (hFptne (s, 0)) =
      circleProjAt w (F (pt (s, 1))) (hFptne (s, 1))
    apply circleProjAt_congr
    have hpt : pt (s, 0) = pt (s, 1) := by
  -- … (truncated)

blocks.tex:
If there were no such interior point, the boundary hypothesis would make
$F-w$ nonzero on the entire closed ball.  The paths
$t\mapsto F(c+sR e^{2\pi it})$, $0\le s\le1$, form an avoiding free
homotopy of loops from the constant $F(c)$ to the boundary path.
The normalized-loop homotopy argument forces boundary winding zero.

blocks.label: def:discrete_winding_number_c
blocks.title: Origin-centered winding
blocks.body:
For $\gamma\in C(I,\mathbb C)$ avoiding zero, normalize by
$\gamma(t)/\|\gamma(t)\|$, take the chosen circle-covering angle lift,
and divide its endpoint increment by $2\pi$.  Write this as $W_C(\gamma)$.
The private bridge in \texttt{Gluck/Winding.lean} identifies it with
$W_0(\gamma)$ by the polar-lift evaluation rule.  Closedness is not a
hypothesis of this definition.

lean.name: Gluck.windingNumberC
lean.code:
noncomputable def windingNumberC (γ : C(I, ℂ)) (h : ∀ t, γ t ≠ 0) : ℝ :=
  windingNumber (normLoop γ h)

blocks.label: thm:discrete_winding_number_c_homotopy
blocks.title: Gluck free-homotopy interface
blocks.body:
For two nowhere-zero paths and a nowhere-zero $H\in C(I\times I,\mathbb C)$
with those paths as its $s=0,1$ endpoints and $H(s,0)=H(s,1)$ for every
$s$, their $W_C$ values agree.

lean.name: Gluck.windingNumberC_eq_of_homotopy
lean.code:
theorem windingNumberC_eq_of_homotopy (γ₀ γ₁ : C(I, ℂ))
    (hγ₀ : ∀ t, γ₀ t ≠ 0) (hγ₁ : ∀ t, γ₁ t ≠ 0)
    (H : C(I × I, ℂ)) (hH : ∀ st, H st ≠ 0)
    (h0 : ∀ t, H (0, t) = γ₀ t) (h1 : ∀ t, H (1, t) = γ₁ t)
    (hloop : ∀ s, H (s, 0) = H (s, 1)) :
    windingNumberC γ₀ hγ₀ = windingNumberC γ₁ hγ₁ := by
  rw [windingNumberC_eq_windingNumberAt, windingNumberC_eq_windingNumberAt]
  exact Complex.windingNumberAt_eq_of_homotopy 0 γ₀ γ₁ hγ₀ hγ₁ H hH h0 h1 hloop

/-! ## The boundary loop of a map on the closed unit disk -/

blocks.tex:
Apply the private bridge at both ends and the general free-homotopy theorem
with avoided point zero.

blocks.label: lem:discrete_winding_number_c_perturb
blocks.title: One-sided perturbation interface
blocks.body:
Let $\gamma,\gamma'$ be nowhere-zero continuous paths, both closed, and
suppose $\|\gamma'(t)-\gamma(t)\|<\|\gamma(t)\|$ for all $t$.
Then $W_C(\gamma)=W_C(\gamma')$.

lean.name: Gluck.windingNumberC_eq_of_perturb
lean.code:
theorem windingNumberC_eq_of_perturb (γ γ' : C(I, ℂ))
    (hγ : ∀ t, γ t ≠ 0) (hγ' : ∀ t, γ' t ≠ 0)
    (hloopγ : γ 0 = γ 1) (hloopγ' : γ' 0 = γ' 1)
    (hpert : ∀ t, ‖γ' t - γ t‖ < ‖γ t‖) :
    windingNumberC γ hγ = windingNumberC γ' hγ' := by
  rw [windingNumberC_eq_windingNumberAt, windingNumberC_eq_windingNumberAt]
  have hpert' : ∀ t, ‖γ' t - γ t‖ < ‖γ t - 0‖ + ‖γ' t - 0‖ := fun t => by
    rw [sub_zero, sub_zero]
    exact (hpert t).trans_le (le_add_of_nonneg_right (norm_nonneg _))
  exact Complex.windingNumberAt_eq_of_norm_sub_lt 0 γ γ' hloopγ hloopγ' hpert'

blocks.tex:
The one-sided bound implies the symmetric bound after adding the
nonnegative norm $\|\gamma'(t)\|$.  Use the private bridge and the symmetric
perturbation theorem at zero.  All four original nonvanishing and
closedness hypotheses are retained in this interface.

blocks.label: def:discrete_exp_loop
blocks.title: Forward exponential model
blocks.body:
For $c\in\mathbb C$, set $E_c(t)=c e^{2\pi it}$ as a bundled continuous
path.  Both endpoints equal $c$, and its norm is constantly $\|c\|$.

lean.name: Gluck.expLoop
lean.code:
noncomputable def expLoop (c : ℂ) : C(I, ℂ) :=
  ⟨fun t ↦ c * Complex.exp (((2 * π * (t : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I), by fun_prop⟩

@[simp]

blocks.label: def:discrete_exp_loop_rev
blocks.title: Reverse exponential model
blocks.body:
For $c\in\mathbb C$, set $E^-_c(t)=c e^{-2\pi it}$ as a bundled
continuous path.  Both endpoints equal $c$, and its norm is $\|c\|$.

lean.name: Gluck.expLoopRev
lean.code:
noncomputable def expLoopRev (c : ℂ) : C(I, ℂ) :=
  ⟨fun t ↦ c * Complex.exp (((-(2 * π * (t : ℝ)) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I), by fun_prop⟩

@[simp]

blocks.label: lem:discrete_winding_number_c_exp_loop
blocks.title: Forward model winding
blocks.body: For $c\ne0$, $E_c$ is nowhere zero and $W_C(E_c)=1$.

lean.name: Gluck.windingNumberC_expLoop
lean.code:
theorem windingNumberC_expLoop (c : ℂ) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    windingNumberC (expLoop c) (expLoop_ne_zero c hc) = 1 := by
  rw [windingNumberC_eq_windingNumberAt]
  let γ : C(I, ℂ) :=
    ⟨fun t ↦ Complex.exp ((2 * π * (1 : ℤ) * (t : ℝ) : ℝ) * Complex.I), by fun_prop⟩
  have hγ : ∀ t, γ t ≠ 0 := fun _ ↦ Complex.exp_ne_zero _
  calc
    Complex.windingNumberAt 0 (expLoop c) (expLoop_ne_zero c hc) =
        Complex.windingNumberAt 0
          ⟨fun t ↦ c * γ t, continuous_const.mul γ.continuous⟩
          (fun t ↦ mul_ne_zero hc (hγ t)) :=
      Complex.windingNumberAt_congr fun t ↦ by simp [γ, expLoop]
    _ = Complex.windingNumberAt 0 γ hγ :=
      Complex.windingNumberAt_const_mul c hc γ hγ
    _ = 1 := by simpa [γ] using Complex.windingNumberAt_exp_int_mul 1

blocks.tex:
Bridge to $W_0$, identify the path with $c$ times the integer exponential
path for $k=1$, remove the nonzero constant, and evaluate that winding.

blocks.label: lem:discrete_winding_number_c_exp_loop_rev
blocks.title: Reverse model winding
blocks.body: For $c\ne0$, $E^-_c$ is nowhere zero and $W_C(E^-_c)=-1$.

lean.name: Gluck.windingNumberC_expLoopRev
lean.code:
theorem windingNumberC_expLoopRev (c : ℂ) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    windingNumberC (expLoopRev c) (expLoopRev_ne_zero c hc) = -1 := by
  rw [windingNumberC_eq_windingNumberAt]
  let γ : C(I, ℂ) :=
    ⟨fun t ↦ Complex.exp ((2 * π * (-1 : ℤ) * (t : ℝ) : ℝ) * Complex.I), by fun_prop⟩
  have hγ : ∀ t, γ t ≠ 0 := fun _ ↦ Complex.exp_ne_zero _
  calc
    Complex.windingNumberAt 0 (expLoopRev c) (expLoopRev_ne_zero c hc) =
        Complex.windingNumberAt 0
          ⟨fun t ↦ c * γ t, continuous_const.mul γ.continuous⟩
          (fun t ↦ mul_ne_zero hc (hγ t)) :=
      Complex.windingNumberAt_congr fun t ↦ by simp [γ, expLoopRev]
    _ = Complex.windingNumberAt 0 γ hγ :=
      Complex.windingNumberAt_const_mul c hc γ hγ
    _ = -1 := by simpa [γ] using Complex.windingNumberAt_exp_int_mul (-1)

blocks.tex: Use the same constant-scaling computation with integer $k=-1$.

blocks.label: def:discrete_linear_loop
blocks.title: Real-linear boundary model
blocks.body:
For $a,b\in\mathbb C$, put $L_{a,b}(t)=E_a(t)+E^-_b(t)$.
This is the boundary path of $z\mapsto az+b\overline z$.

lean.name: Gluck.linearLoop
lean.code:
noncomputable def linearLoop (a b : ℂ) : C(I, ℂ) :=
  ⟨fun t ↦ expLoop a t + expLoopRev b t,
    (expLoop a).continuous.add (expLoopRev b).continuous⟩

@[simp]

blocks.label: lem:discrete_winding_number_c_linear_loop
blocks.title: Real-linear model winding
blocks.body:
For $\|a\|\ne\|b\|$, the path $L_{a,b}$ avoids zero and
$W_C(L_{a,b})=1$ if $\|b\|<\|a\|$, and $-1$ otherwise.

lean.name: Gluck.windingNumberC_linearLoop
lean.code:
theorem windingNumberC_linearLoop (a b : ℂ) (hab : ‖a‖ ≠ ‖b‖) :
    windingNumberC (linearLoop a b) (linearLoop_ne_zero a b hab) =
      if ‖b‖ < ‖a‖ then 1 else -1 := by
  rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hab with hlt | hgt
  · rw [if_neg (asymm hlt)]
    have hb : b ≠ 0 := norm_pos_iff.1 (lt_of_le_of_lt (norm_nonneg a) hlt)
    have hpert : ∀ t : I, ‖linearLoop a b t - expLoopRev b t‖ < ‖expLoopRev b t‖ := by
      intro t
      have he : linearLoop a b t - expLoopRev b t = expLoop a t := by
        change expLoop a t + expLoopRev b t - expLoopRev b t = expLoop a t
        ring
      rw [he, expLoop_norm, expLoopRev_norm]
      exact hlt
    have h := windingNumberC_eq_of_perturb (expLoopRev b) (linearLoop a b)
      (expLoopRev_ne_zero b hb) (linearLoop_ne_zero a b hab)
      (expLoopRev_loop b) (linearLoop_loop a b) hpert
    rw [← h, windingNumberC_expLoopRev b hb]
  · rw [if_pos hgt]
    have ha : a ≠ 0 := norm_pos_iff.1 (lt_of_le_of_lt (norm_nonneg b) hgt)
    have hpert : ∀ t : I, ‖linearLoop a b t - expLoop a t‖ < ‖expLoop a t‖ := by
      intro t
      have he : linearLoop a b t - expLoop a t = expLoopRev b t := by
        change expLoop a t + expLoopRev b t - expLoop a t = expLoopRev b t
        ring
      rw [he, expLoopRev_norm, expLoop_norm]
      exact hgt
    have h := windingNumberC_eq_of_perturb (expLoop a) (linearLoop a b)
      (expLoop_ne_zero a ha) (linearLoop_ne_zero a b hab)
      (expLoop_loop a) (linearLoop_loop a b) hpert
    rw [← h, windingNumberC_expLoop a ha]

blocks.tex:
A zero would force the two summands to have equal norms, contrary to the
hypothesis.  When $\|b\|<\|a\|$, its difference from $E_a$ has norm
$\|b\|<\|a\|$, so one-sided perturbation gives winding $1$.
In the other case compare with $E^-_b$ to get $-1$.

blocks.label: thm:discrete_poincare_miranda_rect
blocks.title: Poincare--Miranda with weak face inequalities
blocks.body:
Let $a_1\le a_2$, $b_1\le b_2$, and let
$G:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ be continuous on
$K=[a_1,a_2]\times[b_1,b_2]$.  Assume $G_1(a_1,y)\le0$ and
$G_1(a_2,y)\ge0$ for every $y\in[b_1,b_2]$, and $G_2(x,b_1)\le0$ and
$G_2(x,b_2)\ge0$ for every $x\in[a_1,a_2]$.
Then there is $p\in K$ with $G(p)=0$.  Degenerate rectangles and boundary
zeros are allowed.

lean.name: poincare_miranda
lean.code:
theorem poincare_miranda {a₁ a₂ b₁ b₂ : ℝ} (ha : a₁ ≤ a₂) (hb : b₁ ≤ b₂)
    (G : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ × ℝ)
    (hG : ContinuousOn G (Set.Icc a₁ a₂ ×ˢ Set.Icc b₁ b₂))
    (hleft : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc b₁ b₂, (G (a₁, y)).1 ≤ 0)
    (hright : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc b₁ b₂, 0 ≤ (G (a₂, y)).1)
    (hbot : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a₁ a₂, (G (x, b₁)).2 ≤ 0)
    (htop : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a₁ a₂, 0 ≤ (G (x, b₂)).2) :
    ∃ p ∈ Set.Icc a₁ a₂ ×ˢ Set.Icc b₁ b₂, G p = 0 := by
  rcases ha.eq_or_lt with hae | halt
  · have hxmem : a₁ ∈ Set.Icc a₁ a₂ := ⟨le_rfl, ha⟩
    have hg1 : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc b₁ b₂, (G (a₁, y)).1 = 0 := by
      intro y hy
      have h1 := hleft y hy
      have h2 := hright y hy
      rw [← hae] at h2
      linarith
    have hfcont : ContinuousOn (fun y ↦ G (a₁, y)) (Set.Icc b₁ b₂) :=
      hG.comp ((continuous_const.prodMk continuous_id).continuousOn)
        (fun y hy ↦ Set.mk_mem_prod hxmem hy)
    have hcont : ContinuousOn (fun y ↦ (G (a₁, y)).2) (Set.Icc b₁ b₂) :=
      continuous_snd.comp_continuousOn hfcont
    have hmem : (0 : ℝ) ∈
        Set.Icc ((fun y ↦ (G (a₁, y)).2) b₁) ((fun y ↦ (G (a₁, y)).2) b₂) :=
      ⟨hbot a₁ hxmem, htop a₁ hxmem⟩
    obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀mem, hy₀⟩ := intermediate_value_Icc hb hcont hmem
    exact ⟨(a₁, y₀), Set.mk_mem_prod hxmem hy₀mem, Prod.ext (hg1 y₀ hy₀mem) hy₀⟩
  rcases hb.eq_or_lt with hbe | hblt
  · have hymem : b₁ ∈ Set.Icc b₁ b₂ := ⟨le_rfl, hb⟩
    have hg2 : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a₁ a₂, (G (x, b₁)).2 = 0 := by
      intro x hx
      have h1 := hbot x hx
      have h2 := htop x hx
      rw [← hbe] at h2
      linarith
    have hfcont : ContinuousOn (fun x ↦ G (x, b₁)) (Set.Icc a₁ a₂) :=
      hG.comp ((continuous_id.prodMk continuous_const).continuousOn)
        (fun x hx ↦ Set.mk_mem_prod hx hymem)
    have hcont : ContinuousOn (fun x ↦ (G (x, b₁)).1) (Set.Icc a₁ a₂) :=
      continuous_fst.comp_continuousOn hfcont
    have hmem : (0 : ℝ) ∈
        Set.Icc ((fun x ↦ (G (x, b₁)).1) a₁) ((fun x ↦ (G (x, b₁)).1) a₂) :=
      ⟨hleft b₁ hymem, hright b₁ hymem⟩
    obtain ⟨x₀, hx₀mem, hx₀⟩ := intermediate_value_Icc ha hcont hmem
    exact ⟨(x₀, b₁), Set.mk_mem_prod hx₀mem hymem, Prod.ext hx₀ (hg2 x₀ hx₀mem)⟩
  set K : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := Set.Icc a₁ a₂ ×ˢ Set.Icc b₁ b₂
  have hKcomp : IsCompact K := isCompact_Icc.prod isCompact_Icc
  set cx : ℝ := (a₁ + a₂) / 2 with hcx
  set cy : ℝ := (b₁ + b₂) / 2 with hcy
  set w : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ × ℝ := fun p ↦ (p.1 - cx, p.2 - cy) with hw
  have hwcont : Continuous w := by fun_prop
  set Gn : ℕ → ℝ × ℝ → ℝ × ℝ := fun n p ↦ G p + (1 / ((n : ℝ) + 1)) • w p with hGn
  have hpos : ∀ n : ℕ, (0 : ℝ) < 1 / ((n : ℝ) + 1) := fun n ↦ by positivity
  have hzero : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ p ∈ K, Gn n p = 0 := by
    intro n
    apply poincare_miranda_of_lt halt hblt (Gn n)
    · exact hG.add (Continuous.continuousOn (by fun_prop))
    · intro y hy
      have hGl := hleft y hy
      have he : (Gn n (a₁, y)).1 = (G (a₁, y)).1 + (1 / ((n : ℝ) + 1)) * (a₁ - cx) := by
        simp [hGn, hw]
  -- … (truncated)

deps.title: Nonzero boundary winding attains the avoided value
deps.label: thm:discrete_import_degree

blocks.tex:
On a degenerate side the two opposing inequalities force the corresponding
component to vanish identically, and the one-dimensional intermediate value
theorem finds a zero of the other component.
For a nondegenerate rectangle with strict face signs, use the continuous
disk-to-square chart $z\mapsto (\|z\|/\max(|\Re z|,|\Im z|))z$, extended
by zero at the origin, followed by the affine map to $K$.  The norm of the
first chart is at most $2\|z\|$, which proves continuity at zero.
The pulled-back boundary path shares successively the right, top, left,
and bottom open half-planes with the unit circle on the arcs split at
$1/8,3/8,5/8,7/8$.  On each arc the symmetric perturbation inequality is
strict.  Its winding is therefore $1$, and the disk degree theorem gives
a zero.  These chart and four-arc steps are private helpers in the source.
For weak signs, set $G_j(p)=G(p)+(j+1)^{-1}(p-c)$, where $c$ is the
rectangle center.  These maps have strict face signs.  Choose their zeros
in compact $K$ and a convergent subsequence.  The perturbations tend to
zero along it, so continuity gives a zero of $G$ at the limiting point.

chapters.title: Discrete foundations: polygons, turning angles, realizability

blocks.tex: The cyclic polygon is indexed by $\mathbb Z/n$. The edge lengths are free variables; target curvatures determine the incident half-angles. These definitions fix the development and its geometric constraints.

blocks.label: def:discrete_trig
blocks.title: generalized sine, cosine, tangent
blocks.body:
For $K, x \in \mathbb{R}$ set
  \[
    s_K(x) = \begin{cases} \sin x & K = 1\\ \sinh x & K = -1\\ x &
    \text{otherwise,}\end{cases}
    \qquad
    c_K(x) = \begin{cases} \cos x & K = 1\\ \cosh x & K = -1\\ 1 &
    \text{otherwise,}\end{cases}
    \qquad
    t_K(x) = \frac{s_K(x)}{c_K(x)}.
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.cK
lean.code:
noncomputable def cK (K x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if K = 1 then Real.cos x else if K = -1 then Real.cosh x else 1

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.sK
lean.code:
noncomputable def sK (K x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if K = 1 then Real.sin x else if K = -1 then Real.sinh x else x

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.tK
lean.code:
noncomputable def tK (K x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  sK K x / cK K x

blocks.label: lem:discrete_trig_cases
blocks.title: case evaluation

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.cK_zero
lean.code: @[simp] lemma cK_zero (x : ℝ) : cK 0 x = 1 := by norm_num [cK]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.tK_neg_one
lean.code:
@[simp] lemma tK_neg_one (x : ℝ) : tK (-1) x = Real.tanh x := by
  rw [tK, sK_neg_one, cK_neg_one, Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh]

/-! ## Polygon data, moderate arcs, and the turning-angle law -/

variable {n : ℕ}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.cK_one
lean.code: @[simp] lemma cK_one (x : ℝ) : cK 1 x = Real.cos x := by simp [cK]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.cK_neg_one
lean.code: @[simp] lemma cK_neg_one (x : ℝ) : cK (-1) x = Real.cosh x := by norm_num [cK]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.sK_zero
lean.code: @[simp] lemma sK_zero (x : ℝ) : sK 0 x = x := by norm_num [sK]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.sK_neg_one
lean.code: @[simp] lemma sK_neg_one (x : ℝ) : sK (-1) x = Real.sinh x := by norm_num [sK]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.tK_one
lean.code:
@[simp] lemma tK_one (x : ℝ) : tK 1 x = Real.tan x := by
  rw [tK, sK_one, cK_one, Real.tan_eq_sin_div_cos]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.sK_one
lean.code: @[simp] lemma sK_one (x : ℝ) : sK 1 x = Real.sin x := by simp [sK]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.tK_zero
lean.code: @[simp] lemma tK_zero (x : ℝ) : tK 0 x = x := by simp [tK]

blocks.tex:
Immediate from the definition and the quotient identities
  $\tan = \sin/\cos$, $\tanh = \sinh/\cosh$.

blocks.title: Polygon data, moderate arcs, and the turning-angle law

blocks.tex:
Throughout, $n$ is a natural number (with $n \neq 0$, and $3 \le n$ where
stated), curvature data is $\kappa\colon\mathbb{Z}/n\to\mathbb{R}$ and edge
lengths are $\ell\colon\mathbb{Z}/n\to\mathbb{R}$; the cyclic index arithmetic
lives in $\mathbb{Z}/n$, while cumulative (lifted) quantities are defined
through the ordered lift $j \mapsto (j : \mathbb{Z}/n)$ over
$\mathrm{range}$-sums.

blocks.label: def:moderate_arc
blocks.title: strict moderate-arc domain

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ModerateArc

blocks.title: remark
blocks.body:
For $K \in \{0,-1\}$ condition (2) is automatic from $0 < \ell_i$; for
$K = 1$ it encodes $\ell_i < \pi$ (half-lengths in the principal branch of
$\tan$), which keeps $t_1(\ell_i/2)$ positive and the arcsin arguments
honest. The wall is \emph{strict}: this is what makes every turning angle
strictly less than $\pi$ (\cref{lem:turning_angle_lt_pi}), the load-bearing
strictness in the positive-support obstruction. Geometrically the class
restricts every subtended arc to strictly less than half its cycle.

blocks.label: lem:moderate_arc_accessors
blocks.title: moderate-arc accessors

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ModerateArc.wall_right
lean.code:
lemma wall_right (h : ModerateArc K κ ℓ) (i : ZMod n) :
    |κ i| * tK K (ℓ i / 2) < 1 := (h i).2.2.2.2

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ModerateArc.length_pos
lean.code: lemma length_pos (h : ModerateArc K κ ℓ) (i : ZMod n) : 0 < ℓ i := (h i).1

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ModerateArc.tK_pos
lean.code:
lemma tK_pos (h : ModerateArc K κ ℓ) (i : ZMod n) : 0 < tK K (ℓ i / 2) :=
  div_pos (h i).2.1 (h i).2.2.1

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ModerateArc.wall_left
lean.code:
lemma wall_left (h : ModerateArc K κ ℓ) (i : ZMod n) :
    |κ i| * tK K (ℓ (i - 1) / 2) < 1 := (h i).2.2.2.1

blocks.tex:
Projections of the conjuncts of \cref{def:moderate_arc}; positivity of
  $t_K = s_K/c_K$ is the quotient of the two positive-branch conditions.

blocks.label: lem:moderate_arc_zero
blocks.title: moderate arc at $K=0$
blocks.body:
$\mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell$ holds if and only if for every $i$:
  $0<\ell_i$, $|\kappa_i|\,\ell_{i-1}/2 < 1$ and $|\kappa_i|\,\ell_i/2 < 1$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.moderateArc_zero_iff
lean.code:
lemma moderateArc_zero_iff {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} :
    ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ ↔ ∀ i : ZMod n,
      0 < ℓ i ∧ |κ i| * (ℓ (i - 1) / 2) < 1 ∧ |κ i| * (ℓ i / 2) < 1 := by
  constructor
  · intro h i
    obtain ⟨h1, _, _, h4, h5⟩ := h i
    rw [tK_zero] at h4 h5
    exact ⟨h1, h4, h5⟩
  · intro h i
    obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ := h i
    exact ⟨h1, by simpa using half_pos h1, by simp, by simpa using h2, by simpa using h3⟩

blocks.tex:
At $K=0$, $s_0(x)=x$, $c_0(x)=1$, $t_0(x)=x$; condition (2) of
  \cref{def:moderate_arc} reduces to $0<\ell_i/2$, already implied by (1).

blocks.label: def:turning_angle
blocks.title: turning angle, (TA)
blocks.body:
The turning angle at vertex $i$ of the data $(K,\kappa,\ell)$ is
  \[
    \theta_i \;=\; \arcsin\bigl(\kappa_i\, t_K(\ell_{i-1}/2)\bigr)
             \;+\; \arcsin\bigl(\kappa_i\, t_K(\ell_i/2)\bigr).
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.turningAngle
lean.code:
noncomputable def turningAngle (K : ℝ) (κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ) (i : ZMod n) : ℝ :=
  Real.arcsin (κ i * tK K (ℓ (i - 1) / 2)) + Real.arcsin (κ i * tK K (ℓ i / 2))

blocks.label: lem:turning_angle_neg
blocks.title: oddness in $\kappa$
blocks.body: $\theta_i(K, -\kappa, \ell) = -\,\theta_i(K, \kappa, \ell)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.turningAngle_neg
lean.code:
lemma turningAngle_neg (K : ℝ) (κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ) (i : ZMod n) :
    turningAngle K (-κ) ℓ i = -turningAngle K κ ℓ i := by
  simp [turningAngle, neg_mul, Real.arcsin_neg]
  ring

blocks.tex: $\arcsin$ is odd.

blocks.label: lem:turning_angle_sign
blocks.title: sign of the turning angle
blocks.body:
Under $\mathrm{ModerateArc}\,K\,\kappa\,\ell$: if $\kappa_i > 0$ then
  $\theta_i > 0$; if $\kappa_i < 0$ then $\theta_i < 0$; if $\kappa_i = 0$
  then $\theta_i = 0$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.turningAngle_pos
lean.code:
lemma turningAngle_pos {K : ℝ} {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (h : ModerateArc K κ ℓ)
    {i : ZMod n} (hκ : 0 < κ i) : 0 < turningAngle K κ ℓ i :=
  add_pos (Real.arcsin_pos.2 (mul_pos hκ (h.tK_pos (i - 1))))
    (Real.arcsin_pos.2 (mul_pos hκ (h.tK_pos i)))

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.turningAngle_neg_of_neg
lean.code:
lemma turningAngle_neg_of_neg {K : ℝ} {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (h : ModerateArc K κ ℓ)
    {i : ZMod n} (hκ : κ i < 0) : turningAngle K κ ℓ i < 0 :=
  add_neg (Real.arcsin_lt_zero.2 (mul_neg_of_neg_of_pos hκ (h.tK_pos (i - 1))))
    (Real.arcsin_lt_zero.2 (mul_neg_of_neg_of_pos hκ (h.tK_pos i)))

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.turningAngle_eq_zero

blocks.tex:
The positive-branch condition gives $t_K(\ell_j/2) = s_K/c_K > 0$ on both
  adjacent edges, so each $\arcsin$ argument $\kappa_i\, t_K(\ell_j/2)$ has
  the strict sign of $\kappa_i$, and $\arcsin$ is strictly monotone with
  $\arcsin 0 = 0$; the sum of two terms of the same strict sign has that
  sign.

blocks.label: lem:turning_angle_lt_pi
blocks.title: turning angles are strictly moderate
blocks.body:
Under $\mathrm{ModerateArc}\,K\,\kappa\,\ell$, $|\theta_i| < \pi$ for every
  $i$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.abs_turningAngle_lt_pi
lean.code:
lemma abs_turningAngle_lt_pi {K : ℝ} {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (h : ModerateArc K κ ℓ)
    (i : ZMod n) : |turningAngle K κ ℓ i| < Real.pi := by
  have key : ∀ j : ZMod n, |κ i| * tK K (ℓ j / 2) < 1 →
      |Real.arcsin (κ i * tK K (ℓ j / 2))| < Real.pi / 2 := by
    intro j hj
    have habs : |κ i * tK K (ℓ j / 2)| < 1 := by
      rwa [abs_mul, abs_of_pos (h.tK_pos j)]
    rw [abs_lt] at habs ⊢
    exact ⟨Real.neg_pi_div_two_lt_arcsin.2 habs.1, Real.arcsin_lt_pi_div_two.2 habs.2⟩
  have h1 := key (i - 1) (h.wall_left i)
  have h2 := key i (h.wall_right i)
  calc |turningAngle K κ ℓ i|
      ≤ |Real.arcsin (κ i * tK K (ℓ (i - 1) / 2))| +
        |Real.arcsin (κ i * tK K (ℓ i / 2))| := abs_add_le _ _
    _ < Real.pi := by linarith

/-! ## Euclidean development and closure -/

blocks.tex:
Both arcsin arguments have absolute value
  $|\kappa_i|\cdot t_K(\ell_j/2) < 1$ (strict wall; $t_K > 0$ lets the
  absolute value pass through the product), so each $\arcsin$ lies strictly
  inside $(-\pi/2, \pi/2)$ and the sum lies strictly inside $(-\pi,\pi)$.

The Euclidean ($K=0$) development turns the data into a polygonal path in
$\mathbb{C}$. The convention: edge $j$ leaves vertex $j$ after the turn at
vertex $j$, so edge $j$ has heading $\psi_j = \sum_{m \le j}\theta_m$.
Cumulative quantities are defined on the ordered lift ($j \in \mathbb{N}$,
indices cast into $\mathbb{Z}/n$).

blocks.label: def:discrete_development
blocks.title: headings, vertices, closure error
blocks.body:
For $j, k \in \mathbb{N}$:
  \[
    \psi_j = \sum_{m=0}^{j} \theta_{(m : \mathbb{Z}/n)}, \qquad
    v_k = \sum_{j=0}^{k-1} \ell_{(j:\mathbb{Z}/n)}\,
          e^{i \psi_j} \in \mathbb{C},
  \]
  with $\theta$ the $K=0$ turning angles of \cref{def:turning_angle}. The
  \emph{closure gap} is $E(\kappa,\ell) = v_n \in \mathbb{C}$ and the
  \emph{turning sum} is
  $T(\kappa,\ell) = \sum_{i \in \mathbb{Z}/n} \theta_i$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.closureGap
lean.code:
noncomputable def closureGap (κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ) : ℂ :=
  vertexR2 κ ℓ n

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.turningSum
lean.code:
noncomputable def turningSum [NeZero n] (κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : ZMod n, turningAngle 0 κ ℓ i

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.vertexR2
lean.code:
noncomputable def vertexR2 (κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : ℂ :=
  ∑ j ∈ Finset.range k,
    (ℓ (j : ZMod n) : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((heading κ ℓ j : ℂ) * Complex.I)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.heading
lean.code:
noncomputable def heading (κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ) (j : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (j + 1), turningAngle 0 κ ℓ (m : ZMod n)

blocks.label: lem:development_recurrences
blocks.title: development recurrences
blocks.body:
The vertex map satisfies the one-step recurrence
  $v_{k+1} = v_k + \ell_{(k:\mathbb{Z}/n)}\,e^{i\psi_k}$; the heading over a
  full period shifts by the turning sum,
  $\psi_{j+n} = \psi_j + T(\kappa,\ell)$; and for any additive monoid $M$ and
  $g\colon\mathbb{Z}/n\to M$,
  $\sum_{m=0}^{a+n-1} g_{(m:\mathbb{Z}/n)}
    = \sum_{m=0}^{a-1} g_{(m:\mathbb{Z}/n)} + \sum_{i\in\mathbb{Z}/n} g_i$
  (a period block of a lifted cyclic sum equals the full cyclic sum).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.heading_add_n
lean.code:
lemma heading_add_n [NeZero n] {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (hT : turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * Real.pi) (j : ℕ) :
    heading κ ℓ (j + n) = heading κ ℓ j + 2 * Real.pi := by
  unfold heading
  rw [show j + n + 1 = (j + 1) + n from by ring,
    Finset.sum_range_add (fun m => turningAngle 0 κ ℓ (m : ZMod n)) (j + 1) n,
    sum_range_natCast_add (turningAngle 0 κ ℓ) (j + 1)]
  rw [show (∑ i : ZMod n, turningAngle 0 κ ℓ i) = turningSum κ ℓ from rfl, hT]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.vertexR2_succ
lean.code:
lemma vertexR2_succ (κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
    vertexR2 κ ℓ (k + 1) = vertexR2 κ ℓ k
      + (ℓ (k : ZMod n) : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((heading κ ℓ k : ℂ) * Complex.I) :=
  Finset.sum_range_succ _ _

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.sum_range_natCast_add
lean.code:
lemma sum_range_natCast_add {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [NeZero n]
    (f : ZMod n → M) (a : ℕ) :
    ∑ m ∈ Finset.range n, f ((a + m : ℕ) : ZMod n) = ∑ i : ZMod n, f i := by
  have base : ∀ g : ZMod n → M,
      ∑ m ∈ Finset.range n, g (m : ZMod n) = ∑ i : ZMod n, g i := by
    intro g
    rw [← Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun m => g (m : ZMod n)) n]
    exact Fintype.sum_bijective (fun i : Fin n => ((i : ℕ) : ZMod n))
      ⟨fun a b hab => Fin.ext (by
          simpa [ZMod.val_cast_of_lt a.isLt, ZMod.val_cast_of_lt b.isLt] using
            congrArg ZMod.val hab),
        fun z => ⟨⟨z.val, z.val_lt⟩, ZMod.natCast_rightInverse z⟩⟩
      _ _ (fun _ => rfl)
  calc ∑ m ∈ Finset.range n, f ((a + m : ℕ) : ZMod n)
      = ∑ m ∈ Finset.range n, (fun i => f ((a : ZMod n) + i)) (m : ZMod n) := by
        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun m _ => ?_
        push_cast
        rfl
    _ = ∑ i : ZMod n, (fun i => f ((a : ZMod n) + i)) i :=
        base (fun i => f ((a : ZMod n) + i))
    _ = ∑ i : ZMod n, f i :=
        Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.addLeft ((a : ℕ) : ZMod n)) _ _ (fun _ => rfl)

blocks.tex:
The recurrence is the last term of the range sum defining $v_{k+1}$. The
  reindexing identity splits $\mathrm{range}(a+n)$ and reindexes the tail
  block by $m\mapsto m+a$, whose casts $(m+a:\mathbb{Z}/n)$ run over all of
  $\mathbb{Z}/n$ once; the heading shift is its specialization to
  $g = \theta$.

blocks.label: lem:development_periodic
blocks.title: periodicity of the closed development
blocks.body:
If $E(\kappa,\ell) = 0$ and $T(\kappa,\ell) = 2\pi$, then
  $\psi_{j+n} = \psi_j + 2\pi$ and $v_{k+n} = v_k$ for all $j,k$; in
  particular the vertex map descends to a well-defined polygon
  $\mathbb{Z}/n \to \mathbb{C}$, $i \mapsto v_{i.\mathrm{val}}$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.vertexR2_add_n
lean.code:
lemma vertexR2_add_n [NeZero n] {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (hE : closureGap κ ℓ = 0)
    (hT : turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * Real.pi) (k : ℕ) :
    vertexR2 κ ℓ (k + n) = vertexR2 κ ℓ k := by
  induction k with
  | zero => simpa [closureGap, vertexR2] using hE
  | succ k ih =>
    have hedge : (ℓ ((k + n : ℕ) : ZMod n) : ℂ)
          * Complex.exp ((heading κ ℓ (k + n) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
        = (ℓ (k : ZMod n) : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((heading κ ℓ k : ℂ) * Complex.I) := by
      have h1 : ((k + n : ℕ) : ZMod n) = (k : ZMod n) := by
        push_cast [ZMod.natCast_self]
        ring
      have h2 : ((heading κ ℓ k + 2 * Real.pi : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I
          = (heading κ ℓ k : ℂ) * Complex.I + 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I := by
        push_cast
        ring
      rw [h1, heading_add_n hT, h2, Complex.exp_add, Complex.exp_two_pi_mul_I, mul_one]
    rw [show k + 1 + n = (k + n) + 1 from by ring, vertexR2_succ, vertexR2_succ, ih, hedge]

blocks.tex:
Splitting the range sum, $\psi_{j+n} - \psi_j$ is a sum of $n$ consecutive
  turning angles whose indices run over all of $\mathbb{Z}/n$ exactly once,
  hence equals $T = 2\pi$; therefore $e^{i\psi_{j+n}} = e^{i\psi_j}$ and the
  edge vectors are $n$-periodic in $j$, so
  $v_{k+n} - v_k = \sum_{j=k}^{k+n-1} \ell\, e^{i\psi} = e^{i\psi_{k}}\cdot
  (\text{rotation of } E) = 0$; concretely, the block of $n$ consecutive
  edge vectors starting at $k$ is the block starting at $0$ rotated by the
  common phase, and the latter sums to $E = 0$.

blocks.label: def:discrete_polygon
blocks.title: polygon of a closed development
blocks.body:
$P(\kappa,\ell)\colon \mathbb{Z}/n \to \mathbb{C}$,
  $P_i = v_{i.\mathrm{val}}$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.polygonR2
lean.code:
noncomputable def polygonR2 (κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ) : ZMod n → ℂ :=
  fun i => vertexR2 κ ℓ i.val

/-! ## Simple polygons and realizability -/

blocks.label: def:simple_polygon
blocks.title: simple polygon

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.IsSimplePolygon
lean.code:
def IsSimplePolygon (v : ZMod n → ℂ) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : ZMod n, v i ≠ v (i + 1)) ∧
    (∀ i : ZMod n,
      segment ℝ (v i) (v (i + 1)) ∩ segment ℝ (v (i + 1)) (v (i + 1 + 1))
        = {v (i + 1)}) ∧
    (∀ i j : ZMod n, i ≠ j → i + 1 ≠ j → j + 1 ≠ i →
      segment ℝ (v i) (v (i + 1)) ∩ segment ℝ (v j) (v (j + 1)) = ∅)

blocks.label: def:discrete_realizes
blocks.title: Euclidean discrete realizability
blocks.body:
$\mathrm{RealizesR2}\,\kappa$ holds when there exist edge lengths
  $\ell\colon\mathbb{Z}/n\to\mathbb{R}$ with
  \[
    \mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell, \qquad
    E(\kappa,\ell) = 0, \qquad
    T(\kappa,\ell) = 2\pi, \qquad
    \mathrm{IsSimplePolygon}\,\bigl(P(\kappa,\ell)\bigr).
  \]
  \emph{Non-degeneracy (standing definitional directive, user @085): every
  realization must have strictly positive edge lengths, $\ell_j > 0$ ---
  a zero-length edge collapses two vertices, making the object an
  $(n{-}1)$-gon. This clause is ALREADY carried by the first conjunct of
  \cref{def:moderate_arc} (\texttt{ModerateArc.length\_pos}), so the
  definition as stated satisfies the directive; no change was needed.}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RealizesR2
lean.code:
def RealizesR2 [NeZero n] (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ, ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ ∧ closureGap κ ℓ = 0 ∧
    turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * Real.pi ∧ IsSimplePolygon (polygonR2 κ ℓ)

/-! ## The constant profile closes -/

blocks.title: remark
blocks.body:
The normalization $T = 2\pi$ is the positive-orientation gauge: the
program's constructions always produce it, and the obstruction statements of
\cref{chap:discrete_budget} address the reflected gauge $T = -2\pi$ through
the oddness symmetry \cref{lem:turning_angle_neg}. The bridge from (TA) to
the circumcycle phrasing (each triple $(P_{i-1},P_i,P_{i+1})$ lies on a
circle of signed curvature $\kappa_i$) is the tangent--chord equivalence,
deferred to the forthcoming \texttt{TangentChord} chapter; the chord-level
consequence needed early — the Menger chord identity — is proved directly in
\cref{chap:discrete_budget}.

blocks.tex:
A first sanity target validating the definitional layer end to end: the
regular $n$-gon closes the constant profile. (Its \emph{simplicity} — hence
the full constant branch of the discrete Gluck converse — follows once the
discrete convexity lemma L1 lands with the closing engine; it is not needed
for the obstruction chapter.)

blocks.label: lem:regular_gon_closes
blocks.title: regular polygon closes the constant profile
blocks.body:
Let $3 \le n$, $c > 0$, and set $\ell_i = (2/c)\sin(\pi/n)$ for all $i$.
  Then for the constant profile $\kappa \equiv c$:
  $\mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell$, every turning angle equals
  $2\pi/n$, $T = 2\pi$, and $E(\kappa,\ell) = 0$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.regularGon_closes
lean.code:
theorem regularGon_closes {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (hn : 3 ≤ n) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    ModerateArc 0 (fun _ : ZMod n => c)
        (fun _ => 2 / c * Real.sin (Real.pi / n)) ∧
      (∀ i : ZMod n,
        turningAngle 0 (fun _ => c) (fun _ => 2 / c * Real.sin (Real.pi / n)) i
          = 2 * Real.pi / n) ∧
      turningSum (fun _ : ZMod n => c)
        (fun _ => 2 / c * Real.sin (Real.pi / n)) = 2 * Real.pi ∧
      closureGap (fun _ : ZMod n => c)
        (fun _ => 2 / c * Real.sin (Real.pi / n)) = 0 := by
  have hn3 : (3 : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hn
  have hnpos : (0 : ℝ) < n := by linarith
  have hπn_pos : 0 < Real.pi / n := div_pos Real.pi_pos hnpos
  have hπn_le : Real.pi / n ≤ Real.pi / 3 := by gcongr
  have hπn_lt_half : Real.pi / n < Real.pi / 2 := by linarith [Real.pi_pos]
  have hsin_pos : 0 < Real.sin (Real.pi / n) :=
    Real.sin_pos_of_pos_of_lt_pi hπn_pos (by linarith [Real.pi_pos])
  have hsin_lt : Real.sin (Real.pi / n) < 1 := by
    rw [← Real.sin_pi_div_two]
    exact Real.sin_lt_sin_of_lt_of_le_pi_div_two (by linarith) le_rfl hπn_lt_half
  have hl_pos : 0 < 2 / c * Real.sin (Real.pi / n) :=
    mul_pos (div_pos two_pos hc) hsin_pos
  have hkey : c * (2 / c * Real.sin (Real.pi / n) / 2) = Real.sin (Real.pi / n) := by
    field_simp
  have harc : Real.arcsin (Real.sin (Real.pi / n)) = Real.pi / n :=
    Real.arcsin_sin (by linarith) (by linarith)
  -- moderate arc
  have hMA : ModerateArc 0 (fun _ : ZMod n => c)
      (fun _ => 2 / c * Real.sin (Real.pi / n)) := by
    rw [moderateArc_zero_iff]
    intro i
    refine ⟨hl_pos, ?_, ?_⟩ <;>
      simpa [abs_of_pos hc, hkey] using hsin_lt
  -- turning angles
  have hturn : ∀ i : ZMod n,
      turningAngle 0 (fun _ => c) (fun _ => 2 / c * Real.sin (Real.pi / n)) i
        = 2 * Real.pi / n := by
    intro i
    simp only [turningAngle, tK_zero]
    rw [hkey, harc]
    ring
  -- total turning
  have hsum : turningSum (fun _ : ZMod n => c)
      (fun _ => 2 / c * Real.sin (Real.pi / n)) = 2 * Real.pi := by
    unfold turningSum
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => hturn i, Finset.sum_const,
      Finset.card_univ, ZMod.card, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_comm,
      div_mul_cancel₀ _ (ne_of_gt hnpos)]
  -- headings
  have hhead : ∀ j : ℕ,
      heading (fun _ : ZMod n => c) (fun _ => 2 / c * Real.sin (Real.pi / n)) j
        = (j + 1) * (2 * Real.pi / n) := by
    intro j
    unfold heading
    simp only [hturn]
    rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_range, nsmul_eq_mul]
    push_cast
    ring
  refine ⟨hMA, hturn, hsum, ?_⟩
  -- closure gap: finite geometric sum of the n-th roots of unity
  -- … (truncated)

blocks.tex:
Moderate arc: $\ell_i > 0$ and
  $c\,\ell_i/2 = \sin(\pi/n) < 1$ since $0 < \pi/n \le \pi/3 < \pi/2$.
  Turning: both arcsin arguments equal $\sin(\pi/n)$, and
  $\arcsin(\sin(\pi/n)) = \pi/n$ on the principal branch, so
  $\theta_i = 2\pi/n$ and $T = n\cdot(2\pi/n) = 2\pi$. Closure: the headings
  are $\psi_j = (j+1)\cdot 2\pi/n$, so
  $E = \ell_0 \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} e^{2\pi i (j+1)/n}
     = \ell_0\, e^{2\pi i/n}\,\frac{e^{2\pi i} - 1}{e^{2\pi i/n} - 1} = 0$
  by the finite geometric series ($e^{2\pi i/n} \neq 1$ for $n \ge 2$).
The turning-angle inequalities below provide the basic size and sign constraints used by the converse construction.

blocks.label: lem:sin_sq_add_identity
blocks.title: sine addition square identity
blocks.body:
For all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$:
  \[
    \sin^2(a+b) \;=\; \sin^2 a + \sin^2 b + 2 \sin a \sin b \cos(a+b).
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.sin_sq_add_identity
lean.code:
theorem sin_sq_add_identity (a b : ℝ) :
    sin (a + b) ^ 2 =
      sin a ^ 2 + sin b ^ 2 + 2 * sin a * sin b * cos (a + b) := by
  have ha := sin_sq_add_cos_sq a
  have hb := sin_sq_add_cos_sq b
  rw [sin_add, cos_add]
  nlinarith [ha, hb]

blocks.tex:
Expand $\sin(a+b) = \sin a\cos b + \cos a \sin b$ and
  $\cos(a+b) = \cos a\cos b - \sin a\sin b$; both sides equal
  $\sin^2 a\cos^2 b + 2\sin a\cos a\sin b\cos b + \cos^2 a\sin^2 b$ after
  eliminating $\cos^2 = 1 - \sin^2$ (pure ring algebra; the identity is
  unconditional).

blocks.label: lem:menger_arith_helpers
blocks.title: arcsin-sum arithmetic for the chord identity
blocks.body:
For $|x|,|y|\le 1$, with $a=\arcsin x$, $b=\arcsin y$:
  $\sin(a+b) = x\sqrt{1-y^2} + y\sqrt{1-x^2}$, and
  $\sin^2(a+b) = x^2 + y^2 + 2xy\cos(a+b)$. Consequently, writing
  $x = \kappa\ell_0/2$, $y = \kappa\ell_1/2$ under the wall bounds,
  $\kappa\sqrt{\ell_0^2+\ell_1^2+2\ell_0\ell_1\cos(a+b)} = 2\sin(a+b)$ once
  signs are matched.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.sin_arcsin_add_arcsin
lean.code:
theorem sin_arcsin_add_arcsin {x y : ℝ} (hx : |x| ≤ 1) (hy : |y| ≤ 1) :
    sin (arcsin x + arcsin y) = x * sqrt (1 - y ^ 2) + y * sqrt (1 - x ^ 2) := by
  rw [sin_add, sin_arcsin (abs_le.mp hx).1 (abs_le.mp hx).2,
    sin_arcsin (abs_le.mp hy).1 (abs_le.mp hy).2, cos_arcsin, cos_arcsin]
  ring

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.mul_sqrt_chord_eq_two_sin
lean.code:
theorem mul_sqrt_chord_eq_two_sin {κ l₀ l₁ : ℝ}
    (h₀ : 0 < l₀) (h₁ : 0 < l₁)
    (w₀ : |κ| * (l₀ / 2) < 1) (w₁ : |κ| * (l₁ / 2) < 1) :
    κ * sqrt (l₀ ^ 2 + l₁ ^ 2 + 2 * l₀ * l₁ *
        cos (arcsin (κ * (l₀ / 2)) + arcsin (κ * (l₁ / 2)))) =
      2 * sin (arcsin (κ * (l₀ / 2)) + arcsin (κ * (l₁ / 2))) := by
  rcases eq_or_ne κ 0 with hκ | hκ
  · simp [hκ]
  · have hx1 : |κ * (l₀ / 2)| < 1 := by
      rwa [abs_mul, abs_of_pos (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) < l₀ / 2)]
    have hy1 : |κ * (l₁ / 2)| < 1 := by
      rwa [abs_mul, abs_of_pos (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) < l₁ / 2)]
    have hsq := sin_sq_arcsin_add_arcsin hx1.le hy1.le
    have hsin := sin_arcsin_add_arcsin hx1.le hy1.le
    have hsign : 0 ≤ 2 * sin (arcsin (κ * (l₀ / 2)) + arcsin (κ * (l₁ / 2))) / κ := by
      rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hκ with hneg | hpos
      · have hx0 : κ * (l₀ / 2) ≤ 0 := by nlinarith
        have hy0 : κ * (l₁ / 2) ≤ 0 := by nlinarith
        have hs : sin (arcsin (κ * (l₀ / 2)) + arcsin (κ * (l₁ / 2))) ≤ 0 := by
          rw [hsin]
          have h1 := sqrt_nonneg (1 - (κ * (l₁ / 2)) ^ 2)
          have h2 := sqrt_nonneg (1 - (κ * (l₀ / 2)) ^ 2)
          nlinarith
        exact div_nonneg_of_nonpos (by linarith) hneg.le
      · have hx0 : 0 ≤ κ * (l₀ / 2) := by positivity
        have hy0 : 0 ≤ κ * (l₁ / 2) := by positivity
        have hs : 0 ≤ sin (arcsin (κ * (l₀ / 2)) + arcsin (κ * (l₁ / 2))) := by
          rw [hsin]
          have h1 := sqrt_nonneg (1 - (κ * (l₁ / 2)) ^ 2)
          have h2 := sqrt_nonneg (1 - (κ * (l₀ / 2)) ^ 2)
          positivity
        positivity
    have key : κ ^ 2 * (l₀ ^ 2 + l₁ ^ 2 + 2 * l₀ * l₁ *
        cos (arcsin (κ * (l₀ / 2)) + arcsin (κ * (l₁ / 2)))) =
        (2 * sin (arcsin (κ * (l₀ / 2)) + arcsin (κ * (l₁ / 2)))) ^ 2 := by
      linear_combination (-4 : ℝ) * hsq
    have hrw : (2 * sin (arcsin (κ * (l₀ / 2)) + arcsin (κ * (l₁ / 2))) / κ) ^ 2 =
        l₀ ^ 2 + l₁ ^ 2 + 2 * l₀ * l₁ *
          cos (arcsin (κ * (l₀ / 2)) + arcsin (κ * (l₁ / 2))) := by
      rw [div_pow, ← key, mul_div_cancel_left₀]
      exact pow_ne_zero 2 hκ
    rw [← hrw, sqrt_sq hsign]
    field_simp

/-! ## Counting core for N1 -/

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.sin_sq_arcsin_add_arcsin
lean.code:
theorem sin_sq_arcsin_add_arcsin {x y : ℝ} (hx : |x| ≤ 1) (hy : |y| ≤ 1) :
    sin (arcsin x + arcsin y) ^ 2 =
      x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 + 2 * x * y * cos (arcsin x + arcsin y) := by
  have h := sin_sq_add_identity (arcsin x) (arcsin y)
  rwa [sin_arcsin (abs_le.mp hx).1 (abs_le.mp hx).2,
    sin_arcsin (abs_le.mp hy).1 (abs_le.mp hy).2] at h

blocks.tex:
$\sin\arcsin x = x$ and $\cos\arcsin x = \sqrt{1-x^2}$ on $[-1,1]$; the
  square identity is \cref{lem:sin_sq_add_identity} with these substitutions;
  the last line is the square-root extraction feeding
  \cref{lem:menger_chord_identity}.

blocks.label: def:vertex_chord
blocks.title: vertex chord
blocks.body:
For data $(\kappa, \ell)$ at $K=0$, the \emph{vertex chord} at $i$ is
  \[
    m_i \;=\; \sqrt{\ell_{i-1}^2 + \ell_i^2 +
      2\,\ell_{i-1}\ell_i\cos\theta_i}\;\ge 0 .
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.vertexChord
lean.code:
noncomputable def vertexChord (κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ) (i : ZMod n) : ℝ :=
  sqrt (ℓ (i - 1) ^ 2 + ℓ i ^ 2 + 2 * ℓ (i - 1) * ℓ i * cos (turningAngle 0 κ ℓ i))

blocks.title: remark
blocks.body:
$m_i$ is the length of the chord from $P_{i-1}$ to $P_{i+1}$ in any
development: the two edge vectors at vertex $i$ have lengths
$\ell_{i-1}, \ell_i$ and meet at exterior angle $\theta_i$, so
$\|P_{i+1} - P_{i-1}\|^2 = \|\ell_{i-1}e^{i\psi_{i-1}} +
\ell_i e^{i\psi_i}\|^2 = \ell_{i-1}^2 + \ell_i^2 +
2\ell_{i-1}\ell_i\cos\theta_i$ since $\psi_i - \psi_{i-1} = \theta_i$. This
geometric reading is used only in the $n = 3$ argument below
(\cref{lem:chord_eq_dist}).

blocks.label: lem:menger_chord_identity
blocks.title: Menger chord identity
blocks.body:
Under $\mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell$, for every $i$:
  \[
    \kappa_i \, m_i \;=\; 2\,\sin\theta_i .
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.menger_chord_identity
lean.code:
theorem menger_chord_identity {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (h : ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ)
    (i : ZMod n) :
    κ i * vertexChord κ ℓ i = 2 * sin (turningAngle 0 κ ℓ i) := by
  have w₀ := h.wall_left i
  have w₁ := h.wall_right i
  rw [tK_zero] at w₀ w₁
  have key := mul_sqrt_chord_eq_two_sin (κ := κ i)
    (h.length_pos (i - 1)) (h.length_pos i) w₀ w₁
  simpa only [vertexChord, turningAngle, tK_zero] using key

/-! ## N1: positive-turning support -/

deps.title: arcsin-sum arithmetic for the chord identity
deps.label: lem:menger_arith_helpers

blocks.tex:
Write $a = \arcsin(\kappa_i\ell_{i-1}/2)$, $b = \arcsin(\kappa_i\ell_i/2)$,
  so $\theta_i = a + b$, and by the strict wall
  ($|\kappa_i|\ell_j/2 < 1$) the arcsin inverts:
  $\sin a = \kappa_i\ell_{i-1}/2$, $\sin b = \kappa_i\ell_i/2$. By
  \cref{lem:sin_sq_add_identity},
  \[
    \sin^2\theta_i
      = \tfrac{\kappa_i^2}{4}\Bigl(\ell_{i-1}^2 + \ell_i^2
        + 2\ell_{i-1}\ell_i\cos\theta_i\Bigr)
      = \tfrac{\kappa_i^2}{4}\, m_i^2 ,
  \]
  i.e.\ $(2\sin\theta_i)^2 = (\kappa_i m_i)^2$. It remains to match signs.
  If $\kappa_i = 0$ both sides vanish ($\theta_i = 0$ by
  \cref{lem:turning_angle_sign}). If $\kappa_i > 0$ then
  $\theta_i \in (0,\pi)$ by \cref{lem:turning_angle_sign,lem:turning_angle_lt_pi},
  so $\sin\theta_i > 0$, while $\kappa_i m_i \ge 0$; equal squares with equal
  (nonnegative) signs give equality. The case $\kappa_i < 0$ is symmetric
  ($\theta_i \in (-\pi, 0)$, both sides nonpositive).

blocks.title: remark
blocks.body:
The killer profile satisfies the discrete transport of the smooth
value-separated four-vertex hypothesis: with window level $c = 0$, indices
$0 < 1 < 2 < 3$ alternate as
$\kappa_1, \kappa_3 < 0 < \kappa_0, \kappa_2$ — this is
$\mathrm{DFV}(\kappa; 0)$, the shape of the hypothesis carried by the
completed smooth capstones. Unrealizability for every $M$ shows the smooth
hypothesis class is genuinely insufficient discretely; the mixed discrete
theorem must demand positivity of all four window values
($\mathrm{PositiveDFV}$) plus a capacity condition. This is the mathematical
payload separating the discrete program from a mechanical transcription.

blocks.tex:
Throughout this section $n = 3$, and $(\kappa, \ell)$ satisfies
$\mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell$, $E(\kappa,\ell) = 0$ and
$T(\kappa,\ell) = 2\pi$. Note simplicity is \emph{not} assumed: rigidity
already holds for closed turning-normalized data.

blocks.label: lem:triangle_angles_interior
blocks.title: all three angles are interior
blocks.body: Each $\theta_i \in (0, \pi)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.triangle_turning_mem_Ioo
lean.code:
theorem triangle_turning_mem_Ioo {κ ℓ : ZMod 3 → ℝ} (h : ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ)
    (hT : turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * π) (i : ZMod 3) :
    turningAngle 0 κ ℓ i ∈ Set.Ioo 0 π := by
  have hsum : turningAngle 0 κ ℓ 0 + turningAngle 0 κ ℓ 1 + turningAngle 0 κ ℓ 2 =
      2 * π := by
    rw [← sum_zmod3 (turningAngle 0 κ ℓ)]
    exact hT
  have h0 := abs_lt.mp (abs_turningAngle_lt_pi h 0)
  have h1 := abs_lt.mp (abs_turningAngle_lt_pi h 1)
  have h2 := abs_lt.mp (abs_turningAngle_lt_pi h 2)
  rcases zmod3_cases i with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    exact ⟨by linarith, by linarith⟩

blocks.tex:
$\theta_i < \pi$ is \cref{lem:turning_angle_lt_pi}. From
  $\theta_0 + \theta_1 + \theta_2 = 2\pi$ and the other two angles being
  $< \pi$ each: $\theta_i = 2\pi - \theta_j - \theta_k > 2\pi - \pi - \pi = 0$.

blocks.label: lem:triangle_law_of_sines
blocks.title: discrete law of sines at $n=3$
blocks.body:
$\ell_0 \sin\theta_0 = \ell_1 \sin\theta_2$,
  $\ell_1 \sin\theta_1 = \ell_2 \sin\theta_0$, and
  $\ell_2 \sin\theta_2 = \ell_0 \sin\theta_1$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.triangle_law_of_sines
lean.code:
theorem triangle_law_of_sines {κ ℓ : ZMod 3 → ℝ} (hE : closureGap κ ℓ = 0)
    (hT : turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * π) :
    ℓ 0 * sin (turningAngle 0 κ ℓ 0) = ℓ 1 * sin (turningAngle 0 κ ℓ 2) ∧
      ℓ 1 * sin (turningAngle 0 κ ℓ 1) = ℓ 2 * sin (turningAngle 0 κ ℓ 0) ∧
      ℓ 2 * sin (turningAngle 0 κ ℓ 2) = ℓ 0 * sin (turningAngle 0 κ ℓ 1) := by
  set θ0 := turningAngle 0 κ ℓ 0 with hθ0
  set θ1 := turningAngle 0 κ ℓ 1 with hθ1
  set θ2 := turningAngle 0 κ ℓ 2 with hθ2
  have hsum : θ0 + θ1 + θ2 = 2 * π := by
    rw [hθ0, hθ1, hθ2, ← sum_zmod3 (turningAngle 0 κ ℓ)]
    exact hT
  have hcl := triangle_closure hE
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · -- rotate by ψ₂ = θ0+θ1+θ2 = 2π
    have hs := sum_sin_of_closure hcl (θ0 + θ1 + θ2)
    rw [show θ0 - (θ0 + θ1 + θ2) = θ0 - 2 * π from by rw [hsum],
      show θ0 + θ1 - (θ0 + θ1 + θ2) = (θ0 + θ1 + θ2) - θ2 - (θ0 + θ1 + θ2) from by ring,
