      show (θ0 + θ1 + θ2) - θ2 - (θ0 + θ1 + θ2) = -θ2 from by ring,
      show θ0 + θ1 + θ2 - (θ0 + θ1 + θ2) = 0 from by ring,
      Real.sin_sub_two_pi, Real.sin_neg, Real.sin_zero] at hs
    linarith
  · -- rotate by ψ₀ = θ0
    have hs := sum_sin_of_closure hcl θ0
    rw [show θ0 - θ0 = 0 from by ring,
      show θ0 + θ1 - θ0 = θ1 from by ring,
      show θ0 + θ1 + θ2 - θ0 = 2 * π - θ0 from by linarith,
      Real.sin_zero, Real.sin_two_pi_sub] at hs
    linarith
  · -- rotate by ψ₁ = θ0 + θ1
    have hs := sum_sin_of_closure hcl (θ0 + θ1)
    rw [show θ0 - (θ0 + θ1) = -θ1 from by ring,
      show θ0 + θ1 - (θ0 + θ1) = 0 from by ring,
      show θ0 + θ1 + θ2 - (θ0 + θ1) = θ2 from by ring,
      Real.sin_neg, Real.sin_zero] at hs
    linarith

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.sum_sin_of_closure
lean.code:
theorem sum_sin_of_closure {l₀ l₁ l₂ ψ₀ ψ₁ ψ₂ : ℝ}
    (h : (l₀ : ℂ) * Complex.exp (ψ₀ * Complex.I) + l₁ * Complex.exp (ψ₁ * Complex.I) +
      l₂ * Complex.exp (ψ₂ * Complex.I) = 0) (φ : ℝ) :
    l₀ * sin (ψ₀ - φ) + l₁ * sin (ψ₁ - φ) + l₂ * sin (ψ₂ - φ) = 0 := by
  have h2 := congrArg (fun z => (z * Complex.exp (-(φ : ℂ) * Complex.I)).im) h
  simp only [add_mul, mul_assoc, ← Complex.exp_add, zero_mul, Complex.zero_im] at h2
  have e : ∀ ψ : ℝ, (ψ : ℂ) * Complex.I + -(φ : ℂ) * Complex.I =
      ((ψ - φ : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I := by
    intro ψ; push_cast; ring
  rw [e ψ₀, e ψ₁, e ψ₂] at h2
  simp only [Complex.add_im, Complex.mul_im, Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im, zero_mul,
    add_zero, Complex.exp_ofReal_mul_I_im] at h2
  exact h2

blocks.tex:
The closure gap is
  $E = \ell_0 e^{i\psi_0} + \ell_1 e^{i\psi_1} + \ell_2 e^{i\psi_2} = 0$
  with $\psi_0 = \theta_0$, $\psi_1 = \theta_0 + \theta_1$,
  $\psi_2 = \theta_0 + \theta_1 + \theta_2 = 2\pi$. Three rotations of this
  single equation give the three identities, one imaginary part each:
  \begin{itemize}
  \item $\mathrm{Im}(E) = \ell_0\sin\theta_0 +
    \ell_1\sin(\theta_0{+}\theta_1) + \ell_2\sin 2\pi = 0$, and
    $\sin(\theta_0{+}\theta_1) = \sin(2\pi - \theta_2) = -\sin\theta_2$,
    giving $\ell_0\sin\theta_0 = \ell_1\sin\theta_2$;
  \item $\mathrm{Im}(e^{-i\psi_0}E) = \ell_1\sin\theta_1 +
    \ell_2\sin(2\pi - \theta_0) = \ell_1\sin\theta_1 - \ell_2\sin\theta_0
    = 0$;
  \item $\mathrm{Im}(e^{-i\psi_1}E) = -\ell_0\sin\theta_1 +
    \ell_2\sin\theta_2 = 0$ (using $\psi_2 - \psi_1 = \theta_2$ and
    $\psi_0 - \psi_1 = -\theta_1$).
  \end{itemize}

blocks.label: lem:chord_eq_dist
blocks.title: the vertex chord is the opposite edge
blocks.body: At $n = 3$: $m_i = \ell_{i+1}$ for every $i \in \mathbb{Z}/3$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.sq_eq_of_closure
lean.code:
theorem sq_eq_of_closure {l₀ l₁ l₂ ψ₀ ψ₁ ψ₂ : ℝ}
    (h : (l₀ : ℂ) * Complex.exp (ψ₀ * Complex.I) + l₁ * Complex.exp (ψ₁ * Complex.I) +
      l₂ * Complex.exp (ψ₂ * Complex.I) = 0) :
    l₁ ^ 2 = l₀ ^ 2 + l₂ ^ 2 + 2 * l₀ * l₂ * cos (ψ₀ - ψ₂) := by
  have h1 : (l₁ : ℂ) * Complex.exp (ψ₁ * Complex.I) =
      -((l₀ : ℂ) * Complex.exp (ψ₀ * Complex.I) + l₂ * Complex.exp (ψ₂ * Complex.I)) := by
    linear_combination h
  have h2 := congrArg Complex.normSq h1
  rw [Complex.normSq_neg, Complex.normSq_add, Complex.normSq_mul, Complex.normSq_mul,
    Complex.normSq_mul] at h2
  simp only [Complex.normSq_ofReal] at h2
  have habs : ∀ ψ : ℝ, Complex.normSq (Complex.exp (ψ * Complex.I)) = 1 := by
    intro ψ
    rw [Complex.normSq_apply, Complex.exp_ofReal_mul_I_re, Complex.exp_ofReal_mul_I_im]
    linear_combination cos_sq_add_sin_sq ψ
  rw [habs, habs, habs] at h2
  have harg : ((ψ₀ : ℂ)) * Complex.I + ((-ψ₂ : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I =
      ((ψ₀ - ψ₂ : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I := by
    push_cast; ring
  have hre : ((l₀ : ℂ) * Complex.exp (ψ₀ * Complex.I) *
      (starRingEnd ℂ) ((l₂ : ℂ) * Complex.exp (ψ₂ * Complex.I))).re =
      l₀ * l₂ * cos (ψ₀ - ψ₂) := by
    rw [map_mul, ← Complex.exp_conj]
    have hconj : (starRingEnd ℂ) ((ψ₂ : ℂ) * Complex.I) = ((-ψ₂ : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I := by
      simp [Complex.conj_ofReal]
    rw [hconj, Complex.conj_ofReal]
    have hprod : (l₀ : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((ψ₀ : ℂ) * Complex.I) *
        ((l₂ : ℂ) * Complex.exp (((-ψ₂ : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) =
        ((l₀ * l₂ : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.exp (((ψ₀ - ψ₂ : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) := by
      rw [← harg, Complex.exp_add]
      push_cast
      ring
    rw [hprod, Complex.mul_re, Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im,
      Complex.exp_ofReal_mul_I_re, Complex.exp_ofReal_mul_I_im]
    ring
  rw [hre] at h2
  nlinarith [h2]

/-! ## The killer profile -/

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.triangle_chord_eq_opposite
lean.code:
theorem triangle_chord_eq_opposite {κ ℓ : ZMod 3 → ℝ} (h : ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ)
    (hE : closureGap κ ℓ = 0) (hT : turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * π) (i : ZMod 3) :
    vertexChord κ ℓ i = ℓ (i + 1) := by
  set θ0 := turningAngle 0 κ ℓ 0 with hθ0
  set θ1 := turningAngle 0 κ ℓ 1 with hθ1
  set θ2 := turningAngle 0 κ ℓ 2 with hθ2
  have hsum : θ0 + θ1 + θ2 = 2 * π := by
    rw [hθ0, hθ1, hθ2, ← sum_zmod3 (turningAngle 0 κ ℓ)]
    exact hT
  have hcl := triangle_closure hE
  have key : ∀ j : ZMod 3,
      ℓ (j - 1) ^ 2 + ℓ j ^ 2 + 2 * ℓ (j - 1) * ℓ j * cos (turningAngle 0 κ ℓ j) =
        ℓ (j + 1) ^ 2 := by
    intro j
    rcases zmod3_cases j with rfl | rfl | rfl
    · -- vertex 0: chord ℓ₂,ℓ₀ ↦ opposite ℓ₁
      have hsq := sq_eq_of_closure hcl
      rw [show θ0 - (θ0 + θ1 + θ2) = θ0 - 2 * π from by rw [hsum],
        Real.cos_sub_two_pi] at hsq
      rw [show (0 : ZMod 3) - 1 = 2 from by decide,
        show (0 : ZMod 3) + 1 = 1 from by decide, ← hθ0]
      linarith [hsq]
    · -- vertex 1: chord ℓ₀,ℓ₁ ↦ opposite ℓ₂
      have hcl' : (ℓ 1 : ℂ) *
          Complex.exp ((θ0 + θ1 : ℝ) * Complex.I) +
          (ℓ 2 : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((θ0 + θ1 + θ2 : ℝ) * Complex.I) +
          (ℓ 0 : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((θ0 : ℝ) * Complex.I) = 0 := by
        linear_combination hcl
      have hsq := sq_eq_of_closure hcl'
      rw [show θ0 + θ1 - θ0 = θ1 from by ring] at hsq
      rw [show (1 : ZMod 3) - 1 = 0 from by decide,
        show (1 : ZMod 3) + 1 = 2 from by decide, ← hθ1]
      linarith [hsq]
    · -- vertex 2: chord ℓ₁,ℓ₂ ↦ opposite ℓ₀
      have hcl' : (ℓ 2 : ℂ) *
          Complex.exp ((θ0 + θ1 + θ2 : ℝ) * Complex.I) +
          (ℓ 0 : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((θ0 : ℝ) * Complex.I) +
          (ℓ 1 : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((θ0 + θ1 : ℝ) * Complex.I) = 0 := by
        linear_combination hcl
      have hsq := sq_eq_of_closure hcl'
      rw [show θ0 + θ1 + θ2 - (θ0 + θ1) = θ2 from by ring] at hsq
      rw [show (2 : ZMod 3) - 1 = 1 from by decide,
        show (2 : ZMod 3) + 1 = 0 from by decide, ← hθ2]
      linarith [hsq]
  rw [vertexChord, key i, sqrt_sq (h.length_pos (i + 1)).le]

blocks.tex:
By closure the third edge vector is minus the sum of the other two:
  $\ell_{i+1} e^{i\psi_{i+1}} = -(\ell_{i-1}e^{i\psi_{i-1}} +
  \ell_i e^{i\psi_i})$ (indices mod $3$; the three edges are all of them).
  Taking norms and using $\psi_i - \psi_{i-1} = \theta_i$:
  $\ell_{i+1}^2 = \ell_{i-1}^2 + \ell_i^2 +
  2\ell_{i-1}\ell_i\cos\theta_i = m_i^2$, and both are nonnegative
  ($\ell_{i+1} > 0$, $m_i \ge 0$), so $m_i = \ell_{i+1}$.

The entire content reduces to the already-proven Menger chord identity
\cref{lem:menger_chord_identity} ($\kappa_i m_i = 2\sin\theta_i$) together with
the elementary fact that the signed twice-area of the triple is
$\ell_{i-1}\ell_i\sin\theta_i$. No arcsin branch analysis and no circle
geometry are needed downstream; that is the point of routing everything through
the chord identity.

blocks.title: Signed Menger curvature of a planar triple

blocks.label: def:cross_r2
blocks.title: signed twice-area
blocks.body:
For $A, B, C \in \mathbb{C}$ set
  \[
    \Delta(A,B,C) \;=\; \operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{(B-A)}\,(C-A)\bigr)
      \;=\; (B-A) \times (C-A),
  \]
  the $z$-component of the cross product; $\Delta = 2\cdot(\text{signed area
  of the oriented triangle } ABC)$, positive when $A,B,C$ turn left.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.crossR2
lean.code:
def crossR2 (A B C : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  (B - A).re * (C - A).im - (B - A).im * (C - A).re

blocks.label: def:signed_menger_r2
blocks.title: signed Menger curvature
blocks.body:
For $A,B,C \in \mathbb{C}$ with pairwise distinct entries, the
  \emph{signed Menger curvature} of the ordered triple is
  \[
    \operatorname{sMenger}(A,B,C)
      \;=\; \frac{2\,\Delta(A,B,C)}
                 {|B-A|\,|C-B|\,|A-C|}.
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.signedMengerR2
lean.code:
noncomputable def signedMengerR2 (A B C : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  2 * crossR2 A B C / (dist A B * dist B C * dist C A)

blocks.label: lem:smenger_invariant
blocks.title: isometry invariance
blocks.body:
$\operatorname{sMenger}$ is invariant under translation
  ($\operatorname{sMenger}(A+w, B+w, C+w) = \operatorname{sMenger}(A,B,C)$) and
  under rotation by any unit complex number $u$
  ($\operatorname{sMenger}(uA, uB, uC) = \operatorname{sMenger}(A,B,C)$).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.signedMengerR2_add_left
lean.code:
lemma signedMengerR2_add_left (A B C w : ℂ) :
    signedMengerR2 (A + w) (B + w) (C + w) = signedMengerR2 A B C := by
  simp only [signedMengerR2, crossR2_add_left, dist_add_right]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.dist_mul_left_unit
lean.code:
lemma dist_mul_left_unit {u : ℂ} (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) (A B : ℂ) :
    dist (u * A) (u * B) = dist A B := by
  rw [dist_eq_norm, dist_eq_norm, ← mul_sub, norm_mul, hu, one_mul]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.crossR2_rotate
lean.code:
lemma crossR2_rotate {u : ℂ} (hu : u.re ^ 2 + u.im ^ 2 = 1) (A B C : ℂ) :
    crossR2 (u * A) (u * B) (u * C) = crossR2 A B C := by
  have h1 : u * B - u * A = u * (B - A) := by ring
  have h2 : u * C - u * A = u * (C - A) := by ring
  simp only [crossR2, h1, h2, Complex.mul_re, Complex.mul_im]
  linear_combination ((B - A).re * (C - A).im - (B - A).im * (C - A).re) * hu

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.crossR2_add_left
lean.code:
lemma crossR2_add_left (A B C w : ℂ) :
    crossR2 (A + w) (B + w) (C + w) = crossR2 A B C := by
  have h1 : B + w - (A + w) = B - A := by ring
  have h2 : C + w - (A + w) = C - A := by ring
  simp only [crossR2, h1, h2]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.signedMengerR2_rotate
lean.code:
lemma signedMengerR2_rotate {u : ℂ} (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) (A B C : ℂ) :
    signedMengerR2 (u * A) (u * B) (u * C) = signedMengerR2 A B C := by
  have hu2 : u.re ^ 2 + u.im ^ 2 = 1 := by
    have h := Complex.norm_eq_sqrt_sq_add_sq u
    rw [hu] at h
    have h2 := congrArg (· ^ 2) h.symm
    rwa [Real.sq_sqrt (by positivity), one_pow] at h2
  simp only [signedMengerR2, crossR2_rotate hu2, dist_mul_left_unit hu]

/-! ## Tangent–chord identity -/

variable {n : ℕ}

blocks.tex:
Translation cancels in every difference $B-A$, etc. For rotation by $|u|=1$:
  each difference scales by $u$, so $\Delta$ scales by $|u|^2 = 1$ (the cross
  product of $u(B-A), u(C-A)$ is $|u|^2$ times that of $B-A, C-A$) and each
  chord length is unchanged.

blocks.title: The tangent--chord law and the Menger bridge
remark
blocks.body:
(TC) is the Euclidean inscribed-angle theorem in disguise: $\omega$ is the angle
between the chord of length $\ell_i$ and the circle tangent at its endpoint, and
$\sin\omega = \kappa_i\ell_i/2 = (\ell_i/2)/R$. On $S^2/H^2$ the constant-angle
loci are not cycles (Lexell) and only the $t_K$-form survives; that is the
content deferred to the later geometries. Here (TC) is definitional because the
development is built from the arcsin terms directly.

blocks.label: thm:smenger_development
blocks.title: Euclidean Menger bridge, D2
blocks.body:
Let $\mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell$. For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the
  signed Menger curvature of the three consecutive developed vertices equals the
  target curvature at the middle vertex:
  \[
    \operatorname{sMenger}\bigl(v_k,\; v_{k+1},\; v_{k+2}\bigr)
      \;=\; \kappa_{(k+1 \bmod n)} .
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.signedMengerR2_development
lean.code:
theorem signedMengerR2_development {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (h : ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ)
    (k : ℕ) :
    signedMengerR2 (vertexR2 κ ℓ k) (vertexR2 κ ℓ (k + 1))
        (vertexR2 κ ℓ (k + 1 + 1)) = κ ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n) := by
  -- the two edge vectors of the middle triple
  have hu : vertexR2 κ ℓ (k + 1) - vertexR2 κ ℓ k
      = (ℓ (k : ZMod n) : ℂ)
          * Complex.exp ((heading κ ℓ k : ℂ) * Complex.I) := by
    rw [vertexR2_succ]; ring
  have hw : vertexR2 κ ℓ (k + 1 + 1) - vertexR2 κ ℓ (k + 1)
      = (ℓ ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n) : ℂ)
          * Complex.exp ((heading κ ℓ (k + 1) : ℂ) * Complex.I) := by
    rw [vertexR2_succ]; ring
  set i : ZMod n := ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n) with hi
  set a : ℝ := ℓ (k : ZMod n) with ha
  set b : ℝ := ℓ i with hb
  set α : ℝ := heading κ ℓ k with hαd
  set β : ℝ := heading κ ℓ (k + 1) with hβd
  set θ : ℝ := turningAngle 0 κ ℓ i with hθd
  rw [signedMengerR2_of_diffs hu hw]
  -- turning-angle relation β - α = θ
  have hθ : β - α = θ := by
    rw [hβd, heading_succ, ← hi, ← hθd, ← hαd]; ring
  -- edge components and norms
  rw [edge_re, edge_im, edge_re, edge_im]
  have hapos : 0 < a := h.length_pos (k : ZMod n)
  have hbpos : 0 < b := h.length_pos i
  -- the third side is the vertex chord
  have hnorm : ‖(a : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((α : ℂ) * Complex.I)
      + (b : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((β : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ = vertexChord κ ℓ i := by
    rw [Complex.norm_eq_sqrt_sq_add_sq, vertexChord]
    congr 1
    have hi1 : i - 1 = (k : ZMod n) := by rw [hi]; push_cast; ring
    simp only [Complex.add_re, Complex.add_im, edge_re, edge_im]
    rw [hi1, ← ha, ← hb, ← hθd, ← hθ, Real.cos_sub]
    linear_combination a ^ 2 * Real.sin_sq_add_cos_sq α
      + b ^ 2 * Real.sin_sq_add_cos_sq β
  rw [edge_norm, edge_norm, abs_of_pos hapos, abs_of_pos hbpos, hnorm]
  -- final algebra through the Menger chord identity
  have hmenger : κ i * vertexChord κ ℓ i = 2 * Real.sin θ := by
    have := menger_chord_identity h i
    rwa [← hθd] at this
  have hvc := vertexChord_pos h i
  have hnum : a * Real.cos α * (b * Real.sin β) - a * Real.sin α * (b * Real.cos β)
      = a * b * Real.sin θ := by
    rw [← hθ, Real.sin_sub]; ring
  rw [hnum, show 2 * (a * b * Real.sin θ) = a * b * (2 * Real.sin θ) from by ring,
    ← hmenger]
  have ha0 : a ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hapos
  have hb0 : b ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hbpos
  have hvc0 : vertexChord κ ℓ i ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hvc
  field_simp

/-! ## Menger realizability and the forward bridge -/

blocks.tex:
Write $i = k+1 \bmod n$ for the middle index. By the one-step recurrence
  (\cref{lem:development_recurrences}) the two edge vectors are
  $B - A = v_{k+1} - v_k = \ell_k\, e^{i\psi_k}$ and
  $C - B = v_{k+2} - v_{k+1} = \ell_{k+1}\, e^{i\psi_{k+1}}$, with headings
  differing by the turning angle $\psi_{k+1} - \psi_k = \theta_{i}$. The third
  side is $C - A = (B-A) + (C-B)$, whose length is exactly the vertex chord
  $m_i = |C-A|$ of \cref{def:vertex_chord} (the norm computation is the remark
  after that definition). The signed twice-area is
  \[
    \Delta(A,B,C) = (B-A)\times(C-A) = (B-A)\times(C-B)
      = \ell_k\,\ell_{k+1}\,\sin\theta_i
  \]
  (translation invariance kills the common term; the cross product of two
  vectors of lengths $\ell_k, \ell_{k+1}$ at angle $\theta_i$). Hence
  \[
    \operatorname{sMenger}(A,B,C)
      = \frac{2\,\ell_k\ell_{k+1}\sin\theta_i}
             {\ell_k\,\ell_{k+1}\,m_i}
      = \frac{2\sin\theta_i}{m_i}
      = \kappa_i
  \]
  where the last step is the Menger chord identity
  \cref{lem:menger_chord_identity} ($\kappa_i m_i = 2\sin\theta_i$), dividing by
  $m_i > 0$ (the chord is positive since $\ell_k, \ell_{k+1} > 0$ and the edges
  are not anti-parallel, $|\theta_i| < \pi$). Isometry invariance
  (\cref{lem:smenger_invariant}) is what lets the computation be carried out on
  the raw edge vectors rather than on the absolute vertex positions.

blocks.title: Menger realizability and the forward bridge

blocks.label: def:realizes_menger
blocks.title: signed-Menger realizability
blocks.body:
For $\kappa\colon\mathbb{Z}/n\to\mathbb{R}$ (with $3 \le n$),
  $\mathrm{RealizesMenger}\,\kappa$ holds when there is a simple closed polygon
  $v\colon\mathbb{Z}/n\to\mathbb{C}$ with
  $\operatorname{sMenger}(v_{i-1}, v_i, v_{i+1}) = \kappa_i$ for every
  $i\in\mathbb{Z}/n$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RealizesMenger

blocks.label: lem:vertex_eq_polygon
blocks.title: the development read at any natural index
blocks.body:
If $E(\kappa,\ell) = 0$ and $T(\kappa,\ell) = 2\pi$, then for every
  $j \in \mathbb{N}$ the developed vertex $v_j$ agrees with the cyclic polygon
  at the reduced index: $v_j = P(\kappa,\ell)(\overline{j})
  = v_{(\overline{j}).\mathrm{val}}$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.vertexR2_eq_polygon
lean.code:
lemma vertexR2_eq_polygon [NeZero n] {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (hE : closureGap κ ℓ = 0) (hT : turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * Real.pi) (m : ℕ) :
    vertexR2 κ ℓ m = polygonR2 κ ℓ (m : ZMod n) := by
  rw [polygonR2, ZMod.val_natCast]
  conv_lhs => rw [← Nat.mod_add_div m n]
  exact vertexR2_add_mul_n hE hT (m % n) (m / n)

blocks.tex:
Write $j = (j \bmod n) + n\,(j \div n)$. Iterating the period identity
  $v_{k+n} = v_k$ of \cref{lem:development_periodic} exactly $j \div n$ times
  gives $v_j = v_{j \bmod n}$, and $(\overline{j}).\mathrm{val} = j \bmod n$ is
  the definition of the reduction.

Fix $n \ge 3$ and a moderate-arc profile $(\kappa, \ell)$ over $\ZMod n$ with all
$\kappa_i > 0$, whose Euclidean development \emph{closes} with total turning
$2\pi$: $\mathrm{closureGap}(\kappa, \ell) = 0$ and
$\mathrm{turningSum}(\kappa, \ell) = 2\pi$. Write $P_k = \mathrm{vertexR2}\,
\kappa\,\ell\,k$ for the developed vertices and $\psi_k = \mathrm{heading}\,
\kappa\,\ell\,k$ for the cumulative headings, so that the edge from $P_k$ to
$P_{k+1}$ is $\ell_k e^{i\psi_k}$ and consecutive headings differ by the turning
angle $\psi_k - \psi_{k-1} = \theta_k \in (0, \pi)$
(\cref{lem:turning_angle_sign,lem:turning_angle_lt_pi}, using $\kappa_i > 0$).

The goal is
\[
  \mathrm{IsSimplePolygon}(\mathrm{polygonR2}\,\kappa\,\ell).
\]
The mechanism is the classical one: because the edge directions $e^{i\psi_k}$
rotate \emph{strictly monotonically} through exactly one full turn, the polygon
bounds a convex region and is therefore simple. Concretely we prove a
\emph{support half-plane} statement — every vertex lies weakly to the left of
each directed edge line, strictly so unless it is one of that edge's two
endpoints — and read off the three clauses of $\mathrm{IsSimplePolygon}$ from it.

blocks.title: formalization notes
blocks.body:
Mathlib has no simple-polygonal-curve theory, so the support-halfplane proof is
  from-scratch (confirmed by the api-alignment consult,
  \texttt{analogies/discrete-convex-simple.md}). Recommended idioms: for
  \cref{lem:nonadjacent_disjoint}, obtain each open half-plane as
  \texttt{Convex} via \texttt{convex\_halfSpace\_gt} and push the segment inside
  with \texttt{Convex.segment\_subset}; the partial-sum unimodality of
  \cref{lem:support_halfplane} is a manual \texttt{Finset.sum} induction (split
  the range at the $\pi$-crossing index $p$, monotone up then monotone down). All
  chords/directions are in $\mathbb{C}$; use $\mathrm{Im}(e^{-i\psi}\,\cdot)$ for
  the left-distance functional.

blocks.label: lem:heading_strict_mono
blocks.title: single-step heading increase
blocks.body:
If $\kappa_i > 0$ for all $i$ and $(\kappa,\ell)$ is moderate-arc, then
  $\psi_j < \psi_{j+1}$ for every $j$, since
  $\psi_{j+1} - \psi_j = \theta_{(j+1 \bmod n)} > 0$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.heading_lt_succ
lean.code:
lemma heading_lt_succ {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (h : ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ)
    (hκ : ∀ i : ZMod n, 0 < κ i) (j : ℕ) :
    heading κ ℓ j < heading κ ℓ (j + 1) := by
  rw [heading_succ']
  have := turningAngle_pos h (hκ ((j + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n))
  linarith

blocks.tex:
By definition $\psi_{j+1} - \psi_j = \mathrm{turningAngle}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell\,
  ((j+1 : \mathbb{N}) : \ZMod n)$, which is positive by
  \cref{lem:turning_angle_sign} applied with $\kappa_{(j+1)} > 0$ on the
  moderate-arc domain.

blocks.label: lem:heading_strict_mono_global
blocks.title: strict monotonicity of headings
blocks.body:
Under the same hypotheses, $\mathrm{heading}\,\kappa\,\ell$ is strictly
  increasing on $\mathbb{N}$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.heading_strictMono
lean.code:
lemma heading_strictMono {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (h : ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ)
    (hκ : ∀ i : ZMod n, 0 < κ i) : StrictMono (heading κ ℓ) :=
  strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ (heading_lt_succ h hκ)

blocks.tex:
Iterate \cref{lem:heading_strict_mono}: a sequence with every step strictly
  increasing is strictly monotone.

blocks.label: lem:heading_window
blocks.title: heading window bounds
blocks.body:
Under the hypotheses of \cref{lem:heading_strict_mono} together with
  $\mathrm{turningSum}(\kappa,\ell) = 2\pi$: for all $j$,
  $\psi_{j+n} = \psi_j + 2\pi$, and for $j < k < j+n$ one has the strict window
  bound
  \[
    \psi_j \;<\; \psi_k \;<\; \psi_j + 2\pi .
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.heading_sub_lt_two_pi
lean.code:
lemma heading_sub_lt_two_pi [NeZero n] {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (h : ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ)
    (hκ : ∀ i : ZMod n, 0 < κ i) (hT : turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * Real.pi)
    {j k : ℕ} (hjk : j < k) (hkn : k < j + n) :
    heading κ ℓ j < heading κ ℓ k ∧ heading κ ℓ k < heading κ ℓ j + 2 * Real.pi := by
  refine ⟨heading_strictMono h hκ hjk, ?_⟩
  have := heading_strictMono h hκ hkn
  rwa [heading_add_n hT] at this

/-! ## The support half-plane -/

blocks.tex:
The period jump $\psi_{j+n} = \psi_j + 2\pi$ is the lemma
  \texttt{heading\_add\_n} (\cref{lem:development_recurrences}, already proven in
  \cref{chap:discrete_defs}, using $\mathrm{turningSum} = 2\pi$). The lower bound
  $\psi_j < \psi_k$ is \cref{lem:heading_strict_mono}; the upper bound
  $\psi_k < \psi_{j+n} = \psi_j + 2\pi$ is the same monotonicity applied to
  $k < j+n$.

For a directed edge with heading $\psi_k$, the signed distance of a point $z$ to
the \emph{left} of the edge line through $P_k$ is
$\mathrm{Im}\!\left(e^{-i\psi_k}(z - P_k)\right)$.

blocks.label: lem:left_distance_formula
blocks.title: left-distance telescoping
blocks.body:
For $k \le j$,
  \[
    \mathrm{Im}\!\left(e^{-i\psi_k}(P_j - P_k)\right)
      \;=\; \sum_{m=k}^{j-1} \ell_m \,\sin(\psi_m - \psi_k).
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.im_rot_vertex_sub
lean.code:
lemma im_rot_vertex_sub (κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ) {k j : ℕ} (hkj : k ≤ j) :
    (Complex.exp (((-heading κ ℓ k : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
        * (vertexR2 κ ℓ j - vertexR2 κ ℓ k)).im
      = ∑ m ∈ Finset.Ico k j,
          ℓ (m : ZMod n) * Real.sin (heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k) := by
  have hdiff : vertexR2 κ ℓ j - vertexR2 κ ℓ k
      = ∑ m ∈ Finset.Ico k j,
          (ℓ (m : ZMod n) : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((heading κ ℓ m : ℂ) * Complex.I) := by
    rw [vertexR2, vertexR2, ← Finset.sum_Ico_eq_sub _ hkj]
  rw [hdiff, Finset.mul_sum, Complex.im_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun m _ => ?_
  have hexp : Complex.exp (((-heading κ ℓ k : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
        * ((ℓ (m : ZMod n) : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((heading κ ℓ m : ℂ) * Complex.I))
      = (ℓ (m : ZMod n) : ℂ)
          * Complex.exp (((heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) := by
    rw [mul_left_comm, ← Complex.exp_add]
    congr 1
    push_cast
    ring_nf
  rw [hexp, Complex.mul_im, Complex.exp_ofReal_mul_I_re, Complex.exp_ofReal_mul_I_im,
    Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im]
  ring

blocks.tex:
$P_j - P_k = \sum_{m=k}^{j-1} \ell_m e^{i\psi_m}$ by the development
  recurrence \texttt{vertexR2\_succ} (telescoping $\mathrm{vertexR2}$ over
  $[k, j)$). Multiply by $e^{-i\psi_k}$ and take imaginary parts:
  $\mathrm{Im}\!\left(\ell_m e^{i(\psi_m - \psi_k)}\right)
    = \ell_m \sin(\psi_m - \psi_k)$.

blocks.label: lem:support_halfplane
blocks.title: support half-plane
blocks.body:
Assume all $\kappa_i > 0$, $(\kappa,\ell)$ moderate-arc, $\mathrm{closureGap} =
  0$, $\mathrm{turningSum} = 2\pi$. Fix an edge index $k$ and let
  $S(j) := \mathrm{Im}\!\left(e^{-i\psi_k}(P_j - P_k)\right)$ for
  $k \le j \le k+n$. Then $S(j) \ge 0$ for all such $j$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.support_left_nonneg
lean.code:
lemma support_left_nonneg [NeZero n] {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (h : ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ)
    (hκ : ∀ i : ZMod n, 0 < κ i) (hE : closureGap κ ℓ = 0)
    (hT : turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * Real.pi) (k : ℕ) {j : ℕ}
    (hkj : k ≤ j) (hjn : j ≤ k + n) :
    0 ≤ (Complex.exp (((-heading κ ℓ k : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
          * (vertexR2 κ ℓ j - vertexR2 κ ℓ k)).im := by
  rw [im_rot_vertex_sub κ ℓ hkj]
  have hmono := heading_strictMono h hκ
  -- backward representation via closure: ∑_{[k,j)} = −∑_{[j,k+n)}
  have hzero : ∑ m ∈ Finset.Ico k (k + n),
      ℓ (m : ZMod n) * Real.sin (heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k) = 0 := by
    have H := im_rot_vertex_sub κ ℓ (Nat.le_add_right k n)
    rw [vertexR2_add_n hE hT k, sub_self, mul_zero, Complex.zero_im] at H
    exact H.symm
  have hsplit : ∑ m ∈ Finset.Ico k j,
        ℓ (m : ZMod n) * Real.sin (heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k)
      = -∑ m ∈ Finset.Ico j (k + n),
          ℓ (m : ZMod n) * Real.sin (heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k) := by
    have hc := Finset.sum_Ico_consecutive
      (fun m => ℓ (m : ZMod n) * Real.sin (heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k)) hkj hjn
    rw [hzero] at hc
    linarith
  by_cases hcross : ∀ m ∈ Finset.Ico k j, heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k ≤ Real.pi
  · -- forward: every increment is nonnegative
    apply Finset.sum_nonneg
    intro m hm
    rw [Finset.mem_Ico] at hm
    have hαnn : 0 ≤ heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k :=
      sub_nonneg.2 (hmono.monotone hm.1)
    exact mul_nonneg (h.length_pos _).le
      (Real.sin_nonneg_of_nonneg_of_le_pi hαnn (hcross m (Finset.mem_Ico.2 hm)))
  · -- backward: past the π-crossing every increment is nonpositive
    push Not at hcross
    obtain ⟨m₀, hm₀mem, hm₀⟩ := hcross
    rw [Finset.mem_Ico] at hm₀mem
    rw [hsplit, neg_nonneg]
    apply Finset.sum_nonpos
    intro m hm
    rw [Finset.mem_Ico] at hm
    have hm₀m : m₀ < m := lt_of_lt_of_le hm₀mem.2 hm.1
    have hαgt : Real.pi < heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k := by
      have := hmono hm₀m; linarith
    have hkm : k < m := lt_of_le_of_lt hm₀mem.1 hm₀m
    have hwin := heading_sub_lt_two_pi h hκ hT hkm hm.2
    have : Real.sin (heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k) < 0 :=
      sin_neg_of_pi_lt hαgt (by linarith [hwin.2])
    exact mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (h.length_pos _).le this.le

blocks.tex:
Put $\alpha_m := \psi_m - \psi_k$ for $k \le m \le k+n$, so by
  \cref{lem:heading_window} the $\alpha_m$ are strictly increasing with
  $\alpha_k = 0$ and $\alpha_{k+n} = 2\pi$, and $\alpha_m \in (0, 2\pi)$ for
  $k < m < k+n$. By \cref{lem:left_distance_formula},
  $S(j) = \sum_{m=k}^{j-1} \ell_m \sin\alpha_m$, a partial sum with increments
  $\ell_m \sin\alpha_m$ (recall $\ell_m > 0$). The increment is
  \emph{positive} when $\alpha_m \in (0, \pi)$ and \emph{negative} when
  $\alpha_m \in (\pi, 2\pi)$. Because $\alpha_m$ crosses $\pi$ exactly once (it
  is strictly increasing from $0$ to $2\pi$), let $p$ be the largest index with
  $\alpha_p < \pi$. Then:
  \begin{itemize}
    \item $S(k) = 0$ and $S(k+1) = \ell_k \sin\alpha_k = \ell_k \sin 0 = 0$.
    \item On $k+1 \le j \le p+1$ every increment $\ell_m \sin\alpha_m$
      ($k+1 \le m \le p$) is strictly positive, so $S$ is strictly increasing
      there; hence $S(j) > 0$ for $k+1 < j \le p+1$, and $S$ attains its maximum
      $S_{\max} = S(p+1) > 0$.
    \item On $p+1 \le j \le k+n$ every increment ($p+1 \le m \le k+n-1$, where
      $\alpha_m > \pi$) is strictly negative, so $S$ is strictly decreasing
      there, down to its endpoint value.
    \item The endpoint value is $S(k+n) = \mathrm{Im}\!\left(e^{-i\psi_k}
      (P_{k+n} - P_k)\right) = 0$ because the development closes,
      $P_{k+n} = P_k$ (\cref{lem:development_periodic}), so $P_{k+n} - P_k = 0$.
  \end{itemize}
  A strictly-increasing-then-strictly-decreasing sequence pinned to $0$ at both
  its interior boundary points ($S(k+1) = 0$ on the left of the ascent,
  $S(k+n) = 0$ at the end of the descent) is strictly positive at every strictly
  interior index. Thus $S(j) > 0$ for $k+1 < j < k+n$, and $S(j) \ge 0$
  throughout.

blocks.label: lem:support_halfplane_strict
blocks.title: strict support half-plane
blocks.body:
In the setting of \cref{lem:support_halfplane}, moreover $S(j) > 0$ whenever
  $k+1 < j < k+n$ (strictly, except at $j \in \{k, k+1, k+n\}$, i.e.\ at $P_k$
  and $P_{k+1}$).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.support_left_pos
lean.code:
lemma support_left_pos [NeZero n] {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (h : ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ)
    (hκ : ∀ i : ZMod n, 0 < κ i) (hE : closureGap κ ℓ = 0)
    (hT : turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * Real.pi) (k : ℕ) {j : ℕ}
    (hkj : k + 1 < j) (hjn : j < k + n) :
    0 < (Complex.exp (((-heading κ ℓ k : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
          * (vertexR2 κ ℓ j - vertexR2 κ ℓ k)).im := by
  rw [im_rot_vertex_sub κ ℓ (by omega : k ≤ j)]
  have hmono := heading_strictMono h hκ
  have hzero : ∑ m ∈ Finset.Ico k (k + n),
      ℓ (m : ZMod n) * Real.sin (heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k) = 0 := by
    have H := im_rot_vertex_sub κ ℓ (Nat.le_add_right k n)
    rw [vertexR2_add_n hE hT k, sub_self, mul_zero, Complex.zero_im] at H
    exact H.symm
  have hsplit : ∑ m ∈ Finset.Ico k j,
        ℓ (m : ZMod n) * Real.sin (heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k)
      = -∑ m ∈ Finset.Ico j (k + n),
          ℓ (m : ZMod n) * Real.sin (heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k) := by
    have hc := Finset.sum_Ico_consecutive
      (fun m => ℓ (m : ZMod n) * Real.sin (heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k))
      (by omega : k ≤ j) (by omega : j ≤ k + n)
    rw [hzero] at hc
    linarith
  by_cases hcross : ∀ m ∈ Finset.Ico k j, heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k ≤ Real.pi
  · -- forward: the (k+1) increment is strictly positive, the rest nonnegative
    apply Finset.sum_pos'
    · intro m hm
      rw [Finset.mem_Ico] at hm
      have hαnn : 0 ≤ heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k :=
        sub_nonneg.2 (hmono.monotone hm.1)
      exact mul_nonneg (h.length_pos _).le
        (Real.sin_nonneg_of_nonneg_of_le_pi hαnn (hcross m (Finset.mem_Ico.2 hm)))
    · refine ⟨k + 1, Finset.mem_Ico.2 ⟨Nat.le_add_right k 1, hkj⟩, ?_⟩
      have hstep : heading κ ℓ (k + 1) - heading κ ℓ k
          = turningAngle 0 κ ℓ ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n) := by
        rw [heading_succ']; ring
      have hpos : 0 < turningAngle 0 κ ℓ ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n) :=
        turningAngle_pos h (hκ _)
      have hlt : turningAngle 0 κ ℓ ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n) < Real.pi :=
        lt_of_abs_lt (abs_turningAngle_lt_pi h _)
      rw [hstep]
      exact mul_pos (h.length_pos _)
        (Real.sin_pos_of_pos_of_lt_pi hpos hlt)
  · -- backward: past the π-crossing every increment is strictly negative
    push Not at hcross
    obtain ⟨m₀, hm₀mem, hm₀⟩ := hcross
    rw [Finset.mem_Ico] at hm₀mem
    rw [hsplit, neg_pos]
    apply Finset.sum_neg
    · intro m hm
      rw [Finset.mem_Ico] at hm
      have hm₀m : m₀ < m := lt_of_lt_of_le hm₀mem.2 hm.1
      have hαgt : Real.pi < heading κ ℓ m - heading κ ℓ k := by
        have := hmono hm₀m; linarith
      have hkm : k < m := lt_of_le_of_lt hm₀mem.1 hm₀m
      have hwin := heading_sub_lt_two_pi h hκ hT hkm hm.2
      exact mul_neg_of_pos_of_neg (h.length_pos _)
        (sin_neg_of_pi_lt hαgt (by linarith [hwin.2]))
    · exact ⟨j, Finset.mem_Ico.2 ⟨le_rfl, hjn⟩⟩

/-! ## Simplicity from support -/

blocks.tex:
The strict branches of the same increasing-then-decreasing argument: on the
  ascent every increment is strictly positive from $j = k+1$ on, and on the
  descent every increment is strictly negative down to the endpoint value $0$,
  so every strictly interior index carries a strictly positive value.

blocks.title: remark
blocks.body:
\Cref{lem:support_halfplane} is stated over the lifted range
  $k \le j \le k+n$; since $P_{j+n} = P_j$ and the statement is invariant under
  shifting $j$ by a full period, it transfers to the cyclic vertices
  $\mathrm{polygonR2}\,\kappa\,\ell : \ZMod n \to \mathbb{C}$: for a fixed cyclic
  edge $k$, every cyclic vertex is weakly left of the edge line, strictly so
  unless it is $P_k$ or $P_{k+1}$.

blocks.label: lem:edges_nondegenerate
blocks.title: nondegenerate edges
blocks.body:
Each edge is nondegenerate: $P_i \ne P_{i+1}$ for every $i \in \ZMod n$, since
  $P_{i+1} - P_i = \ell_i e^{i\psi_i}$ has modulus $\ell_i > 0$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.polygonR2_edge_ne
lean.code:
lemma polygonR2_edge_ne [NeZero n] {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (h : ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ)
    (hE : closureGap κ ℓ = 0) (hT : turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * Real.pi) (i : ZMod n) :
    polygonR2 κ ℓ i ≠ polygonR2 κ ℓ (i + 1) := by
  have e1 : polygonR2 κ ℓ (i + 1) = vertexR2 κ ℓ (i.val + 1) := by
    have := polygonR2_add_nat hE hT i 1
    simpa using this
  have hd : vertexR2 κ ℓ (i.val + 1) - vertexR2 κ ℓ i.val
      = (ℓ ((i.val : ℕ) : ZMod n) : ℂ)
          * Complex.exp ((heading κ ℓ i.val : ℂ) * Complex.I) := by
    rw [vertexR2_succ]; ring
  have hne : (ℓ ((i.val : ℕ) : ZMod n) : ℂ)
      * Complex.exp ((heading κ ℓ i.val : ℂ) * Complex.I) ≠ 0 := by
    apply mul_ne_zero _ (Complex.exp_ne_zero _)
    exact_mod_cast ne_of_gt (h.length_pos _)
  rw [show polygonR2 κ ℓ i = vertexR2 κ ℓ i.val from rfl, e1]
  intro heq
  apply hne
  rw [← hd, heq, sub_self]

blocks.label: lem:nonadjacent_disjoint
blocks.title: non-adjacent edges are disjoint
blocks.body:
If $i, j \in \ZMod n$ satisfy $i \ne j$, $i+1 \ne j$, $j + 1 \ne i$, then
  \[
    \mathrm{segment}\,\mathbb{R}\,(P_i)(P_{i+1}) \cap
    \mathrm{segment}\,\mathbb{R}\,(P_j)(P_{j+1}) = \varnothing .
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.polygonR2_nonadjacent_disjoint
lean.code:
lemma polygonR2_nonadjacent_disjoint [NeZero n] {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (h : ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ) (hκ : ∀ i : ZMod n, 0 < κ i) (hE : closureGap κ ℓ = 0)
    (hT : turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * Real.pi) (i j : ZMod n) (hij : i ≠ j)
    (hij1 : i + 1 ≠ j) (hji1 : j + 1 ≠ i) :
    segment ℝ (polygonR2 κ ℓ i) (polygonR2 κ ℓ (i + 1))
        ∩ segment ℝ (polygonR2 κ ℓ j) (polygonR2 κ ℓ (j + 1)) = ∅ := by
  rw [Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
  rintro z ⟨hz1, hz2⟩
  obtain ⟨r, r', hr, hr', hrr, hz1eq⟩ := hz1
  obtain ⟨s, s', hs, hs', hss, hz2eq⟩ := hz2
  -- L(z) computed from the near edge: on the edge line, hence 0
  have hLnear : (Complex.exp (((-heading κ ℓ i.val : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
      * (z - polygonR2 κ ℓ i)).im = 0 := by
    rw [← hz1eq, im_rot_affine _ _ _ _ hrr, sub_self, mul_zero, Complex.zero_im,
      mul_zero, zero_add, im_rot_edge_end_zero hE hT i, mul_zero]
  -- L(z) computed from the far edge: strictly positive
  have hLj : 0 < (Complex.exp (((-heading κ ℓ i.val : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
      * (polygonR2 κ ℓ j - polygonR2 κ ℓ i)).im :=
    support_pos_cyclic h hκ hE hT i j (Ne.symm hij) (Ne.symm hij1)
  have hLj1 : 0 < (Complex.exp (((-heading κ ℓ i.val : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
      * (polygonR2 κ ℓ (j + 1) - polygonR2 κ ℓ i)).im :=
    support_pos_cyclic h hκ hE hT i (j + 1) hji1
      (by intro hcontra; exact hij (by linear_combination -hcontra))
  have hLfar : 0 < (Complex.exp (((-heading κ ℓ i.val : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
      * (z - polygonR2 κ ℓ i)).im := by
    rw [← hz2eq, im_rot_affine _ _ _ _ hss]
    rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hs with hs0 | hspos
    · have hs'1 : s' = 1 := by linarith
      rw [← hs0, zero_mul, zero_add, hs'1, one_mul]; exact hLj1
    · nlinarith [mul_pos hspos hLj, mul_nonneg hs' hLj1.le]
  linarith

blocks.tex:
Fix the directed edge $i$ and its line $L_i = \{z : \mathrm{Im}(e^{-i\psi_i}
  (z - P_i)) = 0\}$. Edge $i$ lies on $L_i$. By \cref{lem:support_halfplane},
  every vertex lies weakly left of $L_i$, and \emph{strictly} left unless it is
  $P_i$ or $P_{i+1}$. Both endpoints $P_j, P_{j+1}$ of the other edge are
  distinct from $P_i$ and $P_{i+1}$ (their indices $j, j+1$ avoid $i, i+1$ by the
  non-adjacency hypotheses), hence both lie strictly left of $L_i$. The segment
  $\mathrm{segment}\,\mathbb{R}\,(P_j)(P_{j+1})$ is the convex hull of two points
  strictly in the open left half-plane $\{\mathrm{Im}(e^{-i\psi_i}(z-P_i)) > 0\}$,
  which is convex, so the whole segment lies strictly left of $L_i$. Edge $i$ is
  contained in $L_i$ (imaginary part $= 0$), so the two segments are disjoint.

blocks.label: lem:consecutive_meet_shared
blocks.title: consecutive edges meet only at the shared vertex
blocks.body:
For every $i$,
  \[
    \mathrm{segment}\,\mathbb{R}\,(P_i)(P_{i+1}) \cap
    \mathrm{segment}\,\mathbb{R}\,(P_{i+1})(P_{i+2}) = \{P_{i+1}\}.
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.polygonR2_consecutive_inter
lean.code:
lemma polygonR2_consecutive_inter [NeZero n] {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (h : ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ) (hκ : ∀ i : ZMod n, 0 < κ i) (hE : closureGap κ ℓ = 0)
    (hT : turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * Real.pi) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (i : ZMod n) :
    segment ℝ (polygonR2 κ ℓ i) (polygonR2 κ ℓ (i + 1))
        ∩ segment ℝ (polygonR2 κ ℓ (i + 1)) (polygonR2 κ ℓ (i + 1 + 1))
      = {polygonR2 κ ℓ (i + 1)} := by
  have hLj2 : 0 < (Complex.exp (((-heading κ ℓ i.val : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
      * (polygonR2 κ ℓ (i + 1 + 1) - polygonR2 κ ℓ i)).im := by
    have e2 : polygonR2 κ ℓ (i + 1 + 1) = vertexR2 κ ℓ (i.val + 2) := by
      have h2 := polygonR2_add_nat hE hT i 2
      rw [show i + ((2 : ℕ) : ZMod n) = i + 1 + 1 from by push_cast; ring] at h2
      exact h2
    rw [e2, show polygonR2 κ ℓ i = vertexR2 κ ℓ i.val from rfl]
    exact support_left_pos h hκ hE hT i.val (by omega) (by omega)
  rw [Set.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem]
  refine ⟨⟨right_mem_segment ℝ _ _, left_mem_segment ℝ _ _⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro z ⟨hz1, hz2⟩
  obtain ⟨r, r', hr, hr', hrr, hz1eq⟩ := hz1
  obtain ⟨s, s', hs, hs', hss, hz2eq⟩ := hz2
  have hLnear : (Complex.exp (((-heading κ ℓ i.val : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
      * (z - polygonR2 κ ℓ i)).im = 0 := by
    rw [← hz1eq, im_rot_affine _ _ _ _ hrr, sub_self, mul_zero, Complex.zero_im,
      mul_zero, zero_add, im_rot_edge_end_zero hE hT i, mul_zero]
  have hLfar : (Complex.exp (((-heading κ ℓ i.val : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
      * (z - polygonR2 κ ℓ i)).im
      = s' * (Complex.exp (((-heading κ ℓ i.val : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
          * (polygonR2 κ ℓ (i + 1 + 1) - polygonR2 κ ℓ i)).im := by
    rw [← hz2eq, im_rot_affine _ _ _ _ hss, im_rot_edge_end_zero hE hT i, mul_zero,
      zero_add]
  have hs'0 : s' = 0 := by
    have hz : s' * (Complex.exp (((-heading κ ℓ i.val : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
        * (polygonR2 κ ℓ (i + 1 + 1) - polygonR2 κ ℓ i)).im = 0 := by
      rw [← hLfar, hLnear]
    exact (mul_eq_zero.1 hz).resolve_right (ne_of_gt hLj2)
  rw [← hz2eq, hs'0, zero_smul, add_zero, show s = 1 from by linarith, one_smul]

blocks.tex:
Both segments contain the shared vertex $P_{i+1}$, giving $\supseteq$. For
  $\subseteq$: translate so $P_{i+1} = 0$. The first segment runs into $0$ along
  direction $-e^{i\psi_i}$, the second leaves $0$ along direction
  $e^{i\psi_{i+1}}$, and $\psi_{i+1} - \psi_i = \theta_{i+1} \in (0, \pi)$ by
  \cref{lem:turning_angle_sign,lem:turning_angle_lt_pi}. A point in both segments
  is a nonnegative multiple of $-e^{i\psi_i}$ and of $e^{i\psi_{i+1}}$
  simultaneously; since these two rays are neither equal nor opposite (their
  angular separation $\pi - \theta_{i+1}$ lies strictly in $(0, \pi)$), the only
  common point is $0 = P_{i+1}$. (Concretely, the left-distance
  $\mathrm{Im}(e^{-i\psi_i} \cdot)$ vanishes on the first ray but is
  $\sin\theta_{i+1} > 0$ times the parameter on the second, forcing that
  parameter to $0$.)

blocks.label: thm:convex_simple
blocks.title: L1: positive turning $\Rightarrow$ simple
blocks.body:
Let $n \ge 3$, $[\mathrm{NeZero}\,n]$, $(\kappa,\ell)$ moderate-arc with
  $\kappa_i > 0$ for all $i$, $\mathrm{closureGap}(\kappa,\ell) = 0$, and
  $\mathrm{turningSum}(\kappa,\ell) = 2\pi$. Then
  $\mathrm{IsSimplePolygon}(\mathrm{polygonR2}\,\kappa\,\ell)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.isSimplePolygon_of_turningPositive
lean.code:
theorem isSimplePolygon_of_turningPositive [NeZero n] {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (hn : 3 ≤ n) (h : ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ) (hκ : ∀ i : ZMod n, 0 < κ i)
    (hE : closureGap κ ℓ = 0) (hT : turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * Real.pi) :
    IsSimplePolygon (polygonR2 κ ℓ) :=
  ⟨fun i => polygonR2_edge_ne h hE hT i,
   fun i => polygonR2_consecutive_inter h hκ hE hT hn i,
   fun i j hij hij1 hji1 => polygonR2_nonadjacent_disjoint h hκ hE hT i j hij hij1 hji1⟩

/-! ## The constant branch of D-R²-pos -/

deps.title: consecutive edges meet only at the shared vertex
deps.label: lem:consecutive_meet_shared

blocks.tex:
The three conjuncts of $\mathrm{IsSimplePolygon}$
  (\cref{def:simple_polygon}) are exactly
  \cref{lem:edges_nondegenerate} (nondegeneracy),
  \cref{lem:consecutive_meet_shared} (consecutive edges), and
  \cref{lem:nonadjacent_disjoint} (non-adjacent edges).

blocks.label: thm:realizesR2_constant
blocks.title: constant positive profiles are realized
blocks.body:
For $n \ge 3$ and $c > 0$, the constant profile $\kappa \equiv c$ satisfies
  $\mathrm{RealizesR2}\,(\lambda\,\_.\,c)$, witnessed by the regular $n$-gon of
  edge length $\tfrac{2}{c}\sin(\pi/n)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.realizesR2_const
lean.code:
theorem realizesR2_const [NeZero n] (hn : 3 ≤ n) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    RealizesR2 (fun _ : ZMod n => c) := by
  obtain ⟨hMA, _, hsum, hclose⟩ := regularGon_closes hn hc
  exact ⟨fun _ => 2 / c * Real.sin (Real.pi / n), hMA, hclose, hsum,
    isSimplePolygon_of_turningPositive hn hMA (fun _ => hc) hclose hsum⟩

deps.title: regular polygon closes the constant profile
deps.label: lem:regular_gon_closes

blocks.tex:
\Cref{lem:regular_gon_closes} supplies the witness $\ell \equiv \tfrac{2}{c}
  \sin(\pi/n)$ and discharges three of the four $\mathrm{RealizesR2}$ conjuncts:
  moderate-arc, $\mathrm{closureGap} = 0$, and $\mathrm{turningSum} = 2\pi$
  (each turning angle equals $2\pi/n$, so their sum is $2\pi$). The remaining
  conjunct $\mathrm{IsSimplePolygon}(\mathrm{polygonR2}\,(\lambda\_.c)\,\ell)$ is
  \cref{thm:convex_simple}, whose hypotheses hold: $\kappa \equiv c > 0$ is
  positive, and the closure/turning facts are those just quoted. Thus all four
  conjuncts hold.
Coherence requires the circumcenter of each consecutive vertex triple to lie in its open vertex cone. The moderate-arc identities below imply this geometric condition.

blocks.label: def:circumcenter_r2
blocks.title: circumcenter of a plane triple
blocks.body:
\textit{Source: Dahlberg, discrete circle of curvature $\rho(P)$, p.~2.}
  For $p, q, r \in \mathbb{C}$ with $u = q - p$, $w = r - p$, set
  \[
    \mathrm{circumcenterR2}\,p\,q\,r
      \;=\; p + \frac{\mathrm{i}\,\bigl(|w|^2 u - |u|^2 w\bigr)}
                     {2\,\mathrm{crossR2}\,u\,w},
  \]
  where $\mathrm{crossR2}\,u\,w = \mathrm{Im}(\overline{u}\,w)$ is the
  in-tree cross product (\cref{def:cross_r2}). A total function; its
  characterizing properties hold under the non-collinearity guard
  $\mathrm{crossR2}\,u\,w \ne 0$. (Center of Dahlberg's discrete circle of
  curvature $\rho(P)$ through the triple.)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.circumcenterR2
lean.code:
noncomputable def circumcenterR2 (p q r : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  p + Complex.I * ((normSq (r - p) : ℝ) * (q - p) - (normSq (q - p) : ℝ) * (r - p))
      / (2 * (crossR2 p q r : ℂ))

blocks.label: lem:cross_r2_im_conj_mul
blocks.title: the cross product is the imaginary part of the Hermitian product
blocks.body:
For $u, w \in \mathbb{C}$,
  $\mathrm{crossR2}\,u\,w = \mathrm{Im}\bigl(\overline{u}\,w\bigr)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.crossR2_eq_im_conj_mul
lean.code:
lemma crossR2_eq_im_conj_mul (A B C : ℂ) :
    crossR2 A B C = ((starRingEnd ℂ) (B - A) * (C - A)).im := by
  simp only [crossR2, Complex.mul_im, Complex.conj_re, Complex.conj_im]
  ring

blocks.tex:
Expand both sides in real components; the in-tree definition of
  $\mathrm{crossR2}$ is $u_x w_y - u_y w_x$, which is exactly
  $\mathrm{Im}(\bar u w)$.

blocks.label: lem:circumcenter_dot
blocks.title: perpendicular-bisector identities
blocks.body:
Let $c = \mathrm{circumcenterR2}\,p\,q\,r$ and suppose
  $\mathrm{crossR2}\,(q-p)\,(r-p) \ne 0$. Then
  \[
    \mathrm{Re}\bigl(\overline{(q-p)}\,(c - p)\bigr) = \tfrac12\,|q-p|^2,
    \qquad
    \mathrm{Re}\bigl(\overline{(r-p)}\,(c - p)\bigr) = \tfrac12\,|r-p|^2 .
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.re_conj_circumcenterR2_sub
lean.code:
lemma re_conj_circumcenterR2_sub {p q r : ℂ} (h : crossR2 p q r ≠ 0) :
    ((starRingEnd ℂ) (q - p) * (circumcenterR2 p q r - p)).re = normSq (q - p) / 2 ∧
      ((starRingEnd ℂ) (r - p) * (circumcenterR2 p q r - p)).re = normSq (r - p) / 2 := by
  have hζ : circumcenterR2 p q r - p
      = (Complex.I * ((normSq (r - p) : ℝ) * (q - p) - (normSq (q - p) : ℝ) * (r - p)))
          / (2 * (crossR2 p q r : ℂ)) := by
    rw [circumcenterR2]; ring
  have hden : (2 * (crossR2 p q r : ℂ)) = ((2 * crossR2 p q r : ℝ) : ℂ) := by push_cast; ring
  have hne : (2 * crossR2 p q r : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
    intro h0; exact h (by linarith)
  constructor <;>
  · rw [hζ, hden, mul_div_assoc', Complex.div_ofReal_re]
    rw [div_eq_div_iff hne two_ne_zero]
    simp only [Complex.mul_re, Complex.mul_im, Complex.conj_re, Complex.conj_im,
      Complex.I_re, Complex.I_im, Complex.sub_re, Complex.sub_im, Complex.ofReal_re,
      Complex.ofReal_im, Complex.normSq_apply, crossR2]
    ring

blocks.tex:
Write $\zeta = c - p = \mathrm{i}(|w|^2 u - |u|^2 w)/(2\delta)$ with
  $\delta = \mathrm{Im}(\bar u w)$. Then
  $\mathrm{Re}(\bar u \zeta)
    = \mathrm{Re}\bigl(\mathrm{i}(|w|^2 |u|^2 - |u|^2 \bar u w)\bigr)/(2\delta)
    = |u|^2\,\mathrm{Im}(\bar u w)/(2\delta) = |u|^2/2$,
  using $\mathrm{Re}(\mathrm{i}z) = -\mathrm{Im}(z)$ and
  $\mathrm{Im}(|w|^2|u|^2) = 0$; symmetrically for $w$ (with
  $\mathrm{Im}(\bar w u) = -\delta$). Pure algebra in $\mathbb{C}$.

blocks.label: lem:circumcenter_equidist
blocks.title: the circumcenter is equidistant
blocks.body: Under the same guard, $|c - p| = |c - q| = |c - r|$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.circumcenterR2_equidist
lean.code:
lemma circumcenterR2_equidist {p q r : ℂ} (h : crossR2 p q r ≠ 0) :
    dist (circumcenterR2 p q r) q = dist (circumcenterR2 p q r) p ∧
      dist (circumcenterR2 p q r) r = dist (circumcenterR2 p q r) p := by
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := re_conj_circumcenterR2_sub h
  have key : ∀ x : ℂ,
      ((starRingEnd ℂ) (x - p) * (circumcenterR2 p q r - p)).re = normSq (x - p) / 2 →
        dist (circumcenterR2 p q r) x = dist (circumcenterR2 p q r) p := by
    intro x hx
    have hxp : circumcenterR2 p q r - x = (circumcenterR2 p q r - p) - (x - p) := by ring
    have hsq : normSq (circumcenterR2 p q r - x) = normSq (circumcenterR2 p q r - p) := by
      rw [hxp, normSq_sub' _ _, hx]; ring
    rw [dist_eq_norm, dist_eq_norm,
      ← Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg (circumcenterR2 p q r - x)),
      ← Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg (circumcenterR2 p q r - p)),
      ← Complex.normSq_eq_norm_sq, ← Complex.normSq_eq_norm_sq, hsq]
  exact ⟨key q h1, key r h2⟩

/-! ## Vertex sectors and local regularity -/

blocks.tex:
$|c - q|^2 = |(c-p) - u|^2 = |c-p|^2 - 2\,\mathrm{Re}(\bar u (c-p)) + |u|^2
  = |c-p|^2$ by \cref{lem:circumcenter_dot}; same for $r$.

blocks.label: def:vertex_sector
blocks.title: vertex sector
blocks.body:
\textit{Source: Dahlberg, sector $\mathcal{A}(P)$, p.~2.}
  For a cyclic vertex map $v : \ZMod n \to \mathbb{C}$ and $i \in \ZMod n$,
  \[
    \mathrm{vertexSector}\,v\,i \;=\;
    \bigl\{\, v_i + s\,(v_{i-1} - v_i) + t\,(v_{i+1} - v_i)
      \;:\; s, t \ge 0 \,\bigr\}
  \]
  --- the closed convex cone at $v_i$ spanned by the two incident edge
  directions. (For a non-reflex vertex, interior angle $< \pi$, this is
  exactly Dahlberg's closed convex sector $\mathcal{A}$; every vertex of a
  positively-turning moderate-arc development is non-reflex. The $k = 0$
  half-plane convention is out of scope per the chapter preamble.)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.vertexSector

blocks.label: def:locally_regular
blocks.title: locally regular polygon
blocks.body:
\textit{Source: Dahlberg, Definition 1, p.~3.}
  $\mathrm{LocallyRegularR2}\,v$ holds when for every $i \in \ZMod n$ the
  consecutive triple is non-collinear,
  $\mathrm{crossR2}\,(v_{i-1} - v_i)\,(v_{i+1} - v_i) \ne 0$, and
  \[
    \mathrm{circumcenterR2}\,v_i\,v_{i-1}\,v_{i+1}
      \;\in\; \mathrm{vertexSector}\,v\,i .
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.LocallyRegularR2
lean.code:
def LocallyRegularR2 (v : ZMod n → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : ZMod n, crossR2 (v i) (v (i - 1)) (v (i + 1)) ≠ 0 ∧
    circumcenterR2 (v i) (v (i - 1)) (v (i + 1)) ∈ vertexSector v i

/-! ## Dahlberg's Proposition 1 (non-reflex case) -/

blocks.title: Plateau-aware local extrema and the DFV bridge

blocks.label: def:plateau_local_max
blocks.title: plateau local extrema on a cyclic profile
blocks.body:
\textit{Source: Dahlberg, $I(f,P)/\hat I$ vocabulary, p.~2.}
  For $f : \ZMod n \to \mathbb{R}$ and $i \in \ZMod n$:
  $\mathrm{IsPlateauLocalMax}\,f\,i$ holds when there are an
  $\mathbb{N}$-lift $a$ and a length $k < n$ with
  $i \in \{a, a+1, \dots, a+k\}$ (as residues), $f$ constant $= f(i)$ on
  that run, and $f(a - 1) < f(i)$, $f(a + k + 1) < f(i)$.
  $\mathrm{IsPlateauLocalMin}$ is the same with reversed inequalities
  (its own block below). Two
  plateau extrema are \emph{distinct} when their defining runs are disjoint.
  (Existential form of Dahlberg's definition: a run with strict drops at
  both extended ends is automatically the maximal plateau $I(f,i)$, since a
  constant run cannot cross a strict drop; so this is equivalent to his
  ``$f(Q) < f(P)$ on $\hat I \setminus I$'' and avoids formalizing the
  maximality of $I(f,P)$.)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.IsPlateauLocalMax
lean.code:
def IsPlateauLocalMax (f : ZMod n → ℝ) (i : ZMod n) : Prop :=
  ∃ a k : ℕ, k < n ∧ PlateauMaxRun f a k ∧ ∃ m ≤ k, i = ((a + m : ℕ) : ZMod n)

blocks.label: def:plateau_local_min
blocks.title: plateau local minimum
blocks.body:
As in \cref{def:plateau_local_max} with the strict inequalities reversed:
  $f(a-1) > f(i)$ and $f(a+k+1) > f(i)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.IsPlateauLocalMin
lean.code:
def IsPlateauLocalMin (f : ZMod n → ℝ) (i : ZMod n) : Prop :=
  ∃ a k : ℕ, k < n ∧ PlateauMinRun f a k ∧ ∃ m ≤ k, i = ((a + m : ℕ) : ZMod n)

deps.title: plateau local extrema on a cyclic profile
deps.label: def:plateau_local_max

blocks.label: def:plateau_max_run
blocks.title: explicit plateau maximum run
blocks.body:
$\mathrm{PlateauMaxRun}\,f\,a\,k$ packages the run-level data of
  \cref{def:plateau_local_max}: $f$ constant on the residues of
  $\{a, \dots, a+k\}$, and $f(a-1) < f(a)$, $f(a+k+1) < f(a)$. (The bound
  $k < n$ is \emph{not} part of the predicate --- it is carried alongside it
  by every consumer, e.g.\ \cref{def:plateau_local_max} and
  \cref{cor:dfv_plateau_extrema_window}; it is in fact forced, since a run of
  length $\ge n-1$ would wrap and contradict the strict drop at $a-1$. The bridge
  theorem's conclusion is phrased with these explicit runs, which carry the
  disjointness data two abstract point-form extrema would lose.)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.PlateauMaxRun
lean.code:
def PlateauMaxRun (f : ZMod n → ℝ) (a k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ m ≤ k, f ((a + m : ℕ) : ZMod n) = f (a : ZMod n)) ∧
    f ((a : ZMod n) - 1) < f (a : ZMod n) ∧
    f ((a + k + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n) < f (a : ZMod n)

deps.title: plateau local extrema on a cyclic profile
deps.label: def:plateau_local_max

blocks.label: def:plateau_min_run
blocks.title: explicit plateau minimum run
blocks.body: As \cref{def:plateau_max_run} with the strict inequalities reversed.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.PlateauMinRun
lean.code:
def PlateauMinRun (f : ZMod n → ℝ) (a k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ m ≤ k, f ((a + m : ℕ) : ZMod n) = f (a : ZMod n)) ∧
    f (a : ZMod n) < f ((a : ZMod n) - 1) ∧
    f (a : ZMod n) < f ((a + k + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n)

blocks.label: lem:plateau_max_run_isMax
blocks.title: a maximum run is a plateau local maximum
blocks.body:
If $\mathrm{PlateauMaxRun}\,f\,a\,k$ then every residue of
  $\{a, \dots, a+k\}$ satisfies $\mathrm{IsPlateauLocalMax}\,f$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.PlateauMaxRun.isPlateauLocalMax
lean.code:
lemma PlateauMaxRun.isPlateauLocalMax {f : ZMod n → ℝ} {a k : ℕ} (hk : k < n)
    (h : PlateauMaxRun f a k) : IsPlateauLocalMax f (a : ZMod n) :=
  ⟨a, k, hk, h, 0, Nat.zero_le k, by rw [Nat.add_zero]⟩

blocks.tex:
The run itself is the witnessing run of \cref{def:plateau_local_max};
  constancy transports the plateau value to the chosen point.

blocks.label: lem:plateau_min_run_isMin
blocks.title: a minimum run is a plateau local minimum
blocks.body:
If $\mathrm{PlateauMinRun}\,f\,a\,k$ then every residue of
  $\{a, \dots, a+k\}$ satisfies $\mathrm{IsPlateauLocalMin}\,f$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.PlateauMinRun.isPlateauLocalMin
lean.code:
lemma PlateauMinRun.isPlateauLocalMin {f : ZMod n → ℝ} {a k : ℕ} (hk : k < n)
    (h : PlateauMinRun f a k) : IsPlateauLocalMin f (a : ZMod n) :=
  ⟨a, k, hk, h, 0, Nat.zero_le k, by rw [Nat.add_zero]⟩

/-! ## The DFV window yields Dahlberg's conclusion class -/

blocks.tex: Mirror of \cref{lem:plateau_max_run_isMax}.

blocks.label: thm:dfv_plateau_bridge
blocks.title: the DFV window yields Dahlberg's conclusion class
blocks.body:
If $\mathrm{DFV}(\kappa; c)$ (\cref{def:discrete_fourvertex}), then
  $\kappa$ has two distinct plateau local maxima and two distinct plateau
  local minima (in the sense of \cref{def:plateau_local_max,def:plateau_local_min}).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.dfv_plateau_extrema
lean.code:
theorem dfv_plateau_extrema {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ} {i₁ i₂ i₃ i₄ : ℕ}
    (h12 : i₁ < i₂) (h23 : i₂ < i₃) (h34 : i₃ < i₄) (h41 : i₄ < i₁ + n)
    (hκ1 : c < κ ((i₁ : ℕ) : ZMod n)) (hκ2 : κ ((i₂ : ℕ) : ZMod n) < c)
    (hκ3 : c < κ ((i₃ : ℕ) : ZMod n)) (hκ4 : κ ((i₄ : ℕ) : ZMod n) < c) :
    (∃ a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ : ℕ, k₁ < n ∧ k₂ < n ∧
        PlateauMaxRun κ a₁ k₁ ∧ PlateauMaxRun κ a₂ k₂ ∧
        ∀ m₁, m₁ ≤ k₁ → ∀ m₂, m₂ ≤ k₂ →
          ((a₁ + m₁ : ℕ) : ZMod n) ≠ ((a₂ + m₂ : ℕ) : ZMod n)) ∧
    (∃ a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ : ℕ, k₁ < n ∧ k₂ < n ∧
        PlateauMinRun κ a₁ k₁ ∧ PlateauMinRun κ a₂ k₂ ∧
        ∀ m₁, m₁ ≤ k₁ → ∀ m₂, m₂ ≤ k₂ →
          ((a₁ + m₁ : ℕ) : ZMod n) ≠ ((a₂ + m₂ : ℕ) : ZMod n)) := by
  -- the two period-shifted window values
  have e1 : ((i₁ + n : ℕ) : ZMod n) = ((i₁ : ℕ) : ZMod n) := by
    push_cast [ZMod.natCast_self]; ring
  have e2 : ((i₂ + n : ℕ) : ZMod n) = ((i₂ : ℕ) : ZMod n) := by
    push_cast [ZMod.natCast_self]; ring
  constructor
  · -- MAXIMA: arcs (i₂, i₄) through i₃ and (i₄, i₂+n) through i₁+n
    obtain ⟨a, b, hA1, hA2, hA3, hAc, hAL, hAR⟩ :=
      exists_max_run (fun m : ℕ => κ ((m : ℕ) : ZMod n)) h23.le h34.le
        (lt_trans hκ2 hκ3) (lt_trans hκ4 hκ3)
    obtain ⟨a', b', hB1, hB2, hB3, hBc, hBL, hBR⟩ :=
      exists_max_run (fun m : ℕ => κ ((m : ℕ) : ZMod n)) h41.le
        (show i₁ + n ≤ i₂ + n by omega)
        (by simp only [e1]; exact lt_trans hκ4 hκ1)
        (by simp only [e1, e2]; exact lt_trans hκ2 hκ1)
    have hk1 : b - a < n := by omega
    have hk2 : b' - a' < n := by omega
    refine ⟨a, b - a, a', b' - a', hk1, hk2,
      plateauMaxRun_of_natRun (by omega) hA2 hAc hAL hAR,
      plateauMaxRun_of_natRun (by omega) hB2 hBc hBL hBR, ?_⟩
    intro m₁ hm₁ m₂ hm₂
    exact natCast_zmod_ne (by omega) (by omega)
  · -- MINIMA: arcs (i₁, i₃) through i₂ and (i₃, i₁+n) through i₄
    obtain ⟨a, b, hA1, hA2, hA3, hAc, hAL, hAR⟩ :=
      exists_max_run (fun m : ℕ => -κ ((m : ℕ) : ZMod n)) h12.le h23.le
        (by simpa using lt_trans hκ2 hκ1)
        (by simpa using lt_trans hκ2 hκ3)
    obtain ⟨a', b', hB1, hB2, hB3, hBc, hBL, hBR⟩ :=
      exists_max_run (fun m : ℕ => -κ ((m : ℕ) : ZMod n)) h34.le
        (show i₄ ≤ i₁ + n by omega)
        (by simpa using lt_trans hκ4 hκ3)
        (by simp only [e1]; simpa using lt_trans hκ4 hκ1)
    have hk1 : b - a < n := by omega
    have hk2 : b' - a' < n := by omega
    refine ⟨a, b - a, a', b' - a', hk1, hk2,
      plateauMinRun_of_natRun (by omega) hA2
        (fun x h1 h2 => neg_inj.1 (hAc x h1 h2)) (by simpa using hAL)
        (by simpa using hAR),
      plateauMinRun_of_natRun (by omega) hB2
        (fun x h1 h2 => neg_inj.1 (hBc x h1 h2)) (by simpa using hBL)
        (by simpa using hBR), ?_⟩
    intro m₁ hm₁ m₂ hm₂
    exact natCast_zmod_ne (by omega) (by omega)

deps.label: def:plateau_local_max

blocks.tex:
Let $i_1 < i_2 < i_3 < i_4 < i_1 + n$ be the window, with
  $\kappa_{i_2}, \kappa_{i_4} < c < \kappa_{i_1}, \kappa_{i_3}$. Consider
  the closed cyclic arc $B_1 = [i_2, i_4]$ (through $i_3$) and
  $B_2 = [i_4, i_2 + n]$ (through $i_1 + n$, i.e.\ through $i_1$). On the
  finite arc $B_1$ pick $j$ attaining $\max_{B_1} \kappa \;(> c$, witnessed
  by $i_3)$. The maximal constant run of $\kappa$ through $j$ cannot reach
  either endpoint $i_2, i_4$ (their values are $< c <$ the run value), so
  the run together with its two extension neighbours stays inside $B_1$;
  the extension neighbours are non-attaining points of the arc adjacent to
  a maximal run, hence have value strictly below the max. That run is a
  plateau local max. The same on $B_2$ (witness $i_1$) produces a second
  one; the two runs live in the disjoint open arcs
  $(i_2, i_4)$ and $(i_4, i_2 + n)$, so they are distinct. For minima run
  the mirrored argument on the arcs $[i_1, i_3]$ (through $i_2$) and
  $[i_3, i_1 + n]$ (through $i_4$) with $\min$ in place of $\max$. Finite
  combinatorics on $\mathbb{N}$-lifts throughout; no geometry.
The four-vertex window is a value-separated alternating pattern in a cyclic curvature word. The constant-profile realization and the retained elementary reductions supply the base cases.

blocks.label: def:discrete_fourvertex
blocks.title: discrete four-vertex window
blocks.body:
For $c \in \mathbb{R}$, the profile $\kappa : \ZMod n \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies
  $\mathrm{DFV}(\kappa; c)$ when there exist four cyclically ordered indices —
  represented by $\mathbb{N}$-lifts $i_1 < i_2 < i_3 < i_4 < i_1 + n$ — with
  \[
    \kappa_{i_2},\ \kappa_{i_4} \;<\; c \;<\; \kappa_{i_1},\ \kappa_{i_3}.
  \]
  (Two ``high'' values separated by two ``low'' values, alternating across the
  window level $c$.)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.DFV
lean.code:
def DFV (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (c : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ i₁ i₂ i₃ i₄ : ℕ, i₁ < i₂ ∧ i₂ < i₃ ∧ i₃ < i₄ ∧ i₄ < i₁ + n ∧
    c < κ ((i₁ : ℕ) : ZMod n) ∧ κ ((i₂ : ℕ) : ZMod n) < c ∧
    c < κ ((i₃ : ℕ) : ZMod n) ∧ κ ((i₄ : ℕ) : ZMod n) < c

blocks.label: def:discrete_fourvertex_pos
blocks.title: positive discrete four-vertex hypothesis
blocks.body:
$\mathrm{DiscreteFourVertexPos}\,\kappa$ holds when $\kappa_i > 0$ for all $i$
  and either $\kappa$ is constant or $\mathrm{DFV}(\kappa; c)$ holds for some
  $c > 0$.

blocks.body:
If $\mathrm{DFV}(\kappa; c)$ then $\kappa$ has two disjoint plateau maximum
  runs and two disjoint plateau minimum runs (the conclusion of

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.DFV.plateau_extrema
lean.code:
theorem DFV.plateau_extrema {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ} (h : DFV κ c) :
    (∃ a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ : ℕ, k₁ < n ∧ k₂ < n ∧
        PlateauMaxRun κ a₁ k₁ ∧ PlateauMaxRun κ a₂ k₂ ∧
        ∀ m₁, m₁ ≤ k₁ → ∀ m₂, m₂ ≤ k₂ →
          ((a₁ + m₁ : ℕ) : ZMod n) ≠ ((a₂ + m₂ : ℕ) : ZMod n)) ∧
    (∃ a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ : ℕ, k₁ < n ∧ k₂ < n ∧
        PlateauMinRun κ a₁ k₁ ∧ PlateauMinRun κ a₂ k₂ ∧
        ∀ m₁, m₁ ≤ k₁ → ∀ m₂, m₂ ≤ k₂ →
          ((a₁ + m₁ : ℕ) : ZMod n) ≠ ((a₂ + m₂ : ℕ) : ZMod n)) := by
  obtain ⟨i₁, i₂, i₃, i₄, h12, h23, h34, h41, hκ1, hκ2, hκ3, hκ4⟩ := h
  exact dfv_plateau_extrema h12 h23 h34 h41 hκ1 hκ2 hκ3 hκ4

Unfold \cref{def:discrete_fourvertex} to the explicit lifted window
  $i_1 < i_2 < i_3 < i_4 < i_1 + n$ with the four level inequalities ---

  \cref{thm:dfv_plateau_bridge} (\texttt{dfv\_plateau\_extrema} takes the

The retained analytic lemmas describe a regular level set using an implicit function and preserve open geometric constraints. Only the local analytic ingredients used by the regular-anchor construction are included.

blocks.label: def:collar_solution_data
blocks.title: Closed solutions and their strict interior
blocks.body:
Let \(D \subseteq X\) be a set of \emph{closed solutions} and \(U \subseteq D\)
its \emph{strict interior} (the solutions all of whose moderate-arc walls are
strictly satisfied).

blocks.label: thm:compact_collared_continuation
blocks.title: Compact collared continuation

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.compact_collared_continuation
lean.code:
theorem compact_collared_continuation
    {X K : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace K]
    [T2Space K] [PreconnectedSpace K]
    {D U : Set X} {π : X → K}
    (hD : IsCompact D) (hne : D.Nonempty) (hUD : U ⊆ D)
    (hπ : ContinuousOn π D)
    (hcollar : ∀ x ∈ D, ∃ y ∈ U, π y = π x)
    (hlocal : ∀ x ∈ U, π '' U ∈ 𝓝 (π x)) :
    π '' U = Set.univ := by
  exact closedImage_collared_continuation
    (hD.image_of_continuousOn hπ).isClosed hne hUD hcollar hlocal

blocks.tex:
The image \(\pi(D)\) is closed (compact image of a compact set under a map
continuous on \(D\)) and, by the local-openness hypothesis, \(\pi(U)\) is open.
The collar hypothesis gives \(\pi(D) = \pi(U)\), so \(\pi(U)\) is clopen and
nonempty in the preconnected space \(K\), hence all of \(K\).  This is exactly
\texttt{closedImage\_collared\_continuation} composed with the identifications
\(\pi(D)=\pi(U)\); see the Lean file for the two supporting lemmas
\texttt{fiberPurification\_iff\_image\_eq} and
\texttt{frontier\_subset\_iff\_eq\_univ}.

blocks.title: Discharging local openness: the fibrewise-submersion lemma

blocks.tex:
The local-openness input of \Cref{thm:compact_collared_continuation} is the one
analytic ingredient of the whole wiring, and it is \emph{not} the same statement
as the wall-crossing lemma below (which moves along a fibre at fixed parameter).
We state it first in the abstract form that the application consumes.

blocks.label: thm:regularWallZero_entersInterior
blocks.title: Regular wall zero enters the interior
blocks.body:
Let \(f : E \to F\) be a closure map with a surjective strict derivative \(f'\)
at a configuration \(a\), let \(w\) be an active wall functional with derivative
\(w'\), and let \(v \in \ker f'\) be a tangent direction that is strictly inward
for \(w\) (i.e.\ \(w'(v) > 0\)).  Then there is an exact level-set curve
\(\gamma\) with \(\gamma(0)=a\), \(\gamma'(0)=v\), staying on \(\{f = f(a)\}\) and
strictly increasing \(w\) for all small \(t>0\).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.regularWallZero_entersInterior
lean.code:
theorem regularWallZero_entersInterior
    {E F : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [FiniteDimensional ℝ F]
    {f : E → F} {f' : E →L[ℝ] F} {a v : E}
    {w : E → ℝ} {w' : E →L[ℝ] ℝ}
    (hf : HasStrictFDerivAt f f' a)
    (hsurj : f'.range = ⊤)
    (hv : v ∈ f'.ker)
    (hw : HasFDerivAt w w' a)
    (hpos : 0 < w' v) :
    ∃ (γ : ℝ → E) (ε : ℝ),
      0 < ε ∧
      γ 0 = a ∧
      HasDerivAt γ v 0 ∧
      Tendsto γ (𝓝 0) (𝓝 a) ∧
      ∀ t, 0 < t → t < ε →
        f (γ t) = f a ∧ w a < w (γ t) := by
  let q : f'.ker := ⟨v, hv⟩
  let γ : ℝ → E := fun t =>
    hf.implicitFunction f f' hsurj (f a) (t • q)
  have hγ0 : γ 0 = a := by
    simp [γ, hf.implicitFunction_apply_image hsurj]
  have hq_deriv : HasStrictDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => t • q) q 0 := by
    simpa using ((hasStrictDerivAt_id (𝕜 := ℝ) (0 : ℝ)).smul_const q)
  have hq_tendsto : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => t • q) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 0) := by
    simpa only [ContinuousAt, zero_smul] using hq_deriv.hasDerivAt.continuousAt
  have hγ_tendsto : Tendsto γ (𝓝 0) (𝓝 a) := by
    simpa [γ] using
      (hf.tendsto_implicitFunction hsurj
        (g₁ := fun _ : ℝ => f a) (g₂ := fun t : ℝ => t • q)
        tendsto_const_nhds hq_tendsto)
  have hγ_deriv : HasDerivAt γ v 0 := by
    simpa [γ, q, Function.comp_def] using
      ((hf.to_implicitFunction hsurj).comp_hasStrictDerivAt_of_eq 0 hq_deriv (by simp)).hasDerivAt
  have hlevel : ∀ᶠ t : ℝ in 𝓝 0, f (γ t) = f a := by
    have hp : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => (f a, t • q)) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 (f a, 0)) :=
      tendsto_const_nhds.prodMk_nhds hq_tendsto
    simpa [γ] using hp.eventually (hf.map_implicitFunction_eq hsurj)
  have hwall : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => w (γ t)) (w' v) 0 := by
    simpa [Function.comp_def] using
      hw.comp_hasDerivAt_of_eq 0 hγ_deriv hγ0.symm
  have hslope :
      Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => t⁻¹ * (w (γ t) - w (γ 0)))
        (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (w' v)) := by
    simpa [smul_eq_mul] using hwall.tendsto_slope_zero_right
  have hgood :
      ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), f (γ t) = f a ∧ w a < w (γ t) := by
    filter_upwards [hlevel.filter_mono nhdsWithin_le_nhds,
      hslope.eventually_const_lt hpos, self_mem_nhdsWithin] with t hft hs ht
    refine ⟨hft, ?_⟩
    have hinv : 0 < t⁻¹ := inv_pos.mpr ht
    have hdiff : 0 < w (γ t) - w (γ 0) :=
      pos_of_mul_pos_right hs hinv.le
    rw [hγ0] at hdiff
    exact sub_pos.mp hdiff
  obtain ⟨ε, hε, hεsub⟩ :=
    mem_nhdsGT_iff_exists_Ioo_subset.mp hgood
  refine ⟨γ, ε, hε, hγ0, hγ_deriv, hγ_tendsto, ?_⟩
  intro t ht0 htε
  -- … (truncated)

blocks.tex:
Proved in-tree via Mathlib's finite-dimensional implicit-function theorem
(\texttt{HasStrictFDerivAt.implicitFunction}); the level-set curve is
\(\gamma(t) = \mathrm{implicitFunction}(f(a), t\cdot q)\) with \(q = v \in \ker
f'\), and the strict inward slope follows from the derivative
\(\frac{d}{dt}\,w(\gamma(t))\big|_{0} = w'(v) > 0\).  See the Lean file; the
simultaneous multi-wall form is \texttt{regularWallZero\_entersAllInteriors}.

blocks.title: Joint submersion implies the projection image is a neighbourhood

blocks.tex:
The configuration space of the discrete problem carries two kinds of coordinate:
the \emph{parameter} (the curvature profile \(\kappa\)) and the \emph{fibre
variable} (the edge lengths \(\ell\)).  Solutions are the zero set of a closure
map \(G\), and the parameter map is a projection \(\pi\).  The statement we need
is that near a solution at which the \emph{pair} \((G,\pi)\) is a submersion, the
projection of the solution set covers a neighbourhood of the parameter.

blocks.label: lem:collar_proj_submersion
blocks.title: Joint submersion at a solution opens the parameter image
blocks.body:
Let \(E\) be a complete real normed space, \(F\) and \(K\) complete real normed
spaces, \(G : E \to F\), \(\pi : E \to K\), and let \(x \in E\) satisfy
\(G(x) = 0\).  Suppose \(G\) and \(\pi\) are strictly differentiable at \(x\)
with derivatives \(G'\) and \(\pi'\), and that the \emph{joint} derivative
\[
  v \;\longmapsto\; \bigl(G'(v),\,\pi'(v)\bigr) \;\in\; F \times K
\]
is surjective.  Let \(V\) be a neighbourhood of \(x\) and let \(U \subseteq E\)
be any set with \(\{G = 0\} \cap V \subseteq U\).  Then \(\pi(U)\) is a
neighbourhood of \(\pi(x)\).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.projImage_mem_nhds_of_jointSubmersion
lean.code:
theorem projImage_mem_nhds_of_jointSubmersion
    {E F K : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [CompleteSpace F]
    [NormedAddCommGroup K] [NormedSpace ℝ K] [CompleteSpace K]
    {G : E → F} {π : E → K} {G' : E →L[ℝ] F} {π' : E →L[ℝ] K} {x : E}
    (hGx : G x = 0)
    (hG : HasStrictFDerivAt G G' x) (hπ : HasStrictFDerivAt π π' x)
    (hsurj : (G'.prod π').range = ⊤)
    {V : Set E} (hV : V ∈ 𝓝 x)
    {U : Set E} (hU : {y | G y = 0} ∩ V ⊆ U) :
    π '' U ∈ 𝓝 (π x) := by
  have hH : HasStrictFDerivAt (fun y => (G y, π y)) (G'.prod π') x := hG.prodMk hπ
  have hmap : Filter.map (fun y => (G y, π y)) (𝓝 x) = 𝓝 (G x, π x) :=
    hH.map_nhds_eq_of_surj hsurj
  have hHV : (fun y => (G y, π y)) '' V ∈ 𝓝 ((0 : F), π x) := by
    rw [← hGx, ← hmap]
    exact Filter.image_mem_map hV
  have hWnhds : (fun k : K => ((0 : F), k)) ⁻¹' ((fun y => (G y, π y)) '' V)
      ∈ 𝓝 (π x) :=
    (continuous_const.prodMk continuous_id).continuousAt.preimage_mem_nhds hHV
  refine Filter.mem_of_superset hWnhds ?_
  rintro k hkW
  obtain ⟨y, hyV, hy⟩ := hkW
  have hyG : G y = 0 := (Prod.ext_iff.mp hy).1
  have hyπ : π y = k := (Prod.ext_iff.mp hy).2
  exact ⟨y, hU ⟨hyG, hyV⟩, hyπ⟩

blocks.tex:
Consider \(H := (G,\pi) : E \to F \times K\).  Its strict derivative at \(x\) is
\(v \mapsto (G'(v), \pi'(v))\), which is surjective by hypothesis, so the
inverse-function theorem in the surjective form (Mathlib's
\texttt{HasStrictFDerivAt.map\_nhds\_eq\_of\_surj}, the same step used in
Mathlib's Lagrange-multiplier proof) gives
\(H_*\,\mathcal N(x) = \mathcal N(H(x)) = \mathcal N(0, \pi(x))\).
In particular \(H(V)\) is a neighbourhood of \((0,\pi(x))\).

Let \(W := \{\,k \in K \mid (0,k) \in H(V)\,\}\); it is the preimage of the
neighbourhood \(H(V)\) under the continuous map \(k \mapsto (0,k)\) evaluated at
\(\pi(x)\), hence \(W\) is a neighbourhood of \(\pi(x)\).  If \(k \in W\), pick
\(y \in V\) with \(H(y) = (0,k)\); then \(G(y) = 0\) and \(\pi(y) = k\), so
\(y \in \{G=0\} \cap V \subseteq U\) and \(k \in \pi(U)\).  Thus
\(W \subseteq \pi(U)\) and \(\pi(U)\) is a neighbourhood of \(\pi(x)\).

blocks.label: lem:collar_hlocal_from_submersion
blocks.title: Interior submersion $\Rightarrow$ local openness
blocks.body:
Let \(U\) be a set of solutions of \(G = 0\) that is \emph{relatively open} among
solutions (every \(x \in U\) has a neighbourhood \(V_x\) with
\(\{G = 0\} \cap V_x \subseteq U\)) and at each of whose points the joint
derivative \((G',\pi')\) is surjective.  Then hypothesis~(4) of
\Cref{thm:compact_collared_continuation} holds: \(\pi(U) \in \mathcal N(\pi x)\)
for every \(x \in U\).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.collar_hlocal_of_openSolutionSet
lean.code:
theorem collar_hlocal_of_openSolutionSet
    {E F K : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [CompleteSpace F]
    [NormedAddCommGroup K] [NormedSpace ℝ K] [CompleteSpace K]
    {G : E → F} {π : E → K} {U : Set E}
    (hsol : ∀ x ∈ U, G x = 0)
    (hopen : ∀ x ∈ U, ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 x, {y | G y = 0} ∩ V ⊆ U)
    (hreg : ∀ x ∈ U, ∃ (G' : E →L[ℝ] F) (π' : E →L[ℝ] K),
      HasStrictFDerivAt G G' x ∧ HasStrictFDerivAt π π' x ∧
      (G'.prod π').range = ⊤) :
    ∀ x ∈ U, π '' U ∈ 𝓝 (π x) := by
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨V, hV, hVU⟩ := hopen x hx
  obtain ⟨G', π', hG, hπ, hsurj⟩ := hreg x hx
  exact projImage_mem_nhds_of_jointSubmersion (hsol x hx) hG hπ hsurj hV hVU

/-! ## The set-level continuation engine -/

deps.title: Joint submersion at a solution opens the parameter image
deps.label: lem:collar_proj_submersion

blocks.tex:
Immediate from \Cref{lem:collar_proj_submersion} applied at each \(x \in U\)
with the given \(V_x\).

blocks.label: def:collar_solution_sets
blocks.title: Configuration space, closure map, parameter projection
blocks.body:
Fix \(n \geq 3\).  A \emph{configuration} is a pair
\(p = (\kappa, \ell) \in (\mathbb{Z}/n \to \mathbb{R}) \times
(\mathbb{Z}/n \to \mathbb{R})\).  Define
\[
  G(p) \;=\; \bigl(\,\mathrm{closureGap}\,\kappa\,\ell,\;
                    \mathrm{turningSum}\,\kappa\,\ell - 2\pi \,\bigr)
  \;\in\; \mathbb{C} \times \mathbb{R},
  \qquad
  \pi(p) \;=\; \kappa .
\]
Thus \(G(p) = 0\) says exactly that the development of \((\kappa,\ell)\) closes
with total turning \(2\pi\), and \(\pi\) is the parameter (curvature-profile)
projection.  Given a set \(S\) of admissible profiles we write
\begin{align*}
  U &= \{\,p \;:\; \pi(p) \in S,\ \mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell,\
        G(p) = 0\,\}, \\
  D &\supseteq U \quad\text{a compact set of closed configurations with
        saturated (\(\leq\)) moderate-arc walls.}
\end{align*}
\(U\) is the \emph{strict interior}: the moderate-arc predicate
\(\mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\) is an open condition
(\(0 < \ell_i\) and \(|\kappa_i|\,\ell_{i\pm}/2 < 1\)), so \(U\) is relatively
open among solutions, which is exactly the hypothesis of
\Cref{lem:collar_hlocal_from_submersion}.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.closureMapR3
lean.code:
noncomputable def closureMapR3 [NeZero n]
    (p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ)) : ℂ × ℝ :=
  (closureGap p.1 p.2, turningSum p.1 p.2 - 2 * Real.pi)

deps.title: Closed solutions and their strict interior
deps.label: def:collar_solution_data

blocks.label: lem:collar_realizes_of_mem
blocks.title: Membership of \texorpdfstring{$U$}{U} gives realizability
blocks.body:
If \(n \geq 3\), \(p = (\kappa,\ell) \in U\) and \(\kappa_i > 0\) for all \(i\),
then \(\mathrm{RealizesR2}\,\kappa\).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.realizesR2_of_mem_collarInterior
lean.code:
theorem realizesR2_of_mem_collarInterior [NeZero n] (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    {S : Set (ZMod n → ℝ)} {p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ)}
    (hp : p ∈ collarInterior S) (hpos : ∀ i, 0 < p.1 i) :
    RealizesR2 p.1 := by
  obtain ⟨-, hMA, hG⟩ := hp
  rw [closureMapR3, Prod.ext_iff] at hG
  have hE : closureGap p.1 p.2 = 0 := hG.1
  have hT : turningSum p.1 p.2 = 2 * Real.pi := by
    have h2 : turningSum p.1 p.2 - 2 * Real.pi = 0 := hG.2
    linarith
  exact ⟨p.2, hMA, hE, hT,
    isSimplePolygon_of_turningPositive hn hMA hpos hE hT⟩

deps.title: Configuration space, closure map, parameter projection
deps.label: def:collar_solution_sets

blocks.tex:
By definition of \(U\) the data \((\kappa,\ell)\) is moderate-arc, closes
(\(\mathrm{closureGap} = 0\)) and has total turning \(2\pi\).  Simplicity is
free in the positive case: all turning angles are positive, so the development
is convex, and \(\texttt{isSimplePolygon\_of\_turningPositive}\)
(\Cref{chap:discrete_convexity}) applies.  Unfolding
\(\mathrm{RealizesR2}\) with the witness \(\ell\) concludes.  This is the
Positive-Convexity Collapse: for positive profiles, realizability is exactly
closure existence.

blocks.title: Auxiliary declarations of the wiring file

blocks.tex:
The four blocks of this subsection record the supporting declarations that the
wiring theorem consumes.  They are elementary but load-bearing, and each carries
its own dependency edges.

blocks.label: def:collar_interior
blocks.title: The collar interior as a set
blocks.body:
For a chamber \(S\) of profiles,
\[
  \mathrm{collarInterior}(S)
  \;=\;
  \bigl\{\,p = (\kappa,\ell) \;\bigm|\;
     \kappa \in S,\ \ \mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell,\ \
     G(p) = 0 \,\bigr\},
\]
the set \(U\) of \Cref{def:collar_solution_sets} written as a subset of
\((\mathbb{Z}/n \to \mathbb{R})^2\).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.collarInterior
