blocks.tex:
Everything in the discrete layer so far is indexed by \emph{vertices}: the
turning angle $\theta_i$ of \cref{def:turning_angle} lives at vertex $i$ and
reads the two edges $\ell_{i-1}, \ell_i$ adjacent to it, and the moderate-arc
domain of \cref{def:moderate_arc} is likewise a per-vertex conjunction. This
chapter installs the complementary, \emph{edge}-indexed bookkeeping: each edge
$e$ carries a single scalar
\[
  \beta_e \;=\; \arcsin\!\Bigl(\tfrac{\kappa_e\,\ell_e}{2}\Bigr)
             \;+\; \arcsin\!\Bigl(\tfrac{\kappa_{e+1}\,\ell_e}{2}\Bigr),
\]
the \emph{gap} of that edge --- the total turn the development performs while
traversing $e$, split evenly between its two endpoints by the tangent-chord law.

The point of the change of variables is threefold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{The turning sum becomes a plain sum of the new coordinates.}
  Regrouping the $2n$ arcsines of $T(\kappa,\ell)$ by the edge they mention
  instead of by the vertex that owns them gives $\sum_e \beta_e = T$
  (\cref{lem:gap_sum}). This is a re-indexing, nothing more, but it is what
  makes the constraint $T = 2\pi$ an \emph{affine} condition on the new
  coordinates rather than a transcendental one.
\item \textbf{The moderate-arc domain becomes a product of intervals.} The four
  wall inequalities that mention $\ell_e$ (two from each endpoint) collapse to
  the single two-sided bound $0 < \ell_e < 2/\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})$
  (\cref{lem:moderate_arc_edge}), and on that interval $\beta_e$ is a strictly
  increasing continuous bijection onto $(0, U_e)$ with the explicit wall
  \[
    U_e \;=\; \frac{\pi}{2}
       \;+\; \arcsin\frac{\min(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})}
                         {\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})}
  \]
  (\cref{lem:gap_strict_mono,lem:gap_wall_value_cap}). So the whole strict
  domain, which in $\ell$-coordinates is a conjunction over vertices with
  overlapping constraints, is in $\beta$-coordinates literally the open box
  $\prod_e (0, U_e)$.
\item \textbf{It is the coordinate system of the external four-gap pipeline.}
  Writing $r_i = 1/\kappa_i$ for the osculating radii, the cap is
  $2\min(r_e,r_{e+1})$ and the wall is
  $\pi/2 + \arcsin\bigl(\min(r_e,r_{e+1})/\max(r_e,r_{e+1})\bigr)$
  (\cref{lem:gap_radius_cap,lem:gap_radius_wall}); the ratio appearing there is exactly the
  quantity called $a_i = L_i/H_i$ in that pipeline's notes. Note the inversion:
  a local \emph{minimum} of radius is a local \emph{maximum} of curvature, so a
  ``low'' $L$ in the radius word is a curvature peak.
\end{enumerate}

With the dictionary in place, the concluding statement of the pipeline's
realization arguments --- a gap vector $\beta$ with
$0 < \beta_k < U_k$ for all $k$, $\sum_k \beta_k = 2\pi$ and vanishing closure
--- is repackaged into $\mathrm{RealizesR2}\,\kappa$ by
\cref{thm:realizes_of_gap_vector}, with simplicity supplied for free by the
in-tree \cref{thm:convex_simple} (positive curvature $\Rightarrow$ convex
$\Rightarrow$ simple). The last section isolates, as a purely
order-theoretic lemma with no geometry in it, the global step of that
pipeline's zigzag argument (\cref{lem:high_neighbour_global}).

\medskip

\emph{Scope.} This chapter is a change of coordinates and a repackaging: it
proves no new realization. In particular it does not import, assume, or
depend on any of the pipeline's local four-gap certificates, all of which are
still under external audit; \cref{lem:high_neighbour_global} takes the
consequence it needs as an explicit hypothesis and is therefore vacuous until
someone supplies that hypothesis. Nothing here bears on
Tabachnikov's Problem~2.

Throughout, $n \ge 1$, $\kappa, \ell \colon \mathbb{Z}/n \to \mathbb{R}$, and
$e$ ranges over $\mathbb{Z}/n$. Edge $e$ is the segment from vertex $e$ to
vertex $e+1$; it has length $\ell_e$ and its two endpoints carry curvatures
$\kappa_e$ and $\kappa_{e+1}$.

blocks.label: def:gap_angle
blocks.title: gap angle of an edge
blocks.body:
For $t \in \mathbb{R}$ put
  \[
    \gamma_e(t) \;=\;
      \arcsin\!\Bigl(\frac{\kappa_e\, t}{2}\Bigr)
      \;+\;
      \arcsin\!\Bigl(\frac{\kappa_{e+1}\, t}{2}\Bigr).
  \]
  This is the \emph{gap function} of edge $e$: the total turn contributed by an
  edge of length $t$ sitting between the two curvatures $\kappa_e,
  \kappa_{e+1}$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.gapAngleAt
lean.code:
noncomputable def gapAngleAt (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (e : ZMod n) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Real.arcsin (κ e * (t / 2)) + Real.arcsin (κ (e + 1) * (t / 2))

blocks.label: def:gap_of_config
blocks.title: gap of a configuration
blocks.body:
The \emph{gap} of edge $e$ in the configuration $(\kappa,\ell)$ is
  $\beta_e = \gamma_e(\ell_e)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.gapAngle
lean.code:
noncomputable def gapAngle (κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ) (e : ZMod n) : ℝ :=
  gapAngleAt κ e (ℓ e)

blocks.label: def:edge_cap
blocks.title: edge cap
blocks.body:
For a curvature profile $\kappa$ set
  \[
    C_e \;=\; \frac{2}{\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})} .
  \]
  This is the \emph{edge cap}: the supremum of the lengths edge $e$ may take
  inside the strict moderate-arc domain (\cref{lem:moderate_arc_edge}).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.edgeCap
lean.code:
noncomputable def edgeCap (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (e : ZMod n) : ℝ :=
  2 / max (κ e) (κ (e + 1))

blocks.label: def:edge_wall
blocks.title: edge wall
blocks.body:
For a curvature profile $\kappa$ set
  \[
    U_e \;=\; \frac{\pi}{2}
      \;+\; \arcsin\frac{\min(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})}
                        {\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})} .
  \]
  This is the \emph{edge wall}: the supremum of the gaps edge $e$ may take
  (\cref{lem:gap_wall_value_cap}).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.edgeWall
lean.code:
noncomputable def edgeWall (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (e : ZMod n) : ℝ :=
  Real.pi / 2 + Real.arcsin (min (κ e) (κ (e + 1)) / max (κ e) (κ (e + 1)))

blocks.label: lem:gap_sum
blocks.title: the turning sum is the sum of the gaps
blocks.body:
For $n \ge 1$ and any $\kappa, \ell$,
  \[
    \sum_{e \in \mathbb{Z}/n} \beta_e \;=\; T(\kappa,\ell).
  \]
  \begin{proof}
    
    By \cref{def:turning_angle},
    $T = \sum_i \bigl[\arcsin(\kappa_i \ell_{i-1}/2)
       + \arcsin(\kappa_i \ell_i/2)\bigr]$,
    which splits as $A + B$ with
    $A = \sum_i \arcsin(\kappa_i \ell_{i-1}/2)$ and
    $B = \sum_i \arcsin(\kappa_i \ell_i/2)$. Reindex $A$ by the bijection
    $i = e+1$ of $\mathbb{Z}/n$: it becomes
    $\sum_e \arcsin(\kappa_{e+1} \ell_e/2)$. Adding term by term,
    $A + B = \sum_e \bigl[\arcsin(\kappa_{e+1}\ell_e/2)
        + \arcsin(\kappa_e \ell_e/2)\bigr] = \sum_e \beta_e$.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.sum_gapAngle
lean.code:
lemma sum_gapAngle [NeZero n] (κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ) :
    ∑ e : ZMod n, gapAngle κ ℓ e = turningSum κ ℓ := by
  unfold turningSum turningAngle gapAngle gapAngleAt
  simp only [tK_zero]
  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib, add_comm]
  congr 1
  exact Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.addRight (1 : ZMod n)) _ _
    (fun x => by simp [add_sub_cancel_right])

/-! ## The strict domain in edge coordinates -/

blocks.title: The strict domain in edge coordinates

blocks.label: lem:moderate_arc_edge
blocks.title: the moderate-arc domain is a box in $\ell$
blocks.body:
Assume $\kappa_i > 0$ for every $i$. Then
  \[
    \mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell
    \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
    \forall e,\; 0 < \ell_e < C_e .
  \]
  \begin{proof}
    
    By \cref{lem:moderate_arc_zero}, $\mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell$
    unfolds to: for every vertex $i$, $\ell_i > 0$,
    $|\kappa_i|\,\ell_{i-1}/2 < 1$ and $|\kappa_i|\,\ell_i/2 < 1$. Since
    $\kappa > 0$ we may drop the absolute values.

    ($\Rightarrow$) Fix $e$. Then $\ell_e > 0$; the right wall at vertex $e$
    gives $\kappa_e \ell_e/2 < 1$, and the left wall at vertex $e+1$ gives
    $\kappa_{e+1}\ell_e / 2 < 1$. Hence
    $\max(\kappa_e, \kappa_{e+1})\,\ell_e/2 < 1$, i.e.\ $\ell_e < C_e$
    (the max is positive, so the division is legitimate).

    ($\Leftarrow$) Fix a vertex $i$. Positivity of $\ell_i$ is immediate. The
    hypothesis at $e = i$ gives $\ell_i < C_i \le 2/\kappa_i$, so
    $\kappa_i \ell_i/2 < 1$; the hypothesis at $e = i-1$ gives
    $\ell_{i-1} < C_{i-1} \le 2/\kappa_{i}$ (because $\kappa_i$ is one of the
    two curvatures entering $C_{i-1}$, namely the one at $(i-1)+1 = i$), so
    $\kappa_i \ell_{i-1}/2 < 1$.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.moderateArc_zero_iff_edge
lean.code:
lemma moderateArc_zero_iff_edge {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) :
    ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ ↔ ∀ e : ZMod n, 0 < ℓ e ∧ ℓ e < edgeCap κ e := by
  rw [moderateArc_zero_iff]
  constructor
  · intro h e
    have hmax : 0 < max (κ e) (κ (e + 1)) := lt_max_iff.2 (Or.inl (hκ e))
    obtain ⟨hpos, -, hr⟩ := h e
    obtain ⟨-, hl', -⟩ := h (e + 1)
    rw [abs_of_pos (hκ e)] at hr
    rw [abs_of_pos (hκ (e + 1)), add_sub_cancel_right] at hl'
    exact ⟨hpos, lt_edgeCap_of_walls hmax hr hl'⟩
  · intro h i
    have hpos : 0 < ℓ i := (h i).1
    have hpos' : 0 < ℓ (i - 1) := (h (i - 1)).1
    refine ⟨hpos, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [abs_of_pos (hκ i)]
      exact mul_half_lt_one_of_lt_edgeCap (hκ i)
        (by rw [sub_add_cancel]; exact le_max_right _ _) hpos'.le (h (i - 1)).2
    · rw [abs_of_pos (hκ i)]
      exact mul_half_lt_one_of_lt_edgeCap (hκ i) (le_max_left _ _) hpos.le
        (h i).2

/-! ## The gap function is a bijection onto `(0, U_e)` -/

blocks.label: lem:edge_cap_pos
blocks.title: cap positivity
blocks.body:
If $\kappa_e > 0$ and $\kappa_{e+1} > 0$ then $C_e > 0$, and moreover
  $\kappa_e\,C_e/2 \le 1$ and $\kappa_{e+1}\,C_e/2 \le 1$ with equality in at
  least one of the two.
  \begin{proof}
    
    $\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1}) > 0$, so $C_e = 2/\max > 0$. For each of the
    two curvatures $\kappa \in \{\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1}\}$ we have
    $\kappa \le \max$, hence $\kappa\, C_e/2 = \kappa/\max \le 1$, with
    equality for whichever attains the maximum.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.edgeCap_pos
lean.code:
lemma edgeCap_pos {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} (h : 0 < κ e)
    (h' : 0 < κ (e + 1)) :
    0 < edgeCap κ e ∧ κ e * (edgeCap κ e / 2) ≤ 1 ∧
      κ (e + 1) * (edgeCap κ e / 2) ≤ 1 ∧
      (κ e * (edgeCap κ e / 2) = 1 ∨ κ (e + 1) * (edgeCap κ e / 2) = 1) := by
  have hmax : 0 < max (κ e) (κ (e + 1)) := lt_max_iff.2 (Or.inl h)
  have hhalf : edgeCap κ e / 2 = (max (κ e) (κ (e + 1)))⁻¹ := by
    rw [edgeCap]
    field_simp
  refine ⟨div_pos two_pos hmax, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [hhalf, ← div_eq_mul_inv, div_le_one hmax]
    exact le_max_left _ _
  · rw [hhalf, ← div_eq_mul_inv, div_le_one hmax]
    exact le_max_right _ _
  · rcases le_total (κ e) (κ (e + 1)) with hle | hle
    · exact Or.inr (by rw [hhalf, max_eq_right hle, mul_inv_cancel₀ h'.ne'])
    · exact Or.inl (by rw [hhalf, max_eq_left hle, mul_inv_cancel₀ h.ne'])

blocks.label: lem:gap_strict_mono
blocks.title: the gap function is strictly increasing up to the cap
blocks.body:
Assume $\kappa_e, \kappa_{e+1} > 0$. Then $\gamma_e$ is strictly increasing
  on $[0, C_e]$ and continuous on $\mathbb{R}$.
  \begin{proof}
    
    Continuity is that of $\arcsin$ (a continuous function on all of
    $\mathbb{R}$ in the clamped convention) composed with linear maps.

    For strict monotonicity take $0 \le s < t \le C_e$ and let
    $\kappa \in \{\kappa_e, \kappa_{e+1}\}$. Then
    $\kappa s/2 < \kappa t/2$ (as $\kappa > 0$),
    $-1 \le 0 \le \kappa s/2$, and $\kappa t/2 \le \kappa\,C_e/2 \le 1$ by
    \cref{lem:edge_cap_pos}. Strict monotonicity of $\arcsin$ on $[-1,1]$
    therefore gives $\arcsin(\kappa s/2) < \arcsin(\kappa t/2)$ for each of the
    two curvatures, and $\gamma_e(s) < \gamma_e(t)$ follows by adding.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.gapAngleAt_strictMonoOn
lean.code:
lemma gapAngleAt_strictMonoOn {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} (h : 0 < κ e)
    (h' : 0 < κ (e + 1)) :
    StrictMonoOn (gapAngleAt κ e) (Set.Icc 0 (edgeCap κ e)) := by
  obtain ⟨-, hcl1, hcl2, -⟩ := edgeCap_pos h h'
  intro s hs t ht hst
  exact add_lt_add (arcsin_summand_lt h hcl1 hs.1 hst ht.2)
    (arcsin_summand_lt h' hcl2 hs.1 hst ht.2)

blocks.label: lem:gap_wall_value_zero
blocks.title: the gap function vanishes at zero length

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.gapAngleAt_zero
lean.code:
lemma gapAngleAt_zero (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (e : ZMod n) : gapAngleAt κ e 0 = 0 := by
  simp [gapAngleAt]

blocks.label: lem:gap_wall_value_cap
blocks.title: the gap function reaches the wall at the cap
blocks.body:
Assume $\kappa_e, \kappa_{e+1} > 0$. Then $\gamma_e(C_e) = U_e$.
  \begin{proof}
    
    Write $M = \max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})$ and
    $m = \min(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})$, so that $M > 0$ and $C_e = 2/M$; then
    $\kappa_e\,C_e/2 = \kappa_e/M$ and $\kappa_{e+1}\,C_e/2 = \kappa_{e+1}/M$.
    In the case $\kappa_e \le \kappa_{e+1}$ we have $M = \kappa_{e+1}$,
    $m = \kappa_e$, and the two arguments are $m/M$ and $1$; in the case
    $\kappa_{e+1} \le \kappa_e$ they are $1$ and $m/M$. Either way, since
    addition is commutative,
    $\gamma_e(C_e) = \arcsin 1 + \arcsin(m/M) = \pi/2 + \arcsin(m/M) = U_e$.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.gapAngleAt_edgeCap
lean.code:
lemma gapAngleAt_edgeCap {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} (h : 0 < κ e)
    (h' : 0 < κ (e + 1)) : gapAngleAt κ e (edgeCap κ e) = edgeWall κ e := by
  rcases le_total (κ e) (κ (e + 1)) with hle | hle
  · rw [gapAngleAt, edgeCap, edgeWall, max_eq_right hle, min_eq_left hle]
    have h1 : κ e * (2 / κ (e + 1) / 2) = κ e / κ (e + 1) := by
      field_simp
    have h2 : κ (e + 1) * (2 / κ (e + 1) / 2) = 1 := by
      field_simp
    rw [h1, h2, Real.arcsin_one]
    ring
  · rw [gapAngleAt, edgeCap, edgeWall, max_eq_left hle, min_eq_right hle]
    have h1 : κ e * (2 / κ e / 2) = 1 := by
      field_simp
    have h2 : κ (e + 1) * (2 / κ e / 2) = κ (e + 1) / κ e := by
      field_simp
    rw [h1, h2, Real.arcsin_one]

blocks.label: lem:gap_surjective
blocks.title: every admissible gap is attained, uniquely
blocks.body:
Assume $\kappa_e, \kappa_{e+1} > 0$ and $0 < \beta < U_e$. Then there is a
  unique $t$ with $0 < t < C_e$ and $\gamma_e(t) = \beta$.
  \begin{proof}
    
    \emph{Existence.} $\gamma_e$ is continuous on $[0, C_e]$ and
    $0 \le C_e$ by \cref{lem:edge_cap_pos}, so the intermediate value theorem
    on an open interval gives
    $\bigl(\gamma_e(0),\, \gamma_e(C_e)\bigr) \subseteq \gamma_e\bigl((0,
    C_e)\bigr)$. By \cref{lem:gap_wall_value_zero,lem:gap_wall_value_cap} the left-hand side is
    $(0, U_e)$, which contains $\beta$.

    \emph{Uniqueness.} $\gamma_e$ is strictly increasing on $[0, C_e]$
    (\cref{lem:gap_strict_mono}), hence injective there, and $(0,C_e)
    \subseteq [0,C_e]$.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.exists_unique_length_of_gap
lean.code:
lemma exists_unique_length_of_gap {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} (h : 0 < κ e)
    (h' : 0 < κ (e + 1)) {β : ℝ} (hβ0 : 0 < β) (hβU : β < edgeWall κ e) :
    ∃! t, t ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (edgeCap κ e) ∧ gapAngleAt κ e t = β := by
  have hC : (0 : ℝ) ≤ edgeCap κ e := (edgeCap_pos h h').1.le
  have hsub := intermediate_value_Ioo hC
    ((gapAngleAt_continuous κ e).continuousOn
      (s := Set.Icc 0 (edgeCap κ e)))
  rw [gapAngleAt_zero, gapAngleAt_edgeCap h h'] at hsub
  obtain ⟨t, ht, hval⟩ := hsub ⟨hβ0, hβU⟩
  refine ⟨t, ⟨ht, hval⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro s ⟨hs, hsval⟩
  exact (gapAngleAt_strictMonoOn h h').injOn (Set.Ioo_subset_Icc_self hs)
    (Set.Ioo_subset_Icc_self ht) (hsval.trans hval.symm)

blocks.label: def:gap_length
blocks.title: the inverse: length of a prescribed gap
blocks.body:
For $\kappa$, an edge $e$ and a real $\beta$, let
  $\mathrm{gapLength}\,\kappa\,e\,\beta$ be the length produced by
  \cref{lem:gap_surjective} when $\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1} > 0$ and
  $0 < \beta < U_e$, chosen arbitrarily (junk) otherwise.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.gapLength
lean.code:
noncomputable def gapLength (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (e : ZMod n) (β : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if h : 0 < κ e ∧ 0 < κ (e + 1) ∧ 0 < β ∧ β < edgeWall κ e then
    (exists_unique_length_of_gap h.1 h.2.1 h.2.2.1 h.2.2.2).exists.choose
  else 0

blocks.title: the inverse inverts
blocks.body:
If $\kappa_e, \kappa_{e+1} > 0$ and $0 < \beta < U_e$ then
  $\gamma_e\bigl(\mathrm{gapLength}\,\kappa\,e\,\beta\bigr) = \beta$.

    \cref{def:gap_length} from the existence statement of
    \cref{lem:gap_surjective}.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.gapLength_spec
lean.code:
lemma gapLength_spec {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} {β : ℝ} (h : 0 < κ e)
    (h' : 0 < κ (e + 1)) (hβ0 : 0 < β) (hβU : β < edgeWall κ e) :
    gapAngleAt κ e (gapLength κ e β) = β := by
  rw [gapLength, dif_pos ⟨h, h', hβ0, hβU⟩]
  exact (exists_unique_length_of_gap h h' hβ0 hβU).exists.choose_spec.2

lemma gapLength_mem_Ioo {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} {β : ℝ} (h : 0 < κ e)

The external four-gap notes work with the osculating radii `r_i = 1/κ_i`;
inversion is order-reversing on `(0, ∞)`, so it swaps `min` and `max` and
leaves the wall ratio unchanged. -/

blocks.label: lem:gap_radius_cap
blocks.title: radius form of the cap
blocks.body:
Assume $\kappa_e, \kappa_{e+1} > 0$ and set $r_i = 1/\kappa_i$. Then
  $C_e = 2\,\min(r_e,\, r_{e+1})$.
  \begin{proof}
    
    Inversion $x \mapsto 1/x$ is order-reversing on $(0,\infty)$, so
    $\min(r_e, r_{e+1}) = 1/\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})$; the claim is then
    $C_e = 2/\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})$ restated.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.edgeCap_eq_radius
lean.code:
lemma edgeCap_eq_radius {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} (h : 0 < κ e)
    (h' : 0 < κ (e + 1)) :
    edgeCap κ e = 2 * min (1 / κ e) (1 / κ (e + 1)) := by
  rcases le_total (κ e) (κ (e + 1)) with hle | hle
  · rw [edgeCap, max_eq_right hle,
      min_eq_right (one_div_le_one_div_of_le h hle)]
    ring
  · rw [edgeCap, max_eq_left hle,
      min_eq_left (one_div_le_one_div_of_le h' hle)]
    ring

blocks.label: lem:gap_radius_wall
blocks.title: radius form of the wall

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.edgeWall_eq_radius
lean.code:
lemma edgeWall_eq_radius {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} (h : 0 < κ e)
    (h' : 0 < κ (e + 1)) :
    edgeWall κ e = Real.pi / 2 +
      Real.arcsin (min (1 / κ e) (1 / κ (e + 1)) /
        max (1 / κ e) (1 / κ (e + 1))) := by
  rcases le_total (κ e) (κ (e + 1)) with hle | hle
  · rw [edgeWall, max_eq_right hle, min_eq_left hle,
      min_eq_right (one_div_le_one_div_of_le h hle),
      max_eq_left (one_div_le_one_div_of_le h hle)]
    have harg : (1 : ℝ) / κ (e + 1) / (1 / κ e) = κ e / κ (e + 1) := by
      field_simp [h.ne', h'.ne']
    rw [harg]
  · rw [edgeWall, max_eq_left hle, min_eq_right hle,
      min_eq_left (one_div_le_one_div_of_le h' hle),
      max_eq_right (one_div_le_one_div_of_le h' hle)]
    have harg : (1 : ℝ) / κ e / (1 / κ (e + 1)) = κ (e + 1) / κ e := by
      field_simp [h.ne', h'.ne']
    rw [harg]

blocks.title: Repackaging a gap vector as a realization

blocks.label: thm:realizes_of_gap_data
blocks.title: realizability from edge-coordinate data
blocks.body:
Let $n \ge 3$, let $\kappa_i > 0$ for every $i$, and let $\ell$ satisfy
  \[
    \forall e,\; 0 < \ell_e < C_e,
    \qquad E(\kappa,\ell) = 0,
    \qquad \sum_{e} \beta_e = 2\pi .
  \]
  Then $\mathrm{RealizesR2}\,\kappa$.
  \begin{proof}
    
    The first hypothesis is $\mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell$ by
    \cref{lem:moderate_arc_edge}; the third is $T(\kappa,\ell) = 2\pi$ by
    \cref{lem:gap_sum}. With the closure hypothesis and positivity of $\kappa$
    in hand, \cref{thm:convex_simple} supplies
    $\mathrm{IsSimplePolygon}\,(P(\kappa,\ell))$. The four conjuncts of
    \cref{def:discrete_realizes} are then exactly what we have, witnessed by
    $\ell$.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.realizesR2_of_gapData
lean.code:
theorem realizesR2_of_gapData [NeZero n] {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hℓ : ∀ e : ZMod n, 0 < ℓ e ∧ ℓ e < edgeCap κ e)
    (hE : closureGap κ ℓ = 0)
    (hsum : ∑ e : ZMod n, gapAngle κ ℓ e = 2 * Real.pi) :
    RealizesR2 κ := by
  have hMA : ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ := (moderateArc_zero_iff_edge hκ).2 hℓ
  have hT : turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * Real.pi := by
    rw [← sum_gapAngle]
    exact hsum
  exact ⟨ℓ, hMA, hE, hT, isSimplePolygon_of_turningPositive hn hMA hκ hE hT⟩

deps.title: the turning sum is the sum of the gaps
deps.label: lem:gap_sum

deps.title: the moderate-arc domain is a box in $\ell$
deps.label: lem:moderate_arc_edge

blocks.label: thm:realizes_of_gap_vector
blocks.title: realizability from a gap vector
blocks.body:
Let $n \ge 3$ and $\kappa_i > 0$ for every $i$, and let
  $\beta \colon \mathbb{Z}/n \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy
  \[
    \forall k,\; 0 < \beta_k < U_k,
    \qquad \sum_k \beta_k = 2\pi,
    \qquad E\bigl(\kappa,\ \mathrm{gapLength}\,\kappa\,\cdot\,\beta_\cdot\bigr)
             = 0 .
  \]
  Then $\mathrm{RealizesR2}\,\kappa$, realized by the edge lengths
  $\ell_e = \mathrm{gapLength}\,\kappa\,e\,\beta_e$, and those lengths are
  strictly positive.
  \begin{proof}
    
    Put $\ell_e = \mathrm{gapLength}\,\kappa\,e\,\beta_e$. By
    \cref{lem:gap_length_spec,lem:gap_length_mem} each $\ell_e$ lies in $(0, C_e)$ --- in
    particular every edge length is strictly positive --- and
    $\gamma_e(\ell_e) = \beta_e$, i.e.\ the gaps of the configuration
    $(\kappa,\ell)$ are the prescribed $\beta$. So
    $\sum_e \beta_e = 2\pi$ is the third hypothesis of
    \cref{thm:realizes_of_gap_data} and the assumed vanishing of the closure
    gap is its second. Apply \cref{thm:realizes_of_gap_data}.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.realizesR2_of_gapVector
lean.code:
theorem realizesR2_of_gapVector [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) {β : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (hβ : ∀ k : ZMod n, 0 < β k ∧ β k < edgeWall κ k)
    (hsum : ∑ k : ZMod n, β k = 2 * Real.pi)
    (hE : closureGap κ (fun e => gapLength κ e (β e)) = 0) :
    RealizesR2 κ := by
  have hmem : ∀ e : ZMod n, 0 < gapLength κ e (β e) ∧
      gapLength κ e (β e) < edgeCap κ e := fun e =>
    gapLength_mem_Ioo (hκ e) (hκ (e + 1)) (hβ e).1 (hβ e).2
  refine realizesR2_of_gapData hn hκ hmem hE ?_
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun e _ =>
    show gapAngle κ (fun e' => gapLength κ e' (β e')) e = β e from
      gapLength_spec (hκ e) (hκ (e + 1)) (hβ e).1 (hβ e).2]
  exact hsum

/-! ## The global step of the zigzag argument

Purely order-theoretic — no curvature, no closure, no geometry. The local
consequence feeding `exists_of_high_neighbour` is an explicit hypothesis,
precisely so that this file takes on none of the risk of the unaudited
external local certificates. -/

deps.title: the inverse lands strictly inside the cap
deps.label: lem:gap_length_mem

blocks.title: The global step of the zigzag argument

blocks.tex:
The zigzag argument of the external pipeline is organized as: a family of
\emph{local} certificates, one per consecutive pair of curvature peaks, each of
which either finishes the proof outright or forces a comparison on the
intervening radius; plus a \emph{global} step which observes that those forced
comparisons cannot all hold. Only the global step is proved here. It is
purely order-theoretic --- no curvature, no closure, no geometry --- and it is
stated with the local consequence as a hypothesis, precisely so that the
chapter takes on none of the risk of the unaudited local certificates.

blocks.label: lem:high_neighbour_cyclic
blocks.title: a cyclic family cannot beat both neighbours everywhere
blocks.body:
Let $m \ge 1$ and $H \colon \mathbb{Z}/m \to \mathbb{R}$. Then there is an
  index $i$ with
  \[
    H_{i+1} \le H_i \qquad\text{and}\qquad H_{i+1} \le H_{i+2}.
  \]
  \begin{proof}
    
    $\mathbb{Z}/m$ is a nonempty finite type, so $H$ attains its minimum at
    some $j$. Take $i = j - 1$, so that $i + 1 = j$ and $i + 2 = j + 1$. Then
    $H_{i+1} = H_j \le H_{i}$ and $H_{i+1} = H_j \le H_{j+1} = H_{i+2}$, both
    by minimality.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.exists_le_both_neighbours
lean.code:
lemma exists_le_both_neighbours {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] (H : ZMod m → ℝ) :
    ∃ i : ZMod m, H (i + 1) ≤ H i ∧ H (i + 1) ≤ H (i + 2) := by
  obtain ⟨j, -, hj⟩ :=
    Finset.exists_min_image Finset.univ H Finset.univ_nonempty
  have h1 : j - 1 + 1 = j := sub_add_cancel j 1
  have h2 : j - 1 + 2 = j + 1 := by ring
  exact ⟨j - 1, by rw [h1]; exact hj _ (Finset.mem_univ _),
    by rw [h1, h2]; exact hj _ (Finset.mem_univ _)⟩

blocks.label: lem:high_neighbour_global
blocks.title: global step: some carrier has opposite endpoint defects
blocks.body:
Let $m \ge 1$, let $H \colon \mathbb{Z}/m \to \mathbb{R}$, and let
  $P \colon \mathbb{Z}/m \to \mathrm{Prop}$ be any predicate. Assume the
  \emph{high-neighbour consequence}
  \[
    \forall i,\quad \neg P\,i \;\Longrightarrow\;
      \bigl(H_{i+1} > H_i \ \text{ or }\ H_{i+1} > H_{i+2}\bigr).
  \]
  Then $P\,i$ holds for some $i$.
  \begin{proof}
    
    Suppose not, so $\neg P\,i$ for every $i$ and hence
    $H_{i+1} > H_i$ or $H_{i+1} > H_{i+2}$ for every $i$. Apply
    \cref{lem:high_neighbour_cyclic} to get an index $i$ with
    $H_{i+1} \le H_i$ and $H_{i+1} \le H_{i+2}$; both disjuncts at that $i$
    are contradicted.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.exists_of_high_neighbour
lean.code:
lemma exists_of_high_neighbour {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] {H : ZMod m → ℝ}
    {P : ZMod m → Prop}
    (hloc : ∀ i : ZMod m, ¬P i → H i < H (i + 1) ∨ H (i + 2) < H (i + 1)) :
    ∃ i, P i := by
  by_contra hall
  rw [not_exists] at hall
  obtain ⟨i, h1, h2⟩ := exists_le_both_neighbours H
  rcases hloc i (hall i) with hlt | hlt
  · exact absurd h1 (not_le.2 hlt)
  · exact absurd h2 (not_le.2 hlt)

deps.title: a cyclic family cannot beat both neighbours everywhere
deps.label: lem:high_neighbour_cyclic

blocks.tex: A strict local maximum of a cyclic word has both neighbours smaller. A strict local minimum has both neighbours larger. The retained order lemmas connect these notions to plateau extrema.

blocks.label: def:zz_local_max
blocks.title: strict local maximum
blocks.body:
For $w : \ZMod n \to \mathbb{R}$ and $i \in \ZMod n$, say $i$ is a \emph{strict local
  maximum} of $w$, written $\mathrm{IsStrictLocalMax}\,w\,i$, when
  $w_{i-1} < w_i$ and $w_{i+1} < w_i$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.IsStrictLocalMax
lean.code:
def IsStrictLocalMax (w : ZMod n → ℝ) (i : ZMod n) : Prop :=
  w (i - 1) < w i ∧ w (i + 1) < w i

chapters.title: The four-point converse: orthogonal diagonals, scaling, and cap bases

blocks.tex: The four-point base is an explicit positive orthogonal quadrilateral. Its axis lengths solve the four curvature equations; the retained identities also supply the anchor rank calculations.

blocks.label: def:n4c_four_profile
blocks.title: four-point profile
blocks.body:
For $x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3\in\mathbb{R}$, $\mathrm{fourProfile}(x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3)$
  is the function $\ZMod 4\to\mathbb{R}$ sending $i$ to $x_{i}$, read through
  the canonical representative $i.\mathrm{val}\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.fourProfile
lean.code:
def fourProfile (x₀ x₁ x₂ x₃ : ℝ) : ZMod 4 → ℝ := fun i =>
  ![x₀, x₁, x₂, x₃] ⟨i.val, i.val_lt⟩

blocks.label: def:n4c_orthogonal_quad
blocks.title: orthogonal-diagonal quadrilateral
blocks.body:
For $a,b,c,d>0$ let $\mathrm{orthogonalQuad}(a,b,c,d):\ZMod 4\to\mathbb{C}$
  be the vertex map
  \[
    0\mapsto a,\qquad 1\mapsto b\,i,\qquad 2\mapsto -c,\qquad 3\mapsto -d\,i .
  \]
  Its two diagonals are the segments $[-c,a]$ of the real axis and
  $[-d\,i,b\,i]$ of the imaginary axis, so they meet orthogonally at the
  origin, and $a,b,c,d$ are the four half-diagonals.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalQuad
lean.code:
def orthogonalQuad (a b c d : ℝ) : ZMod 4 → ℂ := fun i =>
  ![(a : ℂ), (b : ℂ) * Complex.I, -(c : ℂ), -(d : ℂ) * Complex.I]
    ⟨i.val, i.val_lt⟩

blocks.label: lem:n4c_quad_simple
blocks.title: the orthogonal quadrilateral is simple
blocks.body:
For $a,b,c,d>0$ the polygon $\mathrm{orthogonalQuad}(a,b,c,d)$ is simple:
  consecutive vertices are distinct, consecutive closed edges meet exactly in
  their shared vertex, and non-adjacent closed edges are disjoint.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.isSimplePolygon_orthogonalQuad
lean.code:
theorem isSimplePolygon_orthogonalQuad {a b c d : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hc : 0 < c) (hd : 0 < d) :
    IsSimplePolygon (orthogonalQuad a b c d) :=
  ⟨orthogonalQuad_edge_ne ha hb hc hd,
    orthogonalQuad_consecutive_inter ha hb hc hd,
    orthogonalQuad_nonadjacent_disjoint ha hb hc hd⟩

blocks.tex:
Each closed edge is a segment with one endpoint on the real axis and one on
  the imaginary axis, so a point $z$ of the edge from $x\in\mathbb{R}$ to
  $y\,i$ has $\Re z = r x$ and $\Im z = s y$ with $r,s\ge 0$, $r+s=1$.  Two
  such segments sharing an axis endpoint but with opposite-sign partners meet
  only in that endpoint: if the two real endpoints $x_+ > 0 > x_-$ are
  opposite in sign, then $\Re z\ge 0$ from one description and $\Re z\le 0$
  from the other, forcing $\Re z = 0$ and hence the coefficient of the real
  endpoint to vanish in each; the same argument with the roles of the axes
  exchanged handles a shared imaginary endpoint.  For the two non-adjacent
  pairs, the same coordinate reading forces $\Re z = \Im z = 0$, i.e.\ $z=0$,
  and $0$ lies on no edge because $r+s=1$ makes at least one of $rx$, $sy$
  nonzero.  Distinctness of consecutive vertices is immediate from
  positivity.

blocks.label: lem:n4c_realizes_menger_orthogonal
blocks.title: curvature of the orthogonal quadrilateral
blocks.body:
Let $a,b,c,d>0$ and $A,B,C,D>0$ satisfy the four Pythagorean relations
  \[
    A^2=a^2+b^2,\quad B^2=b^2+c^2,\quad C^2=c^2+d^2,\quad D^2=d^2+a^2 ,
  \]
  and put
  \[
    \kappa_0=\frac{2a}{AD},\quad \kappa_1=\frac{2b}{AB},\quad
    \kappa_2=\frac{2c}{BC},\quad \kappa_3=\frac{2d}{CD} .
  \]
  Then $\mathrm{RealizesMenger}\,\mathrm{fourProfile}(\kappa_0,\dots,\kappa_3)$,
  witnessed by $\mathrm{orthogonalQuad}(a,b,c,d)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.realizesMenger_fourProfile_of_orthogonal
lean.code:
theorem realizesMenger_fourProfile_of_orthogonal
    {k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ a b c d A B C D : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hc : 0 < c) (hd : 0 < d)
    (hA : 0 < A) (hB : 0 < B) (hC : 0 < C) (hD : 0 < D)
    (hAsq : A ^ 2 = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2) (hBsq : B ^ 2 = b ^ 2 + c ^ 2)
    (hCsq : C ^ 2 = c ^ 2 + d ^ 2) (hDsq : D ^ 2 = d ^ 2 + a ^ 2)
    (hk₀ : 2 * a / (A * D) = k₀) (hk₁ : 2 * b / (A * B) = k₁)
    (hk₂ : 2 * c / (B * C) = k₂) (hk₃ : 2 * d / (C * D) = k₃) :
    RealizesMenger (fourProfile k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃) := by
  refine ⟨orthogonalQuad a b c d, isSimplePolygon_orthogonalQuad ha hb hc hd, ?_⟩
  intro i
  rcases zmod4_cases i with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl
  · change signedMengerR2 (orthogonalQuad a b c d 3) (orthogonalQuad a b c d 0)
        (orthogonalQuad a b c d 1) = k₀
    rw [orthogonalQuad_three, orthogonalQuad_zero, orthogonalQuad_one,
      signedMenger_orthogonal_zero ha hb hd hA hD hAsq (by nlinarith), hk₀]
  · change signedMengerR2 (orthogonalQuad a b c d 0) (orthogonalQuad a b c d 1)
        (orthogonalQuad a b c d 2) = k₁
    rw [orthogonalQuad_zero, orthogonalQuad_one, orthogonalQuad_two,
      signedMenger_orthogonal_one ha hb hc hA hB hAsq hBsq, hk₁]
  · change signedMengerR2 (orthogonalQuad a b c d 1) (orthogonalQuad a b c d 2)
        (orthogonalQuad a b c d 3) = k₂
    rw [orthogonalQuad_one, orthogonalQuad_two, orthogonalQuad_three,
      signedMenger_orthogonal_two hb hc hd hB hC hBsq hCsq, hk₂]
  · change signedMengerR2 (orthogonalQuad a b c d 2) (orthogonalQuad a b c d 3)
        (orthogonalQuad a b c d 0) = k₃
    rw [orthogonalQuad_two, orthogonalQuad_three, orthogonalQuad_zero,
      signedMenger_orthogonal_three ha hc hd hC hD hCsq hDsq, hk₃]

blocks.tex:
By \cref{lem:n4c_quad_simple} the quadrilateral is simple, so only the four
  curvature values must be checked, one per residue.  The distance between a
  real point $x$ and an imaginary point $y\,i$ is $\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$; under the
  four Pythagorean hypotheses the six pairwise distances among consecutive
  triples are exactly $A,B,C,D$ and the two diagonals $a+c$, $b+d$.  At vertex
  $0$ the triple is $(-d\,i,\;a,\;b\,i)$; its two adjacent side lengths are
  $D$ and $A$, and twice the signed area of the triangle is $2a(b+d)/2$, so
  the signed Menger curvature is $2a/(AD)$.  The three remaining residues are
  the same computation with the labels rotated.

The four curvature equations of \cref{lem:n4c_realizes_menger_orthogonal} are
solved by an exact rational formula for the \emph{squared} side lengths.

blocks.label: def:n4c_delta
blocks.title: alternation discriminant
blocks.body: $\Delta(\kappa) = \kappa_0^2\kappa_2^2 - \kappa_1^2\kappa_3^2$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalDelta
lean.code:
def orthogonalDelta (k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  k₀ ^ 2 * k₂ ^ 2 - k₁ ^ 2 * k₃ ^ 2

blocks.label: def:n4c_squareA
blocks.title: first squared side length
blocks.body: $\mathcal A = 4(\kappa_2^2-\kappa_3^2)/\Delta$, intended as $A^2$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalA2
lean.code:
noncomputable def orthogonalA2 (k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  4 * (k₂ ^ 2 - k₃ ^ 2) / orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃

blocks.label: def:n4c_squareB
blocks.title: second squared side length
blocks.body: $\mathcal B = 4(\kappa_0^2-\kappa_3^2)/\Delta$, intended as $B^2$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalB2
lean.code:
noncomputable def orthogonalB2 (k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  4 * (k₀ ^ 2 - k₃ ^ 2) / orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃

blocks.label: def:n4c_squareC
blocks.title: third squared side length
blocks.body: $\mathcal C = 4(\kappa_0^2-\kappa_1^2)/\Delta$, intended as $C^2$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalC2
lean.code:
noncomputable def orthogonalC2 (k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  4 * (k₀ ^ 2 - k₁ ^ 2) / orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃

blocks.label: def:n4c_squareD
blocks.title: fourth squared side length
blocks.body: $\mathcal D = 4(\kappa_2^2-\kappa_1^2)/\Delta$, intended as $D^2$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalD2
lean.code:
noncomputable def orthogonalD2 (k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  4 * (k₂ ^ 2 - k₁ ^ 2) / orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃

blocks.tex:
The four Pythagorean relations then hold \emph{identically} in the
$\kappa_i$; no positivity is needed, only $\Delta\ne 0$.  In each case the
common factor cancels and what remains is one two-term telescoping of
$\Delta = \kappa_0^2\kappa_2^2-\kappa_1^2\kappa_3^2$.

blocks.label: lem:n4c_identityA
blocks.title: first Pythagorean identity
blocks.body:
If $\Delta\ne 0$ then
  $\mathcal A = \tfrac14\kappa_0^2\,\mathcal A\mathcal D
     + \tfrac14\kappa_1^2\,\mathcal A\mathcal B$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalA2_identity
lean.code:
lemma orthogonalA2_identity {k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ}
    (hΔ : orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ ≠ 0) :
    orthogonalA2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ =
      k₀ ^ 2 * orthogonalA2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalD2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 +
        k₁ ^ 2 * orthogonalA2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalB2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 := by
  unfold orthogonalA2 orthogonalB2 orthogonalD2
  field_simp [hΔ]
  unfold orthogonalDelta
  ring

blocks.tex:
Clearing denominators and cancelling the common factor
  $4(\kappa_2^2-\kappa_3^2)/\Delta$ reduces the claim to
  $\kappa_0^2(\kappa_2^2-\kappa_1^2)+\kappa_1^2(\kappa_0^2-\kappa_3^2) = \Delta$,
  i.e.\ to
  $\kappa_0^2\kappa_2^2-\kappa_0^2\kappa_1^2
   +\kappa_0^2\kappa_1^2-\kappa_1^2\kappa_3^2
   = \kappa_0^2\kappa_2^2-\kappa_1^2\kappa_3^2$.

blocks.label: lem:n4c_identityB
blocks.title: second Pythagorean identity
blocks.body:
If $\Delta\ne 0$ then
  $\mathcal B = \tfrac14\kappa_1^2\,\mathcal A\mathcal B
     + \tfrac14\kappa_2^2\,\mathcal B\mathcal C$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalB2_identity
lean.code:
lemma orthogonalB2_identity {k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ}
    (hΔ : orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ ≠ 0) :
    orthogonalB2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ =
      k₁ ^ 2 * orthogonalA2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalB2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 +
        k₂ ^ 2 * orthogonalB2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalC2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 := by
  unfold orthogonalA2 orthogonalB2 orthogonalC2
  field_simp [hΔ]
  unfold orthogonalDelta
  ring

blocks.tex:
Cancelling $4(\kappa_0^2-\kappa_3^2)/\Delta$ leaves
  $\kappa_1^2(\kappa_2^2-\kappa_3^2)+\kappa_2^2(\kappa_0^2-\kappa_1^2) = \Delta$,
  again a telescoping in $\kappa_1^2\kappa_2^2$.

blocks.label: lem:n4c_identityC
blocks.title: third Pythagorean identity
blocks.body:
If $\Delta\ne 0$ then
  $\mathcal C = \tfrac14\kappa_2^2\,\mathcal B\mathcal C
     + \tfrac14\kappa_3^2\,\mathcal C\mathcal D$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalC2_identity
lean.code:
lemma orthogonalC2_identity {k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ}
    (hΔ : orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ ≠ 0) :
    orthogonalC2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ =
      k₂ ^ 2 * orthogonalB2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalC2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 +
        k₃ ^ 2 * orthogonalC2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalD2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 := by
  unfold orthogonalB2 orthogonalC2 orthogonalD2
  field_simp [hΔ]
  unfold orthogonalDelta
  ring

blocks.tex:
Cancelling $4(\kappa_0^2-\kappa_1^2)/\Delta$ leaves
  $\kappa_2^2(\kappa_0^2-\kappa_3^2)+\kappa_3^2(\kappa_2^2-\kappa_1^2) = \Delta$,
  telescoping in $\kappa_2^2\kappa_3^2$.

blocks.label: lem:n4c_identityD
blocks.title: fourth Pythagorean identity
blocks.body:
If $\Delta\ne 0$ then
  $\mathcal D = \tfrac14\kappa_3^2\,\mathcal C\mathcal D
     + \tfrac14\kappa_0^2\,\mathcal A\mathcal D$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalD2_identity
lean.code:
lemma orthogonalD2_identity {k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ}
    (hΔ : orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ ≠ 0) :
    orthogonalD2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ =
      k₃ ^ 2 * orthogonalC2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalD2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 +
        k₀ ^ 2 * orthogonalA2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalD2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 := by
  unfold orthogonalA2 orthogonalC2 orthogonalD2
  field_simp [hΔ]
  unfold orthogonalDelta
  ring

blocks.tex:
Cancelling $4(\kappa_2^2-\kappa_1^2)/\Delta$ leaves
  $\kappa_3^2(\kappa_0^2-\kappa_1^2)+\kappa_0^2(\kappa_2^2-\kappa_3^2) = \Delta$,
  telescoping in $\kappa_0^2\kappa_3^2$.

\texttt{RealizesMenger} records a simple polygon with the right curvatures.
The project's realizability predicate $\mathrm{RealizesR2}$ asks for more: a
positive edge-length vector satisfying every strict arcsine \emph{moderate
wall}, closing, with total turn exactly $2\pi$, and with simple development.
The orthogonal quadrilateral supplies all four at once.

blocks.label: thm:n4c_realization_data
blocks.title: the orthogonal quadrilateral is a moderate development
blocks.body:
Under the hypotheses of \cref{lem:n4c_realizes_menger_orthogonal}, the
  length vector $\ell=\mathrm{fourProfile}(A,B,C,D)$ satisfies
  \[
    \mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell,\qquad
    \mathrm{closureGap}\,\kappa\,\ell = 0,\qquad
    \mathrm{turningSum}\,\kappa\,\ell = 2\pi,
  \]
  and the development $\mathrm{polygonR2}\,\kappa\,\ell$ is simple.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonal_realization_data
lean.code:
theorem orthogonal_realization_data
    {k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ a b c d A B C D : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hc : 0 < c) (hd : 0 < d)
    (hA : 0 < A) (hB : 0 < B) (hC : 0 < C) (hD : 0 < D)
    (hAsq : A ^ 2 = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2) (hBsq : B ^ 2 = b ^ 2 + c ^ 2)
    (hCsq : C ^ 2 = c ^ 2 + d ^ 2) (hDsq : D ^ 2 = d ^ 2 + a ^ 2)
    (hk₀ : 2 * a / (A * D) = k₀) (hk₁ : 2 * b / (A * B) = k₁)
    (hk₂ : 2 * c / (B * C) = k₂) (hk₃ : 2 * d / (C * D) = k₃) :
    ModerateArc 0 (fourProfile k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃) (fourProfile A B C D) ∧
      closureGap (fourProfile k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃) (fourProfile A B C D) = 0 ∧
      turningSum (fourProfile k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃) (fourProfile A B C D) =
        2 * Real.pi ∧
      IsSimplePolygon
        (polygonR2 (fourProfile k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃) (fourProfile A B C D)) := by
  let ℓ : ZMod 4 → ℝ := fourProfile A B C D
  have hk₀pos : 0 < k₀ := by rw [← hk₀]; positivity
  have hk₁pos : 0 < k₁ := by rw [← hk₁]; positivity
  have hk₂pos : 0 < k₂ := by rw [← hk₂]; positivity
  have hk₃pos : 0 < k₃ := by rw [← hk₃]; positivity
  have haA : a < A := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos hb]
  have hbA : b < A := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos ha]
  have hbB : b < B := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos hc]
  have hcB : c < B := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos hb]
  have hcC : c < C := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos hd]
  have hdC : d < C := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos hc]
  have hdD : d < D := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos ha]
  have haD : a < D := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos hd]
  have hMA : ModerateArc 0 (fourProfile k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃) ℓ := by
    rw [moderateArc_zero_iff]
    intro i
    rcases zmod4_cases i with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl
    · simp only [ℓ, fourProfile_zero]
      rw [abs_of_pos hk₀pos, ← hk₀]
      refine ⟨hA, ?_, ?_⟩
      · calc
          2 * a / (A * D) * (D / 2) = a / A := by field_simp
          _ < 1 := (div_lt_one hA).2 haA
      · calc
          2 * a / (A * D) * (A / 2) = a / D := by field_simp
          _ < 1 := (div_lt_one hD).2 haD
    · simp only [ℓ, fourProfile_one]
      rw [abs_of_pos hk₁pos, ← hk₁]
      refine ⟨hB, ?_, ?_⟩
      · calc
          2 * b / (A * B) * (A / 2) = b / B := by field_simp
          _ < 1 := (div_lt_one hB).2 hbB
      · calc
          2 * b / (A * B) * (B / 2) = b / A := by field_simp
          _ < 1 := (div_lt_one hA).2 hbA
    · simp only [ℓ, fourProfile_two]
      rw [abs_of_pos hk₂pos, ← hk₂]
      refine ⟨hC, ?_, ?_⟩
      · calc
          2 * c / (B * C) * (B / 2) = c / C := by field_simp
          _ < 1 := (div_lt_one hC).2 hcC
      · calc
          2 * c / (B * C) * (C / 2) = c / B := by field_simp
          _ < 1 := (div_lt_one hB).2 hcB
    · simp only [ℓ, fourProfile_three]
      rw [abs_of_pos hk₃pos, ← hk₃]
  -- … (truncated)

blocks.tex:
Write the four turns.  By definition
  $\theta_i = \arcsin(\kappa_i\ell_{i-1}/2) + \arcsin(\kappa_i\ell_i/2)$, and
  with $\kappa_0=2a/(AD)$, $\ell_3=D$, $\ell_0=A$ we get
  $\kappa_0\ell_3/2 = a/A$ and $\kappa_0\ell_0/2 = a/D$; cyclically,
  \[
    \theta_0 = \arcsin\tfrac aA + \arcsin\tfrac aD,\quad
    \theta_1 = \arcsin\tfrac bA + \arcsin\tfrac bB,\quad
    \theta_2 = \arcsin\tfrac cB + \arcsin\tfrac cC,\quad
    \theta_3 = \arcsin\tfrac dC + \arcsin\tfrac dD .
  \]
  \emph{Walls.}  Each Pythagorean relation makes a leg strictly shorter than
  its hypotenuse ($a<A$ because $b>0$, and so on), so every argument above
  lies strictly inside $(0,1)$ and each moderate wall is strict.

  \emph{Turn sum.}  The key elementary identity is
  \[
    h^2 = x^2+y^2,\ x,y,h>0
    \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
    \arcsin\tfrac xh + \arcsin\tfrac yh = \tfrac\pi2 ,
  \]
  which holds because $\sqrt{1-(x/h)^2} = y/h$ turns
  $\arccos(x/h)$ into $\arcsin(y/h)$, and
  $\arccos = \pi/2 - \arcsin$.  Regrouping the eight arcsines by
  \emph{hypotenuse} rather than by vertex,
  \[
    \sum_i\theta_i
    = \Bigl(\arcsin\tfrac aA+\arcsin\tfrac bA\Bigr)
    + \Bigl(\arcsin\tfrac bB+\arcsin\tfrac cB\Bigr)
    + \Bigl(\arcsin\tfrac cC+\arcsin\tfrac dC\Bigr)
    + \Bigl(\arcsin\tfrac dD+\arcsin\tfrac aD\Bigr)
    = 4\cdot\tfrac\pi2 = 2\pi .
  \]
  This is the polygon's four right angles at the diagonal crossing, read
  through the development.

  \emph{Closure.}  The same identity, in exponential form,
  $e^{\,i\arcsin(x/h)} = y/h + i\,x/h$, evaluates each developed direction:
  there is one global unit phase $\rho$ with
  $e^{\,i\psi_0}=\rho u_0$, \dots, $e^{\,i\psi_3}=\rho u_3$, where $u_0,\dots,u_3$
  are the four explicit unit vectors
  $(-a+ib)/A$, $(-c-ib)/B$, $(c-id)/C$, $(a+id)/D$ --- the normalized side
  vectors of the quadrilateral.  Then
  $A u_0 + B u_1 + C u_2 + D u_3 = (-a+ib)+(-c-ib)+(c-id)+(a+id) = 0$,
  so $\mathrm{closureGap} = \rho\cdot 0 = 0$.

  \emph{Simplicity.}  All four turns are positive and sum to $2\pi$, so the
  development is convex, hence simple (\cref{thm:convex_simple}).

chapters.title: The four-arc rectangle: boundary loops, sign windings, and interior zeros

blocks.tex:
Two ingredients are needed and are supplied here.

\begin{enumerate}
  \item A \emph{canonical} boundary parameterization
    (\texttt{FourArcRectangle.lean}).  The rectangle boundary is traversed
    counterclockwise from the midpoint of the right face, and the four faces
    occupy exactly the four arcs cut at $\tfrac18,\tfrac38,\tfrac58,\tfrac78$
    of the parameter interval.  Fixing this convention once is what lets the
    sign hypotheses in the second file be stated as four clean arc conditions.
  \item A \emph{sign-to-winding} lemma
    (\texttt{CrossedFourArcWinding.lean}).  If a loop's four arcs lie in the
    lower, left, right and upper open half-planes respectively --- the
    \emph{crossed} pattern, in which opposite arcs are on opposite sides ---
    then the loop misses the origin and has winding number exactly $1$.
\end{enumerate}

The chapter also collects four compactness lemmas used to make such an
argument survive a perturbation parameter $\varepsilon$: they turn ``positive
at every zero of the $\varepsilon=0$ slice'' into ``uniformly positive for all
small $\varepsilon$''.

\medskip

blocks.label: def:fad_square_x
blocks.title: abscissa of the standard square loop
blocks.body:
For $t$ in the unit interval,
  $X(t) = \max\bigl(-1,\min(1,|8t-4|-2)\bigr)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.fourArcSquareX
lean.code:
def fourArcSquareX (t : unitInterval) : ℝ :=
  max (-1) (min 1 (|8 * (t : ℝ) - 4| - 2))

blocks.label: def:fad_square_y
blocks.title: ordinate of the standard square loop

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.fourArcSquareY
lean.code:
def fourArcSquareY (t : unitInterval) : ℝ :=
  max (-1) (min 1 (max (2 - |8 * (t : ℝ) - 2|) (8 * (t : ℝ) - 8)))

blocks.tex:
Together $(X,Y)$ traverse $\partial[-1,1]^2$ once counterclockwise starting at
$(1,0)$: the right face on $[0,\tfrac18]\cup[\tfrac78,1]$, the top face on
$[\tfrac18,\tfrac38]$, the left face on $[\tfrac38,\tfrac58]$, the bottom face
on $[\tfrac58,\tfrac78]$.

blocks.label: lem:fad_square_cont
blocks.title: the square loop is continuous
blocks.body:
$X$ is continuous; likewise $Y$
  ($\mathrm{continuous\_fourArcSquareY}$).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.continuous_fourArcSquareX
lean.code:
lemma continuous_fourArcSquareX : Continuous fourArcSquareX := by
  unfold fourArcSquareX
  fun_prop

deps.title: abscissa of the standard square loop
deps.label: def:fad_square_x

blocks.tex: Compositions of $\max$, $\min$, $|\cdot|$ and affine maps.

blocks.label: lem:fad_square_mem
blocks.title: the square loop stays in the square
blocks.body:
$X(t)\in[-1,1]$ for every $t$; likewise $Y$
  ($\mathrm{fourArcSquareY\_mem\_Icc}$).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.fourArcSquareX_mem_Icc
lean.code:
lemma fourArcSquareX_mem_Icc (t : unitInterval) :
    fourArcSquareX t ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1 := by
  constructor
  · exact le_max_left _ _
  · exact max_le (by norm_num) (min_le_left _ _)

deps.title: abscissa of the standard square loop
deps.label: def:fad_square_x

blocks.tex:
The outer $\max(-1,\cdot)$ gives the lower bound; the inner $\min(1,\cdot)$
  gives the upper bound once the outer $\max$ is resolved.

blocks.label: lem:fad_faces_closed
blocks.title: the four closed faces
blocks.body:
$X(t)=1$ for $t\le\tfrac18$ or $t\ge\tfrac78$; $Y(t)=1$ for
  $\tfrac18\le t\le\tfrac38$; $X(t)=-1$ for $\tfrac38\le t\le\tfrac58$;
  $Y(t)=-1$ for $\tfrac58\le t\le\tfrac78$
  ($\mathrm{fourArcSquareY\_eq\_one\_of\_top}$,
  $\mathrm{fourArcSquareX\_eq\_neg\_one\_of\_left}$,
  $\mathrm{fourArcSquareY\_eq\_neg\_one\_of\_bottom}$).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.fourArcSquareX_eq_one_of_right
lean.code:
lemma fourArcSquareX_eq_one_of_right {t : unitInterval}
    (ht : (t : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 8 ∨ 7 / 8 ≤ (t : ℝ)) :
    fourArcSquareX t = 1 := by
  rcases ht with ht | ht
  · unfold fourArcSquareX
    rw [abs_of_nonpos (by linarith [t.2.1])]
    rw [min_eq_left (by linarith), max_eq_right (by norm_num)]
  · unfold fourArcSquareX
    rw [abs_of_nonneg (by linarith)]
    rw [min_eq_left (by linarith), max_eq_right (by norm_num)]

deps.label: def:fad_square_x

blocks.tex:
On each of the four parameter ranges the inner expression saturates its
  clamp: e.g.\ for $t\le\tfrac18$ one has $|8t-4|-2 = 2-8t \ge 1$, so the
  $\min$ returns $1$ and the $\max$ leaves it.

blocks.label: lem:fad_faces_open
blocks.title: the four open faces avoid the far edge
blocks.body:
On the \emph{open} right arc ($t\le\tfrac18$ or $t>\tfrac78$) one has
  $Y(t)>-1$; and cyclically for the other three arcs
  ($\mathrm{neg\_one\_lt\_fourArcSquareX\_of\_top}$,
  $\mathrm{fourArcSquareY\_lt\_one\_of\_left}$,
  $\mathrm{fourArcSquareX\_lt\_one\_of\_bottom}$).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.neg_one_lt_fourArcSquareY_of_right
lean.code:
lemma neg_one_lt_fourArcSquareY_of_right {t : unitInterval}
    (ht : (t : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 8 ∨ 7 / 8 < (t : ℝ)) :
    -1 < fourArcSquareY t := by
  rcases ht with ht | ht
  · unfold fourArcSquareY
    rw [abs_of_nonpos (by linarith)]
    rw [show 2 - -(8 * (t : ℝ) - 2) = 8 * (t : ℝ) by ring]
    have hinner : max (8 * (t : ℝ)) (8 * (t : ℝ) - 8) = 8 * (t : ℝ) :=
      max_eq_left (by linarith)
    rw [hinner, min_eq_right (by linarith), max_eq_right (by linarith [t.2.1])]
    norm_num at ht ⊢
    linarith [t.2.1]
  · unfold fourArcSquareY
    rw [abs_of_nonneg (by linarith)]
    rw [show 2 - (8 * (t : ℝ) - 2) = 4 - 8 * (t : ℝ) by ring]
    have hinner : max (4 - 8 * (t : ℝ)) (8 * (t : ℝ) - 8) =
        8 * (t : ℝ) - 8 := max_eq_right (by linarith)
    rw [hinner, min_eq_right (by linarith [t.2.2]), max_eq_right (by linarith)]
    norm_num at ht ⊢
    linarith

        (continuous_const.mul continuous_fourArcSquareY))⟩

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.fourArcRectangleBoundary_mem
lean.code:
theorem fourArcRectangleBoundary_mem
    {u₁ u₂ v₁ v₂ : ℝ} (hu : u₁ ≤ u₂) (hv : v₁ ≤ v₂)
    (t : unitInterval) :
    fourArcRectangleBoundary u₁ u₂ v₁ v₂ t ∈
      Set.Icc u₁ u₂ ×ˢ Set.Icc v₁ v₂ := by
  have hx := fourArcSquareX_mem_Icc t
  have hy := fourArcSquareY_mem_Icc t
  have hdu : 0 ≤ u₂ - u₁ := sub_nonneg.mpr hu
  have hdv : 0 ≤ v₂ - v₁ := sub_nonneg.mpr hv
  have hxlo : 0 ≤ (u₂ - u₁) * (1 + fourArcSquareX t) :=
    mul_nonneg hdu (by linarith [hx.1])
  have hxhi : 0 ≤ (u₂ - u₁) * (1 - fourArcSquareX t) :=
    mul_nonneg hdu (by linarith [hx.2])
  have hylo : 0 ≤ (v₂ - v₁) * (1 + fourArcSquareY t) :=
    mul_nonneg hdv (by linarith [hy.1])
  have hyhi : 0 ≤ (v₂ - v₁) * (1 - fourArcSquareY t) :=
    mul_nonneg hdv (by linarith [hy.2])
  constructor
  · constructor <;>
      simp only [fourArcRectangleBoundary, ContinuousMap.coe_mk] <;>
      nlinarith
  · constructor <;>
      simp only [fourArcRectangleBoundary, ContinuousMap.coe_mk] <;>
      nlinarith

blocks.title: Crossed four-arc signs force winding one

blocks.label: def:fad_crossed_pattern
blocks.title: crossed four-arc sign pattern
blocks.body:
A loop $\gamma$ in $\mathbb{C}$ has the \emph{crossed four-arc signs} when
  \begin{align*}
    \Im\gamma(t)&<0 &&\text{for } t\le\tfrac18 \text{ or } \tfrac78<t,\\
    \Re\gamma(t)&<0 &&\text{for } \tfrac18\le t<\tfrac38,\\
    \Re\gamma(t)&>0 &&\text{for } \tfrac38<t\le\tfrac58,\\
    \Im\gamma(t)&>0 &&\text{for } \tfrac58\le t<\tfrac78,
  \end{align*}
  together with the two corner conditions $\Im\gamma(\tfrac38)<0$ and
  $\Re\gamma(\tfrac78)<0$.

blocks.label: thm:fad_ne_zero
blocks.title: crossed signs exclude the origin
blocks.body: A loop with the crossed four-arc signs is nowhere zero.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ne_zero_of_crossed_fourArcs
lean.code:
theorem ne_zero_of_crossed_fourArcs
    (gamma : C(unitInterval, ℂ))
    (hright : ∀ t : unitInterval,
      ((t : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 8 ∨ 7 / 8 < (t : ℝ)) → (gamma t).im < 0)
    (htop : ∀ t : unitInterval,
      1 / 8 ≤ (t : ℝ) → (t : ℝ) < 3 / 8 → (gamma t).re < 0)
    (hleft : ∀ t : unitInterval,
      3 / 8 < (t : ℝ) → (t : ℝ) ≤ 5 / 8 → 0 < (gamma t).re)
    (hbottom : ∀ t : unitInterval,
      5 / 8 ≤ (t : ℝ) → (t : ℝ) < 7 / 8 → 0 < (gamma t).im)
    (htopLeft : ∀ t : unitInterval, (t : ℝ) = 3 / 8 → (gamma t).im < 0)
    (hbottomRight : ∀ t : unitInterval, (t : ℝ) = 7 / 8 → (gamma t).re < 0) :
    ∀ t, gamma t ≠ 0 := by
  intro t hzero
  have hre : (gamma t).re = 0 := by simpa using congrArg Complex.re hzero
  have him : (gamma t).im = 0 := by simpa using congrArg Complex.im hzero
  by_cases h1 : (t : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 8
  · linarith [hright t (Or.inl h1)]
  by_cases h3 : (t : ℝ) < 3 / 8
  · linarith [htop t (by linarith) h3]
  by_cases he3 : (t : ℝ) = 3 / 8
  · linarith [htopLeft t he3]
  have ht3 : 3 / 8 < (t : ℝ) :=
    lt_of_le_of_ne (le_of_not_gt h3) (Ne.symm he3)
  by_cases h5 : (t : ℝ) ≤ 5 / 8
  · linarith [hleft t ht3 h5]
  by_cases h7 : (t : ℝ) < 7 / 8
  · linarith [hbottom t (by linarith) h7]
  by_cases he7 : (t : ℝ) = 7 / 8
  · linarith [hbottomRight t he7]
  · have ht7 : 7 / 8 < (t : ℝ) :=
      lt_of_le_of_ne (le_of_not_gt h7) (Ne.symm he7)
    linarith [hright t (Or.inr ht7)]

blocks.tex:
Every parameter lies in one of the four arcs, and on each the corresponding
  strict inequality forbids the value $0$; the two corner hypotheses cover the
  two parameters $\tfrac38$ and $\tfrac78$ at which the arc conditions
  constrain only the coordinate that is allowed to vanish there.

blocks.label: thm:fad_winding_one
blocks.title: crossed signs give winding number one
blocks.body:
A nowhere-zero loop $\gamma$ with $\gamma(0)=\gamma(1)$ and the crossed
  four-arc signs has $\mathrm{windingNumberC}\,\gamma = 1$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.windingNumberC_eq_one_of_crossed_fourArcs
lean.code:
theorem windingNumberC_eq_one_of_crossed_fourArcs
    (gamma : C(unitInterval, ℂ)) (hgamma : ∀ t, gamma t ≠ 0)
    (hloop : gamma 0 = gamma 1)
    (hright : ∀ t : unitInterval,
      ((t : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 8 ∨ 7 / 8 < (t : ℝ)) → (gamma t).im < 0)
    (htop : ∀ t : unitInterval,
      1 / 8 ≤ (t : ℝ) → (t : ℝ) < 3 / 8 → (gamma t).re < 0)
    (hleft : ∀ t : unitInterval,
      3 / 8 < (t : ℝ) → (t : ℝ) ≤ 5 / 8 → 0 < (gamma t).re)
    (hbottom : ∀ t : unitInterval,
      5 / 8 ≤ (t : ℝ) → (t : ℝ) < 7 / 8 → 0 < (gamma t).im)
    (htopLeft : ∀ t : unitInterval, (t : ℝ) = 3 / 8 → (gamma t).im < 0)
    (hbottomRight : ∀ t : unitInterval, (t : ℝ) = 7 / 8 → (gamma t).re < 0) :
    Gluck.windingNumberC gamma hgamma = 1 := by
  let H : C(unitInterval × unitInterval, ℂ) :=
    ⟨fun st ↦ crossedFourArcModel st.2 +
      (st.1 : ℝ) • (gamma st.2 - crossedFourArcModel st.2), by fun_prop⟩
  have hH : ∀ st, H st ≠ 0 := fun st ↦ crossed_four_arc_line_homotopy_ne_aux
    gamma hright htop hleft hbottom htopLeft hbottomRight st.1 st.2
  have hzero : ∀ t, H (0, t) = crossedFourArcModel t := by
    intro t
    simp [H]
  have hone : ∀ t, H (1, t) = gamma t := by
    intro t
    simp [H]
  have hHloop : ∀ s, H (s, 0) = H (s, 1) := by
    intro s
    simp only [H, ContinuousMap.coe_mk]
    rw [crossed_four_arc_model_loop_aux, hloop]
  have hwind := Gluck.windingNumberC_eq_of_homotopy crossedFourArcModel gamma
    crossed_four_arc_model_ne_aux hgamma H hH hzero hone hHloop
  exact hwind ▸ crossed_four_arc_model_winding_aux

blocks.tex:
Compare $\gamma$ with the explicit model loop
  $M(t) = e^{\,i\varphi(t)}$, where $\varphi$ is the piecewise-affine phase
  \[
    \varphi(t) = \tfrac{9\pi}{8} + \pi t + 2\pi\max\bigl(0,\min(t-\tfrac38,\tfrac12)\bigr),
  \]
  which is $\tfrac{9\pi}{8}+\pi t$ for $t\le\tfrac38$, then
  $\tfrac{3\pi}{8}+3\pi t$ on $[\tfrac38,\tfrac78]$, then
  $\tfrac{17\pi}{8}+\pi t$.  Its total increase is
  $\varphi(1)-\varphi(0) = 2\pi$, so $M$ has winding number $1$; the model
  visits the four arcs with exactly the crossed signs, and the two designated
  corners with the designated signs.

  The comparison is a straight-line homotopy.  On each arc, $\gamma$ and $M$
  satisfy the \emph{same} strict half-plane inequality, and a half-plane is
  convex and misses the origin, so $(1-s)\gamma(t)+sM(t)$ is nonzero for every
  $s$.  At the two corner parameters the corner hypotheses supply the missing
  half-plane.  Hence the homotopy is zero-free, and since winding is a
  homotopy invariant of zero-free loops, $\gamma$ and $M$ have the same
  winding number.

blocks.label: thm:fad_exists_zero
blocks.title: nonzero winding forces an interior zero
blocks.body:
Let $u_1<u_2$, $v_1<v_2$ and let $F$ be continuous on the closed rectangle.
  If the boundary loop of $F$ is nowhere zero and has nonzero winding number,
  then $F$ has a zero in the \emph{open} rectangle.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.exists_zero_of_fourArcRectangleBoundary_winding
lean.code:
theorem exists_zero_of_fourArcRectangleBoundary_winding
    {u₁ u₂ v₁ v₂ : ℝ} (hu : u₁ < u₂) (hv : v₁ < v₂)
    {F : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ}
    (hF : ContinuousOn F (Set.Icc u₁ u₂ ×ˢ Set.Icc v₁ v₂))
    (gamma : C(unitInterval, ℂ)) (hgamma : ∀ t, gamma t ≠ 0)
    (hgammaEq : ∀ t, gamma t =
      F (fourArcRectangleBoundary u₁ u₂ v₁ v₂ t))
    (hwind : Gluck.windingNumberC gamma hgamma ≠ 0) :
    ∃ z ∈ Set.Ioo u₁ u₂ ×ˢ Set.Ioo v₁ v₂, F z = 0 := by
  by_contra hnot
  push Not at hnot
  exact hwind (windingNumberC_eq_zero_of_no_interior_zero_aux
    hu hv hF gamma hgamma hgammaEq hnot)

blocks.tex:
Suppose $F$ has no zero in the open rectangle.  Contract the boundary loop
  radially towards the centre $c = \bigl(\tfrac{u_1+u_2}2,\tfrac{v_1+v_2}2\bigr)$:
  \[
    H(s,t) = (1-s)\,c + s\cdot\mathrm{boundary}(t) .
  \]
  Because the rectangle is a product of intervals, $H(s,t)$ lies in the
  \emph{open} rectangle for every $s<1$ and on the boundary at $s=1$.  Hence
  $F\circ H$ is zero-free: for $s<1$ by the assumption, at $s=1$ by the
  hypothesis on the boundary loop.  It is a homotopy of loops from the
  constant loop at $F(c)$ to the boundary loop, so the two have equal winding
  numbers; the constant one is $0$, contradicting the hypothesis.

The retained local opening lemmas turn zero dormant lengths into positive lengths while maintaining the closure and turning equations. Surjectivity at a regular four-edge anchor supplies their hypotheses.

The single-wall primitive is
$\mathrm{regularWallZero\_entersInterior}$, stated as
\cref{thm:regularWallZero_entersInterior} in
\cref{chap:discrete_collared_continuation}: at a regular zero of $f$, a kernel
direction $v$ with $w'v>0$ integrates to an exact level-set curve
$\gamma$ with $\gamma(0)=a$, $\gamma'(0)=v$, on which the wall slack $w$ is
strictly positive for all small $t>0$.  This section builds on it.

blocks.label: thm:wc_enters_all
blocks.title: one curve enters all active walls at once
blocks.body:
With finitely many walls and a single $v\in\ker f'$ which is strictly inward
  for every one of them, one curve on the exact fibre enters all of them
  simultaneously.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.regularWallZero_entersAllInteriors
lean.code:
theorem regularWallZero_entersAllInteriors
    {ι E F : Type*} [Finite ι]
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [FiniteDimensional ℝ F]
    {f : E → F} {f' : E →L[ℝ] F} {a v : E}
    {w : ι → E → ℝ} {w' : ι → E →L[ℝ] ℝ}
    (hf : HasStrictFDerivAt f f' a)
    (hsurj : f'.range = ⊤)
    (hv : v ∈ f'.ker)
    (hw : ∀ i, HasFDerivAt (w i) (w' i) a)
    (hpos : ∀ i, 0 < w' i v) :
    ∃ (γ : ℝ → E) (ε : ℝ),
      0 < ε ∧
      γ 0 = a ∧
      HasDerivAt γ v 0 ∧
      Tendsto γ (𝓝 0) (𝓝 a) ∧
      ∀ t, 0 < t → t < ε →
        f (γ t) = f a ∧ ∀ i, w i a < w i (γ t) := by
  let q : f'.ker := ⟨v, hv⟩
  let γ : ℝ → E := fun t =>
    hf.implicitFunction f f' hsurj (f a) (t • q)
  have hγ0 : γ 0 = a := by
    simp [γ, hf.implicitFunction_apply_image hsurj]
  have hq_deriv : HasStrictDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => t • q) q 0 := by
    simpa using ((hasStrictDerivAt_id (𝕜 := ℝ) (0 : ℝ)).smul_const q)
  have hq_tendsto : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => t • q) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 0) := by
    simpa only [ContinuousAt, zero_smul] using hq_deriv.hasDerivAt.continuousAt
  have hγ_tendsto : Tendsto γ (𝓝 0) (𝓝 a) := by
    simpa [γ] using
      (hf.tendsto_implicitFunction hsurj
        (g₁ := fun _ : ℝ => f a) (g₂ := fun t : ℝ => t • q)
        tendsto_const_nhds hq_tendsto)
  have hγ_deriv : HasDerivAt γ v 0 := by
    simpa [γ, q, Function.comp_def] using
      ((hf.to_implicitFunction hsurj).comp_hasStrictDerivAt_of_eq 0 hq_deriv (by simp)).hasDerivAt
  have hlevel : ∀ᶠ t : ℝ in 𝓝 0, f (γ t) = f a := by
    have hp : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => (f a, t • q)) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 (f a, 0)) :=
      tendsto_const_nhds.prodMk_nhds hq_tendsto
    simpa [γ] using hp.eventually (hf.map_implicitFunction_eq hsurj)
  have hwall : ∀ i, HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => w i (γ t)) (w' i v) 0 := by
    intro i
    simpa [Function.comp_def] using
      (hw i).comp_hasDerivAt_of_eq 0 hγ_deriv hγ0.symm
  have hwall_good : ∀ i, ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), w i a < w i (γ t) := by
    intro i
    have hslope :
        Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => t⁻¹ * (w i (γ t) - w i (γ 0)))
          (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (w' i v)) := by
      simpa [smul_eq_mul] using (hwall i).tendsto_slope_zero_right
    filter_upwards [hslope.eventually_const_lt (hpos i), self_mem_nhdsWithin]
      with t hs ht
    have hinv : 0 < t⁻¹ := inv_pos.mpr ht
    have hdiff : 0 < w i (γ t) - w i (γ 0) :=
      pos_of_mul_pos_right hs hinv.le
    rw [hγ0] at hdiff
    exact sub_pos.mp hdiff
  have hgood :
      ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), f (γ t) = f a ∧ ∀ i, w i a < w i (γ t) := by
    filter_upwards [hlevel.filter_mono nhdsWithin_le_nhds,
      Filter.eventually_all.2 hwall_good] with t hft hwt
  -- … (truncated)
